name: Sörmlandsleden
description: The official Sörmlandsleden stage catalog with 94 stages and branch connectors. Stages 1-10 are deeply enriched; the remaining official stages are represented from Sörmlandsleden's catalog and marked for the same research workflow across books, hiker blogs, forums, reviews, local rules, and service maps.
gettingThere: Start and end access varies by selected stage. The Stockholm-area stages include Björkhagen metro, Handen commuter rail, Östertälje commuter rail, and Järna commuter rail. Later stages span Södermanland and require checking regional buses, train stations, parking, and local road access for the selected section.
campingRules: Rules change by reserve. Nackareservatet/Erstavik and Rudan are restrictive enough that overnight plans should use signed/designated places only. Tyresta national park/reserve allows camping only at designated sites such as Tyresta by and selected shelter/rest areas under posted limits. Paradiset/Orlången-area short tenting is more permissive but still excludes sensitive ground, meadows, and signed no-camping areas. Fires should be treated as official-fireplace-only, and current fire bans always override stored data.
utilities: The strongest service nodes are Björkhagen, Alby friluftsgård, Tyresta by, Rudans gård/Handen, Paradiset, Lida friluftsgård, Östertälje, Tveta friluftsgård, and Järna.
Shelter-rich areas include Årsjön, Trehörningen/Ugglekojan, Paradiset, Kvarnsjön, Lida/Getaren, and Herrvreten.
Several facilities are seasonal or after-hours dependent; the app stores known positions but planning should still check the linked source before departure.
waterSources: Most dependable refills are at staffed/outdoor centers: Alby, Tyresta by, Rudan, Paradiset, Lida, Tveta, and urban endpoints.
Natural sources and pumps such as Sandakällan, Högdalen, Riddartorp, Kvarnsjön, and Herrvreten should be treated or filtered and may be dry or poor quality.
Carry enough water between confirmed taps, especially on stages 6, 8, and 10.
notes: The full official catalog is included so filters and route planning do not hide later Sörmlandsleden stages.

Branches such as 5:1, 12:1, and similar connector stages are official sections but not always a simple linear continuation. The route builder groups them separately so branch plans do not accidentally include unrelated mainline sections.
All official stages and branch connectors have route-group coverage, facility enrichment, water status, access context, and reserve/current-condition notes where research found them.
Recent reports mention temporary reroutes, storm-felled trees, or weak markings around Kolardammarna, Rudan/Handen, Tysslinge/Lövstalund, Södertälje canal works, and some forest sections.
Facility coordinates with approximate wording should be verified against signage before using them as sole safety-critical resources.

sections.name: Stage 1: Björkhagen to Skogshyddan
sections.description: Urban-accessible start through Nackareservatet and Erstavik, with several good exit options but limited reliable drinking water.
utilities: Björkhagen has metro access and nearby city services.
Söderbysjön has bathing, grills, and seasonal toilets; nearby golf/club services vary by season.
Skogshyddan/Lovisedal has local access roads and limited parking rather than a staffed trail service point.
waterSources: Sandakällan is a natural source between Tenntorpsvägen and Sandasjön. Nacka publishes test values, but drinking is still at your own risk.
Carry city water from Björkhagen when starting this stage.
notes: Nackareservatet and Strålsjön-Erstavik rules make this a poor overnight candidate.
Strålsjön-Erstavik forbids tenting; dogs must be leashed and fires are only allowed in a brought grill or designated place.
Fires are only allowed at arranged grill places near Markuskyrkan/outdoor gym and Söderbysjön; otherwise fire is prohibited in the reserve.
Dogs are not allowed on Söderbysjöns badplats June 1-August 31.
2024 comments mention missed or hidden turns around the golf restaurant and golf-course/gravel-road area; keep the GPX visible.

sections.name: Stage 2: Skogshyddan to Alby friluftsgård
sections.description: Short connector stage toward Tyresö, useful as part of a Björkhagen-Alby day or an easy start toward Tyresta.
utilities: Most reliable services are at Alby friluftsgård at the end of the stage.
waterSources: Carry water in from before Skogshyddan/Sandakällan or use Alby as a practical refill if facilities are open.
notes: Treat this as a low-facility connector: no strong mid-stage water/toilet/shelter evidence was found.
Kolardammarna has an official autumn/winter 2025 sediment-removal reroute via the promenade path to the right of the ponds before reconnecting to the normal route.

Reports through November 16, 2025 still mention weak markings around Kolardammarna and a horse/stable area; a December 27, 2025 response says markings were improved during autumn and will be reviewed again in spring.

Årsjön has a wind shelter, fireplace, dry toilet, and nearby swimming rocks.
Krusboda grocery near the start and Café Rödkullan at Uddby gård about 0.5 km off-route can be useful if open.

Tyresta by has drinking water at the visitor/farm area.
notes: Steep/slippery sections and boardwalks can be slick year-round; offline map recommended.
Naturkartan warns that bark-beetle-damaged spruces can fall; avoid forest sections during strong wind.
Community reports mention occasional confusing marking and fallen trees between Nyfors and Tyresta; offline map recommended.

sections.name: Stage 5:1: Kvarnängens IP Nynäshamn to Vansta, Ösmo
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 5:1, Kvarnängens IP Nynäshamn to Vansta, Ösmo.
utilities: Official area: Nynäshamns Kommun.

Parking is available at Kvarnängens sporthallar/Kvarnängens IP. The official trail board is by Kvarnängen bus stop on Nynäsvägen, about 100 m from the parking; no all-hours public toilet or tap was verified at the sports halls.

Nynäsgård commuter rail is the practical train approach; follow orange markings past Nynäshamns gymnasium for about 1.9 km to the trail board. No station toilet or tap was verified, and Trafikverket's Nynäsgård rebuild may make station access longer during works.

At the north end, Vansta bus stop is about 0.3-0.4 km from the stage end, while Ösmo station and Ösmo centrum services are about 1.2 km away. ICA Ösmo and Ösmo simhall are opening-hour-dependent services, not trail facilities.

Ösmo simhall can be useful for paid, opening-hour-dependent toilets/showers when open; Willys Sandtorp and ICA Maxi Nynäshamn are larger Nynäshamn-side services near the Nynäsgård approach but are not core trail facilities.

Bus 783 broadly parallels parts of the stage via Kvarnängen, Älgviken, Björsta, Vansta, and Ösmo, giving several practical bailout/access points. Check live SL before starting because bus and train timetables change seasonally.
waterSources: Fjättersjön/Fjättern is described by Sörmlandsleden as a spring lake with good water and rest spots, but no independent potable-water test was found; treat/filter it and carry backup.

Sörmlandsleden says drinking water, toilets, and waste disposal are available through public arrangements in the built-up areas at both endpoints, but exact all-hours public toilet/tap/waste points were not verified. Treat endpoint services as shop, sports-facility, or simhall dependent.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
Access connector from Nynäshamn toward Ösmo/Vansta. Official, Naturkartan, AllTrails, STF, and OSM agree on 9.5 km; disregard the 8.45 km distance found on Äventyrligare for this stage.

The mapped main line is the through-route from Kvarnängen trail board/bus stop to Vansta and measures about 9.31 km. The official 9.5 km catalog distance includes nearby access context, especially the short Kvarnängens IP/parking spur, which should be modeled as a selectable access connector rather than forced into the main line.

The route passes Nynäs gods, Fjättersjön/Fjättern, Valsjö, Björsta, runic remains, Älby grave field, and Vansta gård. The Valsjö/Tuppstensgrottan side trip is worthwhile but has been reported as easy to miss.

Cultural remains along and near the route, including runic remains, grave fields, Valsjö-area historic structures, and fornborg traces around Fjättern, should be treated as protected look-but-do-not-disturb sites. Do not move, dig, cover, alter, damage, or remove anything; report finds instead of collecting them.

No Naturvårdsregistret nature reserve, national park, animal/plant protection area, or Natura 2000 overlap was found for the route corridor, but the stage intersects Berga vattenskyddsområde. Keep toilet needs far from water, do not wash gear or dishes in lakes/streams, avoid fuel or chemical spills, and pack out waste.

Dogs must be leashed through the grazing pasture before Valsjö during May-October. National dog supervision rules are stricter from 1 March to 20 August, dogs should be leashed near grazing animals, and dogs must also be leashed on Nynäshamn/Ösmo public-place areas covered by municipal rules.

No designated campsite is confirmed on 5:1. Camping is prohibited on Nynäshamn public-place areas shown in municipal appendices. Elsewhere, only short allemansrätten tenting may be possible on durable natural ground, away from homes, not on farmland or grazing pasture.

Fires should be limited to prepared Fjättern/Fjättersjön grill places. Nynäshamn lists Öster om Fjättern and Norr om Fjättern/Fjätterns NO strand as bring-your-own-wood sites with no toilet and no shelter. Check current fire-ban status before using any fireplace; fixed public grill places may be allowed under ordinary bans but solid-fuel grilling is forbidden even at fixed grill places under stricter bans.

Fjättern is managed as FK Alcedo club water: fishing requires a valid fishing card, rules can change, and fishing is hand-gear only under the published rules. Boats, canoes, and other floating craft are not allowed. Carry out waste from lake visits.

Recent hiker reports describe the route as generally usable, but markings can be faded in places; keep the map handy. Expect mud or wet ground in spring and autumn, snow/ice in winter and early spring, and possible insects or overgrown vegetation in early summer.

Community reports describe a varied but not especially wild route with road/gravel sections, cultural remains, some traffic/speedway/rail noise, and lower/wetter areas that can be buggy in early summer.
The official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-26 research pass; verify current notices before hiking.

sections.name: Stage 5:2: Vansta, Ösmo to Hemfosa
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 5:2, Vansta, Ösmo to Hemfosa.
utilities: Official area: Haninge Kommun, Nynäshamns Kommun.
Ösmo has commuter rail, buses, grocery/cafe services, and station parking near the start; the official access from Ösmo station is about 15 minutes on foot to Vansta via Nybblevägen/Hugins väg.
Segersäng station is now a mid-stage access/bailout because the April 2026 official reroute passes directly through the station. No shop, tap, or toilet was verified at Segersäng.
Hemfosa has commuter rail access near the rerouted line and small parking at the north transition to stage 5:3. No shop, tap, or toilet was verified at Hemfosa.
Körunda hotel/restaurant and golf services sit off-route near Muskan and can be useful if open, but they are customer/opening-hour-dependent services rather than trail facilities.

Public map data is especially fragile here: Sörmlandsleden currently lists 17.5 km after the April 2026 reroute, Naturkartan's updated line measures about 15.08 km and displays 15.0 km, OSM predates the reroute, and third-party tracks vary widely.
There are no reliable public toilets or potable refill taps between Ösmo services and Hemfosa. Segersäng is excellent for rail bailout, but should not be treated as a resupply point.
waterSources: No verified public drinking-water tap was found on the trail itself. Carry enough water or treat/filter natural water.
Muskan has lake/bathing water only; it is not a verified potable source. Treat/filter/boil any lake water and avoid polluting the shoreline.

Do not generalize Muskan as safe bathing water everywhere: Nynäshamn has warned about contaminated sediment at the planned Sköndalsvägen/majbrasan bay, which is separate from the north Muskan shelter/bathing area.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden now lists 5:2 as 17.5 km and says the stage has a new route from April 2026 between Segersäng and Hemfosa. Naturkartan's API geometry was updated 2026-04-27 and appears continuous/current at about 15.08 km, but its displayed 15.0 km length conflicts with the official 17.5 km; show the official distance and keep the geometry caveat visible.

The old Segersäng-Hemfosa alignment was reported nearly impassable from fallen trees, poor visibility, overgrowth, and high water through 2025. The April 2026 reroute is signed and described as easier, mostly along a gated forest road closed to cars, but an April 2026 hiker comment calls it a long hard-gravel transport stretch.

Current northbound reroute description: pass through Segersäng station, follow Segersängsvägen about 150 m, turn left onto a forest road, pass a road barrier after another about 150 m, then continue roughly 7 km toward Hemfosa. The best visible current geometry is Naturkartan's updated 2026-04-27 line; use field markings over stale OSM or old downloaded GPX.
Muskan is the key rest/overnight area: official text lists a shelter at the north end of the lake with bathing nearby.

Do not rely on Naturkartan's 15.0 km metadata, AllTrails' noisy 9.3 mile/18.2 km variants, OSM relation 562617, Äventyrligare, TopoGPS-style copies, older guidebooks, or the 2025 long-distance passport for current planning unless they clearly show a post-April-2026 update.

OSM relation 562617 is specifically stale for route drawing north of Segersäng: it was last edited before the reroute, retains stale distance/start behavior, includes an extra south-of-Vansta/Ösmo approach, and follows the old north-of-Segersäng line. Keep it as background evidence only until updated.

The official public page still loads a bundled full-network GPX named Leden-2024-12-04.gpx. Do not use that filename or old downloads as proof of current Stage 5:2 geometry after the April 2026 reroute.
A 2023 official comment says the path was adjusted near the fifth golf hole on the west side of Muskan; follow current orange markings around the golf-course edge.

Sörmlandsleden runs east of Slätmossen-Borgberget nature reserve. Avoid detours into the reserve while Länsstyrelsen advises against entry because dead spruces can fall suddenly and the reserve path is closed/unmaintained.

No official campsite or toilet was confirmed on 5:2. Nynäshamn's Muskan grill-place listing explicitly says no toilet at the shelter area. Muskan shelter is first-come, cannot be booked, has no guaranteed firewood or bin service, and shelter-community sources describe it as small, with limited sleeping space and poor tenting. Any camping outside shelters must follow allemansrätten plus local reserve or landowner restrictions.

As of the 2026-04-27 research pass, Länsstyrelsen Stockholm showed no county-wide fire ban, but that is time-sensitive. Use prepared fireplaces only, bring your own fuel if needed, and check current county/municipal fire-ban status before lighting anything.

From 1 March to 20 August dogs must be under extra strict control, and leash use is the safer assumption near grazing animals, golf-course edges, reserve boundaries, settlements, station areas, and Muskan bird-sensitive areas such as Mariaholmen in nesting season.
The official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-28 research pass, but its comments document the recent reroute history; verify current notices before hiking.
Older blogs mention Transjön shelter on Segersäng-Hemfosa, but current official staging places Transjön on Stage 5:3 after Hemfosa. Keep Transjön as a continuation option, not a Stage 5:2 facility.

sections.name: Stage 5:3: Hemfosa to Etapp 6 (1 km från Paradiset)
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 5:3, Hemfosa to Etapp 6 (1 km från Paradiset).
utilities: Official area: Haninge Kommun, Huddinge kommun, Nynäshamns Kommun, Stockholm.
Hemfosa station is the practical rail access, but the official stage start is about 1 km west by road at Hemfosavägen.
Mid-route access is possible near Sofielund/Sorundavägen by bus when service is running; check SL because service can be sparse.

The official stage ends at the Etapp 6 junction about 1 km south of Paradiset. Paradiset has large parking, toilet, water pump, shelter/rest area, and bus access via Bruket or Ådran, but those facilities are technically on the Etapp 6 continuation.

Hjälmsätersvägen and Sofielund can be useful road/bus access points around Österby/Sorundavägen, while Västra skolan and Slåboda are separate Tornberget reserve access points rather than direct Stage 5:3 finishes.
No grocery, cafe, restaurant, or resupply was verified on core Stage 5:3. Tungelsta services are well off-route and should be treated as a separate transport/detour plan, not stage infrastructure.

Check SL the same day for Hemfosa commuter-rail service and bus 848/709 access. Line 848 serves Sofielund/Sorundavägen seasonally/sparsely, and line 709 serves Bruket/Ådran for Paradiset exits. Stored timetable PDFs valid into 2026 still need live verification.
waterSources: No reliable potable water was verified on core 5:3. Carry water and treat/filter any natural lake water.

Paradiset water pump is the strongest verified refill, but it sits about 0.6-1.0 km beyond the official 5:3 endpoint on the Etapp 6 continuation and should still be treated as self-responsibility water rather than a tested municipal guarantee.
Transjön, Vädersjön, Vedasjön, Tornbergssjön, and other lakes/streams are natural water only. Third-party shelter data describes Transjön water as unknown quality; filter/boil and carry backup.
Older comments mention a source/pump around 5.5 km with bad taste/smell and no bacterial testing; do not mark it as dependable drinking water without fresh verification.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden lists 5:3 as Hemfosa to Etapp 6, 1 km from Paradiset, 15 km, with the page modified 2026-01-26. OSM/Naturkartan/Äventyrligare/AllTrails and older community sources often label the practical route as Hemfosa-Paradiset or Hemfosa-Tornberget and may include the Hemfosa station approach, Paradiset continuation, or older naming.

For route drawing, prefer the official full-line GPX/OSM/Naturkartan geometry that ends at the 5:3/Etapp 6/Tornbergsslingan junction around 59.148530, 18.018296. The official public GPX segment measures about 14.1 km and OSM about 14.4 km, while the official catalog distance is 15 km; show 15 km as canonical and treat map length as approximate.

OSM relation 2343975 is geometrically useful but its `to=Paradiset` tag is misleading relative to the current official endpoint. OSM Etapp 6 relation 2343842 carries the roughly 0.85-1.0 km continuation from the 5:3 junction to Paradiset; keep that as a connector rather than merging it into Stage 5:3.

Hemfosa station access is a separate roughly 1.0-1.1 km connector and should not be snapped into the canonical Stage 5:3 distance. The Paradiset continuation via Etapp 6 is also a separate connector; AllTrails/TopoGPS/Wikiloc-style Hemfosa-Paradiset tracks are useful extended-trip variants, not the stage boundary.

Österby nature reserve has an active bark-beetle/dead-spruce warning: trees can fall suddenly even without obvious warning, especially in wind, and Länsstyrelsen says the Sörmlandsleden path in the reserve is no longer maintained by them. Sörmlandsleden's 2024-12-01 fault report and 2025 comments describe fallen trees, orange-tape detours, crawling/climbing obstacles, and passable but awkward conditions. Avoid this reserve section in windy weather and do not climb unstable windthrows.

Expect varied forest, lakes, hällmark, wetter low areas, open fields near Hjälmsättra, some road walking, and the Tornberget tower. Vädersjön and other low/wet areas can be slow after rain or snowmelt; older reports mention flooded trail, slippery duckboards, mud, bugs, dense growth, roots, stones, and windfall obstacles. Treat those as condition signals rather than exact current defects.

Road 257/Väländan-area road walking can have heavy traffic and imperfect/missing signage in comments. Trafikverket work on 257/Tungelstavägen runs into summer 2027; keep the map handy and use care around road margins and crossings.

Fires in the reserve landscape should stay at prepared fireplaces and never on bare rock, cliffs, or slabs. Österby, Tornberget, and Paradiset rules prohibit damaging living or dead trees, so do not collect deadwood for fuel. Check current fire-ban status; no firewood is guaranteed at shelters.

Tornberget and Paradiset reserve rules require dogs and other pets not to run loose. From 1 March to 20 August, Swedish national dog rules require extra strict control in nature; using a lead is the safer default on this stage.

Österby, Tornberget, and Paradiset include Natura 2000 or sensitive old-forest/wetland values. Stay on marked paths where practical, keep noise and dog disturbance low, and avoid trampling wetland or shore vegetation.

Paradiset reserve allows short tenting under local rules if vegetation is not damaged and you avoid agricultural land/hay meadows, but verify signs on site. Huddinge guidance describes one, maximum two, nights; Transjön shelter is first-come, small, and not bookable.

Paradiset parking and firewood are convenience context, not guarantees. Local reports describe popular lots and firewood sometimes being gone; transit-first planning and carrying a stove are more reliable.

sections.name: Stage 6:1: Huddinge stn to Hökärr (etapp 6)
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 6:1, Huddinge stn to Hökärr (etapp 6).
utilities: Official area: Botkyrka kommun, Huddinge kommun, Stockholm.
Huddinge station and centrum provide commuter rail, bus terminal, shops, restaurants, toilets, and paid commuter/centrum parking at the start.

Several bus-access/bailout options exist before the forest deepens, including Sörskogen, Visättra sportcenter, Gladö Kvarn/Kvarnsjön, and Lidavägen/Hökärrsvägen area stops; check current SL departures.

The Hökärr endpoint is a junction with Etapp 6 at about 59.164973, 17.967248, not a convenient station finish. Plan a pickup, walk out 2.5-3 km to a bus, or continue on Etapp 6 toward Lida or Paradiset.

Visättra sportcenter has opening-hour-dependent toilets and hockey-season cafe context, and OSM maps a nearby water tap, but none of that should be treated as dependable trail infrastructure without live/local verification.
Nyboviksbadet and Affärsviken at Kvarnsjön offer useful off-route bathing/toilet/parking context in season, but they are detours or side-access points and bathing water is not a potable refill.

Flemingsberg station/centrum and Visättra shops can work as urban bailout or resupply before the wilder southern half. After Visättra/Flemingsberg, no reliable shop or public toilet was verified through Gladö kvarn, Nytorp, Kärrsjön, or Hökärr.

Hökärrsvägen, Gladö Kvarn, and Kvarnsjön stops appear in side-access material around the Gladö/Kvarnsjön area, commonly with SL 744 references, but source naming varies. Verify the exact stop and line in the SL app the same day.
waterSources: Scoutstugan Nytorp pump is the official water point after about 10 km, but scout-cottage information says the hand-pump water is for washing dishes/hands, quality is not guaranteed, it can be brownish, and users should bring drinking water. Treat/filter/boil and carry backup even though OSM maps it as a manual drinking-water pump.
An OSM-mapped water tap near Visättra sportcenter may exist, but it is not an official Stage 6:1 water source and should be verified on site before relying on it.
The old Trefaldighetskällan above Mariedalsvägen is explicitly described by Sörmlandsleden as dry and should not be mapped as water.

Kvarnsjön and Kärrsjön are natural lake water only; treat/filter/boil if used and carry enough from Huddinge. Kärrsjön is muddy/not good for bathing according to Stage 6 context and should not be presented as a swimming or drinking-water source.
Orlången/Flemingsbergsviken has documented poor water-quality context in Huddinge material and should never be presented as a drinking-water source.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Urban-to-forest access connector from Huddinge station to Hökärr/stage 6, officially 13 km. Official Sörmlandsleden page metadata was checked as modified 2025-10-14 and showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-28 pass. OSM and third-party lengths vary between roughly 12.7 and 14 km, while some blogs include extra continuation/access distance; treat line length as approximate and follow current orange markings.

For route drawing, use the cleaned continuous OSM/Naturkartan chain from Huddinge station/start to the Hökärr/Etapp 6 shared node at about 59.164973, 17.967248. OSM relation 2343843 has a stale 14 km tag: raw member sum is about 13.75 km because it includes noisy/dangling members, while the connected routable line with a tiny Visättra snap gap measures about 13.04 km and matches the official/Naturkartan 13 km.

Stage 6:1 is an access connector, not a normal continuation in the main chain. In the route builder, offer it when the user selects or approaches Hökärr/Etapp 6, and keep onward Stage 6 choices toward Lida and Paradiset separate.

Official description is easy walking on mixed roads and lightly hilly terrain, then rockier forest near Nytorp, Kvarnsjöberget, Kärrsjön, and Valtertummaberget. Recent 2025 user reports describe the stage as well marked and maintained, but winter and freeze-thaw conditions can be very icy; microspikes/broddar are sensible in winter/early spring.

The route crosses or touches several Huddinge reserves including Flemingsbergsskogen, Orlången, Gladö Kvarnsjön, and Gladöskogen. Dogs should be leashed in protected areas; national 1 March-20 August dog-control rules also apply. Orlången, Gladö Kvarnsjön, and Gladöskogen prohibit camping more than two consecutive nights in the same place, while Flemingsbergsskogen still requires low-impact allemansrätten practice where not otherwise signed.

Reserve rules commonly prohibit fires on bare rock/cliffs and damaging live or dead wood. Use only established fireplaces where allowed, check current fire bans and grass-fire risk, and do not assume public firewood. Scoutstugan/Nytorp fireplaces and toilets belong to booked scout-facility context unless signs say otherwise.
No official shelter or dependable on-route toilet is listed for 6:1. Huddinge centrum/start services and optional Etapp 6 continuation services are the practical utility nodes.

Recent official comment in 2025 says joining at Flemingsberg worked well and the trail was very well marked. Older trip reports describe icy/slippery winter conditions, mud/snow, old storm-fallen trees, and some ambiguity around Gladö Kvarn/construction/horse paths; treat as seasonal/local caution, not a current closure.

Gladö Kvarn/Kvarnsjön is a known navigation-attention area: older reports describe losing the trail near the mill/road transition, and OSM relation 2343843 has a dangling Kvarnvägen/Gladövägen member. Use current orange markings over raw relation fragments.

Fishing in Huddinge lakes generally requires the correct fishing card, with exceptions not relevant here. Keep this warning around Orlången, Kvarnsjön, and Kärrsjön, and note that eating fish from Orlången should be approached cautiously because Huddinge has measured pollutants and advises caution where fresh measurements are missing.

Kvarnsjön Gladö fishing is not generally open to hikers; sources describe it as restricted to the local fishing-association members, and motor-driven boats are prohibited. Keep this as rule context around the lake rather than a recreation recommendation.

Kärrsjön firepit, tent/rest context, and former Kvarnsjön shelter belong to adjacent Stage 6 planning around the Hökärr junction. Show them as continuation context, not as core Stage 6:1 shelter infrastructure. The former Kvarnsjön spring on Stage 6 has contradictory dry/wet reports from 2024-2026 and should remain seasonal/unreliable.

sections.name: Stage 11: Järna to Vattgruvan
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 11, Järna to Vattgruvan.
utilities: Official area: Järna, Södertäljes kommun.
Järna station has commuter rail, buses, and parking about 600 m from the Rönnvägen/Tavestaskolan stage start. Buses 784/785 can also shorten the start approach when they fit the schedule.

Järna has the safest resupply before starting, including ICA, Coop, Pressbyrån, cafes, restaurants, pharmacy/fuel context around the station and Storgatan, but do not assume an all-hours public toilet; a hiker report says even station/Preem/Coop/bakery toilets were difficult early in the morning and ICA helped when asked.

Järna station commuter parking has been reported as 24 h only, and Tavestaskolan/Järna IP parking is conditional with overnight restrictions reported in 2025, including a 00-06 ban report. Check current signs before leaving a car.

Vattgruvsmossen/Vattgruvan has road access and parking at the stage end; the stage steward notes up to 72 h parking, while Länsstyrelsen says the visitor parking/access road has been improved but still has rough sections in places.

The Vattgruvan end is not a rail station and has no equally clean public-transport exit. For a transit-friendly finish, continue via stage 12 and the 12:1 connector toward Mölnbo, or arrange pickup/taxi.

Naturkartan/OSM/Vindskyddskartan support a toilet at Vattgruvsmossen parking and a 2026-04-26 trail comment also reports a toilet at the end, but Länsstyrelsen's visitor-service list is less explicit. Treat it as likely, not guaranteed, until field-checked.
Almviks Gård side services and an OSM-mapped water point north/east of Vattgruvan are off-route and opening/field-verification dependent; do not present them as Stage 11 core utilities.
waterSources: Official spring about 5 km west of Järna; natural and untested, so treat/filter.
Recent official-page comments conflict: the spring was reported dry on 2024-09-07, flowing on 2024-10-19, and fresh on 2025-05-01. Carry backup, especially in dry periods.
Mellanbygget is a good tent/rest spot but explicitly has no water. Do not confuse Vattgruvan/Stora Kobäcken mining or lake water with potable water.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Officially 9 km and medium difficulty; the official page was checked as modified 2025-11-18 and showed no current fault reports. Naturkartan and OSM also list 9 km, Äventyrligare gives 8.92 km, and AllTrails gives about 9.2 km with roughly 320 m ascent and a 2.5-3 hour typical pace. The walking is often experienced as easy in dry conditions, but rocky/hilly forest and mine-hole hazards justify the medium label.

For route drawing, use the official Järna-to-Vattgruvan identity, but beware source quirks: OSM relation 2441745 has correct from/to tags yet reversed member order, Naturkartan snaps the Järna start to the Stage 10/11 join about 42 m from the official coordinate, and Topo GPS route 203163 continues beyond Vattgruvan into stages 12 and 12:1. The extracted official full-GPX segment measures about 8.51 km while OSM raw members measure about 9.01 km; keep official 9 km as the planning distance.

Do not draw Järna station access as Stage 11; the station/parking is about 600 m from the Rönnvägen/Tavestaskolan stage start. Likewise, do not include Stora Kobäcken in Stage 11; it is a Stage 12 continuation about 200-300 m past Vattgruvan.

Sjuenda Kronopark and the Järna/Vattgruvan mining landscape contain over 200 old mine holes across a roughly 5 km historic ore field, many unprotected. Stay on marked trail unless you are deliberately visiting signed mine features, and keep children/dogs close.

Mining around Järna/Vattgruvan dates from the 1600s into the late 1800s, with named features including Tunnelgruvan, Jungfrugruvan, Storgruvan, Mossgruvan, Kruthuset, and the deep Vattgruvan shafts. Treat all remains as protected look-but-do-not-disturb heritage.

Do not enter shafts, climb around openings, move stones, dig, carve, or disturb heritage features. Vattgruvan's deepest shaft is described as going more than 100 m diagonally downward, and mine-hole hazards are worse in snow, leaf cover, low light, or with children/dogs.

Current official and community comments in 2025-2026 describe the stage as well marked, beautiful, and passable, while Friluftsfrämjandet and older reviews noted Tunnelgruvan could be too wet or partly flooded to enter safely.
Vattgruvsmossen reserve rules include dogs leashed, fires only at designated places, no damage to vegetation/dead wood, and no camping more than two consecutive nights in the same place.
Vattgruvsmossen and nearby bog/boardwalk terrain can be wet and rooty; waterproof shoes are sensible, especially after rain or in spring/autumn.
No current official fault report was found for Stage 11 during the 2026-04-28 pass; the latest checked official comment from 2026-04-26 reported the route well marked and easy to follow.

Stora Kobäcken shelter/fireplace/toilet/natural-water context is about 200-300 m beyond the stage end on stage 12. It is important for overnight planning, but should be shown as an adjacent continuation facility; recent field reports mention recent renovation, good tent/hammock options, flat tent space, blueberries, stony ground near the shelter, and no guaranteed wood.
Mats Wenner's long-distance account calls stages 11 and 12 personal favorites, and multiple trip reports highlight the mine history as the stage's standout feature.
During hunting season, especially around the large moose hunt from 8 October, watch for active-hunting signs, many parked cars, or local notices and choose another area if hunting seems active.
Wolf presence has been noted in the wider Mölnbo/Sjundareviret context. This is not a specific danger alert, but it reinforces keeping dogs leashed and securing food if overnighting on continuations.

facilities.name: Järna station access
facilities.description: Commuter rail and bus access about 600 m from the Rönnvägen stage start; official access commonly routes Stockholm City via Södertälje hamn to Järna. Check current SL service.

facilities.name: Järna / Rönnvägen stage start
facilities.description: Official stage start near Rönnvägen/Tavestaskolan after the short walk from Järna station.

facilities.name: Rönnvägen/Tavestaskolan bus access
facilities.description: Start-area bus access for routes such as 784/785 when service is running, reducing the walk from Järna station.

facilities.name: Järna start-area parking
facilities.description: Start-nearby parking cluster. Treat as conditional: station parking is reported 24 h and Tavestaskolan/Järna IP is mainly weekend/school-holiday context with overnight restrictions, including 00-06 restrictions, reported in 2025.

facilities.name: Järna town resupply
facilities.description: Nearby grocery, cafe, pharmacy, and fuel options in Järna. Toilet access is not guaranteed; a 2024 hiker comment says ICA helped when asked after other morning options were difficult.

facilities.name: Coop Järna resupply
facilities.description: Additional start-area grocery option near Järna station. Opening-hour-dependent and not a guaranteed toilet.

facilities.name: Preem Järna service caveat
facilities.description: Fuel/convenience near the start, but not a public toilet guarantee; a 2024 hiker comment specifically failed to find morning toilet access here.

facilities.name: Järna toilet caveat
facilities.description: Planning warning, not a service point: do not rely on station or shop toilets outside opening/customer access. Use confirmed facilities before arrival if starting early.

facilities.name: Stage 11 geometry/source caveat
facilities.description: Official start and OSM/Naturkartan Stage 10/11 join differ by about 42 m; OSM relation 2441745 is direction-reversed despite correct from/to tags. Official full-GPX extraction can measure about 8.51 km while OSM raw members measure about 9.01 km. Draw by official identity and current shared-node topology, not raw relation order.

facilities.name: Early-stage firepit / Eldplatsen
facilities.description: Mapped early-stage firepit/rest context. Not an official water, shelter, or resupply point; use only if local signs and current fire rules allow.

facilities.name: Spring-side small tent/rest area
facilities.description: Small tent/rest option near the official spring, with room for a couple of tents according to official text. Verify ground and leave no trace.

facilities.name: Spring west of Järna
facilities.description: Official natural spring after about 5 km, about 100 m from the trail. Seasonal/reliability caveat: reported dry in Sep 2024, flowing in Oct 2024 and May 2025. Treat/filter and carry backup.

facilities.name: Sjuenda Kronopark mine-hole warning
facilities.description: Hazard zone: the forest/mining area has over 200 old mine holes, many unprotected, across a broad historic ore field. Stay on marked trail and use signed boards for history context.

facilities.name: Järna gruvor information board
facilities.description: Mining-history information board in the Järna gruvor/Tunnelgruvan cluster. Look-but-do-not-disturb heritage; mine holes can be dangerous and protected by heritage rules.

facilities.name: Tunnelgruvan
facilities.description: Signed mining feature/horizontal shaft area. Visits are at own risk; Friluftsfrämjandet found it too wet to enter fully in September 2024, and wet/slippery/unsafe conditions can occur. Do not enter unsafe openings.

facilities.name: Jungfrugruvan
facilities.description: Signed mine-history point in the old Järna mining area; stay out of unprotected holes.

facilities.name: Mossgruvan
facilities.description: Additional mapped mine-history point in the Järna gruvor cluster. Treat as protected heritage and hazardous terrain; avoid unmarked openings.

facilities.name: Storgruvan
facilities.description: Signed mine-history point near the route; stay on safe ground around shafts and spoil heaps.

facilities.name: Mellanbygget tent/rest option
facilities.description: Good tent/rest option near the farther torp ruin according to official route text, but no water. Coordinate is SGU/route-context derived and should be field-verified.

facilities.name: Vattgruvan / Stage 12 join
facilities.description: OSM Stage 11/12 shared node, about 31 m from the official Stage 12 start coordinate. Clip Stage 11 here; Stora Kobäcken is Stage 12 continuation.

facilities.name: Vattgruvan / Vattgruvsmossen parking
facilities.description: Stage-end access and reserve parking; official steward note says good parking up to 72 h where signed, OSM maps a small lot, and Naturkartan photo context suggests more spaces. Länsstyrelsen warns some access-road sections remain poor. Check signs and drive carefully.

facilities.name: Vattgruvan end toilet
facilities.description: Likely accessible toilet by the stage end/parking: mapped in OSM/Naturkartan/Vindskyddskartan and reported in a 2026-04-26 Sörmlandsleden comment. Still verify locally because not every official facility list is consistent.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen entrance picnic/info
facilities.description: Reserve entrance picnic/information area near the stage end.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen reserve rules
facilities.description: Reserve/Natura 2000 rule marker: dogs leashed, camping no more than two consecutive nights, fires only at designated places, no motor vehicles off roads, and no damaging or collecting living/dead wood, plants, invertebrates, mosses, lichens, wood fungi, rock, or soil.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen wet footing warning
facilities.description: Bog/reserve approach can be wet with roots, stones, and boardwalks. Waterproof shoes are recommended after rain or outside dry summer conditions.

facilities.name: Kruthuset / Vattgruvorna heritage
facilities.description: Old stone powder-house and mining-remains area near Vattgruvan. Länsstyrelsen notes eight deep shafts and Vattgruvan reaching just over 100 m down.

facilities.name: Almviks Gård side service
facilities.description: Off-route bakery/farm-service context northeast of Vattgruvan. Verify opening hours and access; do not treat as a guaranteed Stage 11 service.

facilities.name: Almviks Gård mapped water point
facilities.description: OSM-mapped off-route drinking-water point. Low confidence for hikers; verify locally before relying on it.

facilities.name: Hunting season awareness
facilities.description: Hiking is not forbidden during hunting, but during active hunting periods, especially from the large moose hunt starting 8 October, watch for signs, many parked cars, or local notices and choose another area if hunting appears active.

facilities.name: Sjundareviret wolf context
facilities.description: Soft wildlife context from local hiking reports in the wider Mölnbo/Sjundareviret area. Not a danger alert by itself, but keep dogs leashed and secure food if overnighting on continuations.

facilities.name: Stora Kobäcken shelter (stage 12 continuation)
facilities.description: Shelter about 200-300 m beyond the stage end on stage 12. Naturkartan/Vindskyddskartan describe shelter, grill/fireplace, benches, boardwalk to water, roughly 4 sleeping places, tent space, nearby parking/toilet context, and unknown-quality water. Recent reports mention recent renovation, good tent/hammock options, flat tent space, blueberries, and stony ground near the shelter. Useful for overnight planning, but not core stage 11.

facilities.name: Stora Kobäcken fireplace (stage 12 continuation)
facilities.description: Designated fireplace at Stora Kobäcken. Bring your own wood or charcoal; no supplied firewood should be assumed, Naturkartan explicitly says bring your own, and current fire bans override use.

facilities.name: Stora Kobäcken natural water (stage 12 continuation)
facilities.description: Surface water by the adjacent continuation shelter area; quality is unknown and not a drinking tap. Treat/filter/boil if used.

sections.name: Stage 12: Vattgruvan to Yngsviken
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 12, Vattgruvan to Yngsviken.
utilities: Official area: Södertäljes kommun.
Vattgruvan/Vattgruvsmossen and Yngsviken are access/parking points rather than service nodes. Exact stage access by public transport is awkward.

Vattgruvsmossen parking is verified but small; OSM maps about 3 spaces. Road access is via Billsta/road 57, and Länsstyrelsen notes the road/parking has been improved while some approach-road sections remain poor.
Vattgruvsmossen has an accessible toilet/changing-table point by the parking according to Naturkartan/OSM and recent trail comments, making it the strongest confirmed toilet on the core stage.
For public transport, practical approaches are adding stage 11 from Järna, using the stage 12:1 connector from Mölnbo, or arranging pickup/taxi near Yngsviken.

Stora Alsjön reserve parking gives a useful side access and local-loop option, but it is not the same as the Yngsviken endpoint. Naturkartan describes about 6 cars at Stora Alsjön parking; Yngsviken has official parking/access, but exact parking geometry and capacity are under-mapped.
No shops are on the stage. Mölnbo/24Food via stage 12:1 and Järna before stage 11 are the nearest rail-side resupply options.
Högfors and Molstaberg bus stops are only side-access context and not clean trailheads. Verify live service and walking routes before treating them as exits.
waterSources: No verified potable tap was found on core stage 12. Carry water and treat/filter natural sources.

Trönsjön is described by Sörmlandsleden as having good-quality water, rest, and bathing, and municipal water data reports high ecological status, but it is still natural lake water and Sörmlandsleden does not test or guarantee it. Treat/filter/boil and carry backup.

Stora Kobäcken, Lilla Horssjön, Stora Horssjön, Stora Alsjön, and nearby Yngern are natural surface water only; do not label them as drinking-water taps. Vindskyddskartan specifically treats Lilla Horssjön water quality as unknown.

OSM has isolated off-route drinking-water/water-point nodes near Sjundasjön/Almvik, but multiple research passes found no official or on-stage corroboration. Do not rely on them without field verification.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Officially 8.5 km but demanding: repeated rocky climbs/descents over hällmark, steep lake-shore sections at Stora Alsjön, and a steep descent toward Yngsviken make this slower than the distance suggests. AllTrails rates the route hard/challenging at about 8.9 km and 304 m gain; use that as effort context, not the canonical distance.

Distance sources disagree: official/Naturkartan list 8.5 km, Äventyrligare and AllTrails are around 8.3-8.9 km, OSM relation 2390742 measures about 8.36 km but is still tagged 9.5 km, and official full-GPX extraction can under-measure around 7.98 km from simplification/snap differences. Use the official distance and current markings.

For route drawing, use OSM/Naturkartan topology but override stale distance metadata: Stage 12 should run from the Vattgruvan Stage 11/12 shared node around 59.082122, 17.449356 to the Yngsviken Stage 12/13 shared node around 59.108280, 17.379178. Store the printed official start 59.082017,17.449867 separately, but snap topology to the shared OSM node.

At the Stage 12:1 junction around 59.081138, 17.426726, show a clear T-junction: east/northeast toward Vattgruvan/Järna, west toward Yngsviken, and south on connector 12:1 toward Mölnbo. Do not merge Mölnbo station access into Stage 12 or Stage 12:1's official distance; 12:1 is Mölnbo IP to Stage 12, with Mölnbo station as an extra access connector.
Near Vattgruvan, smaller mine holes are not fenced and larger shafts sit near the route. Stay on marked trail and keep children/dogs close.

Vattgruvsmossen rules include dogs leashed, no camping more than two consecutive nights, fires only at designated places, no disturbing wildlife, no off-road driving, and no damaging vegetation, dead wood, rock, or soil. The reserve is also Natura 2000 SE0110006.

Stora Alsjön reserve/Natura 2000 rules require fires only at designated fireplaces and prohibit damaging/removing living or dead wood, rock, soil, plants, mosses, lichens, and wood-living fungi. Motor vehicles are limited to roads. Flowers, berries, and edible mushrooms are allowed, but firewood boxes may be empty and wood collection is not allowed.

Stora Alsjön reserve water/fishing rights are not clearly open to hikers; reserve-plan material ties fishing to landowners and sources do not establish public fishing rights. Do not recommend fishing unless the user has explicit current permission. If continuing into Stora Envättern, fishing is explicitly prohibited.

A January 2024 user report praised the Stora Alsjön north shelter location but noted wet-floor/design issues; a 2024 overnight report also questioned weather protection at Stora Alsjön and wind exposure at Lilla Horssjön. Treat shelters as useful but not stormproof.
A 2024 comment reported a missing/downed sign about 1 km before Yngsviken; the official page showed no current fault report during the 2026-04-28 research pass.

Recent Vattgruvan loop comments add dated condition warnings: a 2025-09-14 user report described sunken/disintegrated boardwalks after wet weather and felled spruce with no cut-through, while a 2025-07-19 comment emphasized water scarcity for overnighting. Vardagstur's 2024 account also reported bark-beetle affected forest and detours around fallen trees north/east toward the Yngsviken/Djupsjön direction. Treat these as user-reported conditions, not official closures, and be cautious in wind.

Do not confuse Stage 12 with nearby branches/continuations and local loops: Vattgruvsmossen/Vattgruvan loops near the start, the 12:1 Mölnbo connector, Stora Alsjön blue/local trails, and Stage 13/Djupsjön facilities all need separate route-builder treatment. The official Vattgruvan round loop is a separate 9 km suggestion that only partly uses Sörmlandsleden, and OSM relation 20109615 should not be merged into Stage 12.

Horssjöarna naming is inconsistent in sources: map data and official coordinates place the shelter at Lilla Horssjön, while one steward note says Stora Horssjön. Keep the shelter at Lilla Horssjön and treat Stora Horssjön as fire/rest context unless field-verified.

facilities.name: Vattgruvan stage start
facilities.description: Official stage start at Vattgruvan/Vattgruvsmossen. Road access is signed from road 57/Billsta, but approach-road conditions can be rough.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen parking
facilities.description: Small parking by the reserve/stage start; OSM maps about 3 spaces while official text says good parking at Yngsviken/Vattgruvan. Approach road is improved but still rough in places, and current local signs should be checked.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen accessible toilet
facilities.description: Accessible toilet/changing-table point by the parking, confirmed by Naturkartan/OSM and recent trail comments. Treat as the strongest confirmed toilet on core Stage 12.

facilities.name: Vattgruvan mine-hole warning
facilities.description: Hazard/rule marker: old mine field with several smaller unfenced mine holes near the trail and larger fenced shafts off trail. Keep children/dogs close and be extra cautious in snow, dusk, or poor visibility.

facilities.name: Stage 12 geometry/source caveat
facilities.description: OSM relation 2390742 is topologically useful but still tagged 9.5 km; measured OSM geometry is about 8.36 km, while official/Naturkartan list 8.5 km and official full-GPX extraction can under-measure around 7.98 km. Clip Stage 12 to Vattgruvan-Yngsviken and keep Vattgruvan loops separate.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen reserve/Natura rules
facilities.description: Reserve/Natura 2000 SE0110006 context: dogs leashed, camping max two consecutive nights, fires only at designated sites, no off-road driving, no disturbing wildlife, and no damaging vegetation, dead wood, rock, soil, mosses, lichens, or wood fungi.

facilities.name: Vattgruvan local-loop caveat
facilities.description: The official Vattgruvan round loop is a separate 9 km suggestion that only partly follows Sörmlandsleden. OSM also has Vattgruvan rundslinga, Vattgruvsmossen, Blå leden, and Kolbottenrundan relations nearby; do not merge these into Stage 12.

facilities.name: Stora Kobäcken shelter
facilities.description: Shelter/rest area about 250-300 m beyond the start with benches, boardwalk to water, nearby tenting, and about 4 sleeping places in shelter-map data. First-come; pack out waste. Recent reports say tent pegging can be awkward on rocky ground.

facilities.name: Stora Kobäcken fireplace
facilities.description: Designated fireplace at Stora Kobäcken. Naturkartan/Länsstyrelsen context says bring your own firewood; current fire bans and local fire-risk guidance override use.

facilities.name: Stora Kobäcken natural water
facilities.description: Lake/tjärn water at the rest area; quality is not verified as potable. Treat/filter/boil.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen entrance fireplace/picnic
facilities.description: Additional mapped fireplace/picnic context near the Vattgruvsmossen entrance. Medium confidence; use only where signs and current fire-ban status allow.

facilities.name: Kristinagruvan / Järna gruvor
facilities.description: Mining-history point near the early part of the stage. Treat mine remains as hazardous protected heritage.

facilities.name: Etapp 12:1 junction to Mölnbo
facilities.description: Connector junction for the 4 km Mölnbo IP route; show Mölnbo station as a separate access spur beyond the official 12:1 start. This is the most practical rail approach to the middle of Stage 12. Official GPX nearest point is around 59.080787,17.426609, so allow small snap tolerance.

facilities.name: Trönsjön rest, swim, and natural water
facilities.description: Rest/swim area where Sörmlandsleden notes good-quality water. It is still natural lake water, not a potable tap; treat/filter.

facilities.name: Stora Horssjön fire/rest point
facilities.description: Mapped fire/rest context at Stora Horssjön. Do not treat this as a shelter; sources place the confirmed shelter at Lilla Horssjön despite one official steward note using Stora Horssjön wording.

facilities.name: Stora Alsjön viewpoint/rest
facilities.description: View/rest point near Stora Alsjön terrain. Fires and wood use are restricted by reserve rules.

facilities.name: Stora Alsjön reserve/Natura rules
facilities.description: Reserve/Natura 2000 SE0110161 context: fires only at designated places; do not damage or remove live/dead wood, vegetation, mosses, lichens, wood-living fungi, rock, or soil; motor vehicles only on roads; do not assume fishing rights are open.

facilities.name: Horssjöarna tent/rest area
facilities.description: Officially recommended tent/rest/bathing area between the Horssjö lakes, with tenting west of the trail. Use durable ground and avoid crowding.

facilities.name: Lilla Horssjön shelter
facilities.description: Official shelter about 150 m east of the trail between the Horssjö lakes; first-come and no guaranteed firewood. Vindskyddskartan notes bathing/rest context, unknown-quality water, difficult foot-only access over stones, and possible exposure to cold wind. Some source text says Stora Horssjön, but coordinates/map sources support Lilla Horssjön.

facilities.name: Lilla Horssjön fireplace
facilities.description: Fireplace by Lilla Horssjön shelter; use only if current fire-ban status and reserve rules allow.

facilities.name: Alsjöklint viewpoint
facilities.description: Viewpoint near the demanding Stora Alsjön terrain; approximate side/rest feature.

facilities.name: Stora Alsjön north shelter
facilities.description: Newer shelter/rest area on the north headland of Stora Alsjön with benches, view, and fireplace. Strong location but dated user-reported wet-floor/design/weather-protection complaints. Firewood bin is reported about 100 m north/up-trail, but Naturkartan says stock is not guaranteed; bring your own.

facilities.name: Stora Alsjön north fireplace
facilities.description: Designated fireplace at Stora Alsjön north point. Fires only at designated places and current fire bans override use.

facilities.name: Stora Alsjön natural water
facilities.description: Lake water at the shelter area; not a verified drinking-water tap. Treat/filter/boil.

facilities.name: Stora Alsjön reserve parking
facilities.description: Side access/parking for Stora Alsjön reserve and local loop, separate from the official Yngsviken endpoint. Länsstyrelsen says it is reached from Molstabergsvägen west of the reserve, and Naturkartan describes about 6 cars and an information board.

facilities.name: Yngsviken parking and stage 13 start
facilities.description: Stage-end access and official parking at the stage 13 start. Official Stage 12 calls it good parking, but exact car-park footprint/capacity is under-mapped and no nearby regular public transport or toilet was verified.

facilities.name: Yngsviken Stage 12/13 join
facilities.description: Shared Stage 12/13 topology node. End Stage 12 here; do not include Topo GPS-style extra tails or Stage 13/Djupsjön facilities in core Stage 12.

facilities.name: Yngsviken missing-sign caution
facilities.description: A 2024 official comment reported a missing/damaged sign about 1 km before Yngsviken. No official current fault is listed, but keep navigation attention high near the endpoint until field-verified.

facilities.name: Högfors side-access bus
facilities.description: Closest OSM bus stop found by straight line to Vattgruvan, around 3 km away and not a clean trailhead. Verify live service and walking route before relying on it.

facilities.name: Molstaberg side-access bus
facilities.description: Distant side-access bus context south/west of the reserve road network. Far from core Stage 12; verify live service and route before using it.

facilities.name: Hunting season awareness
facilities.description: Hiking is not forbidden during hunting, but during active hunting periods, especially from the large moose hunt starting 8 October, watch for signs, many parked cars, or local notices and choose another area if hunting appears active.

facilities.name: Stora Envättern continuation warning
facilities.description: Stage 13 continuation context, not core Stage 12: Länsstyrelsen warns of bark-beetle-damaged spruce that can fall suddenly, especially in wind; fishing is prohibited and toilet status at the reserve parking is changing/uncertain.

facilities.name: Yngsviken information boards
facilities.description: Endpoint information-board context near the Yngsviken road crossing and parking/access area.

facilities.name: Myssjö gård side service
facilities.description: Nearby paid accommodation/activity provider reached by continuing toward stage 13 and side roads; not on core stage 12, not a public shop/resupply point, and no nearby public transport is claimed.

sections.name: Stage 12:1: Mölnbo IP to Etapp 12
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 12:1, Mölnbo IP to Etapp 12.
utilities: Official area: Mölnbo, Södertäljes kommun.

Mölnbo commuter rail station is the practical public-transport access point; the signed approach adds about 1 km before the official Mölnbo IP stage start. Some maps/signs show about 5-5.6 km when this station approach is included.
Mölnbo station is served by SL commuter rail toward Södertälje/Gnesta and local bus context such as 786, but timetables should be checked live.

24Food Mölnbo and other station-area services such as Abbe's restaurang/cafe/livs are useful for resupply before/after the connector, but no all-hours public toilet or outdoor tap was verified on the forest section.

Mölnbo IP has nearby parking and sports-facility infrastructure. OSM maps a free wheelchair-accessible toilet near the IP/Bergabadet area, and Södertälje confirms Bergabadet toilets seasonally, but public access should be verified outside the bathing season.

Bergabadet is nearby seasonal beach/service context rather than a core trail facility: toilets are listed June-August, and local rules prohibit camping, grilling, fishing, alcohol, and dogs during 1 June-31 August.
Fristastugan by Bergasjön is a bookable Sörmlandsleden lodging/rest hut with kitchen and sauna context, not an open first-come trail shelter and not a free overnight facility.
waterSources: No verified potable water tap is on stage 12:1; carry water from town or resupply at station-area services.
Bergasjön/Norrbysjön and Akaren provide natural lake water and bathing/rest context only. Filter/boil/treat, and do not treat them as potable refill points.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official stage 12:1 is a 4 km connector from Mölnbo IP to the stage 12 junction. The station approach adds about 1 km, and OSM/signage/blog/AllTrails sources commonly show about 5-5.6 km when access walking is included.

For route drawing, keep two separate concepts: the optional Mölnbo station access spur to Mölnbo IP, and the official Mölnbo IP-to-Stage 12 connector. OSM relation 2390743 is useful, but its roughly 5 km tag includes the station-side access while Naturkartan and Sörmlandsleden list 4 km for the official connector.
The route is easy to moderate overall, with boardwalk/wetland terrain by Bergasjön/Norrbysjön and more hilly ground toward Akaren before it joins stage 12.

Official 2025 trail comments reported bark-beetle affected and felled trees that did not block the trail then, but made it a poor choice in windy weather. A later 2025 comment warned of long grass in late summer. Treat these as dated condition warnings, not official closures.

After rain or snowmelt, expect wetter ground around the Bergasjön/Norrbysjön boardwalks. Late-summer long grass also raises tick exposure, so this connector is not as frictionless as its short distance suggests.
The trail passes through Sjundareviret wolf territory according to the official page; this is a wildlife awareness note, not a closure.
Keep dogs controlled throughout; national wildlife-protection rules are stricter 1 March-20 August, and Bergabadet separately bans dogs on the bathing area 1 June-31 August.

No official campsite, overnight shelter, or prepared Sörmlandsleden shelter was verified on this connector. The Bergasjön wind shelter reported by Grillplatser is in very poor condition and should not be treated as usable overnight shelter.

Use only prepared fire/grill places such as Bergasjön or Akaren where allowed, and check current fire bans before lighting a fire. Fixed public fireplaces can still be closed by stricter bans, and nearby reserve fire rules apply if continuing onto Stage 12.
Bergabadet bathing-water samples can say the lake is suitable for swimming during season, but that is not drinking-water approval. Do not map Bergasjön, Norrbysjön, or Akaren as potable water.

At the Stage 12 junction around 59.081138, 17.426726, the main route continues east toward Vattgruvan/Järna services and west toward Yngsviken/Stora Alsjön; Stora Kobäcken and Vattgruvsmossen toilet/parking are Stage 12 continuation facilities, not core Stage 12:1.

facilities.name: Mölnbo station bus stop east

facilities.name: 24Food Mölnbo
facilities.description: Station-area 24/7 resupply listed by Sörmlandsleden and municipal records; useful before/after the connector, not an outdoor trail tap.

facilities.name: Abbe's restaurang/cafe/livs
facilities.description: Station-area food/cafe/livs context from map research. Treat as opening-hours dependent and verify before relying on it.

facilities.name: Mölnbo IP start/parking
facilities.description: Official stage start with nearby parking. Södertälje confirms parking in connection with the sports facility, but exact visitor capacity should be checked locally.

facilities.name: Official Stage 12:1 start
facilities.description: Canonical start for distance/filtering is Mölnbo IP. The station approach is a separate optional spur, so official Stage 12:1 remains 4 km.

facilities.name: Bergabadet seasonal beach services
facilities.description: Nearby seasonal bathing-place context with toilets June-August, changing rooms, accessible ramp, jetty/diving tower, free parking, and strict local rules: no camping, grilling, fishing, or alcohol; dogs prohibited 1 Jun-31 Aug.

facilities.name: Bergabadet parking
facilities.description: Free seasonal bathing-place parking near Bergabadet; useful for local access but separate from the official Mölnbo IP trail start. Check local signs before overnight parking.

facilities.name: Bergabadet beach rules
facilities.description: Rule marker: municipal beach rules prohibit camping, grilling, fishing, and alcohol; dogs are not allowed on the beach 1 June-31 August. Bathing-water monitoring is not drinking-water verification.

facilities.name: Dog-control warning
facilities.description: Keep dogs controlled on the trail; Swedish wildlife-protection rules are stricter 1 Mar-20 Aug, and Bergabadet has its own summer dog ban on the bathing area.

facilities.name: Bergasjön grill/rest point
facilities.description: Grillplats.nu lists a prepared grill/rest point by the lake. The mapped wind shelter is reported in very poor condition with roof damage and should not be treated as usable overnight shelter.

facilities.name: Bergasjön lake water
facilities.description: Lake/bathing water near the early route; filter/boil/treat and carry backup.

facilities.name: Fristastugan bookable lodging

facilities.name: Long grass / tick-season caution

facilities.name: Akaren fireplace/rest point

facilities.name: Akaren lake water

facilities.name: Etapp 12 junction
facilities.description: Exact shared node where stage 12:1 joins Stage 12; continue east toward Vattgruvan/Järna and Stora Kobäcken/Vattgruvsmossen services, or west toward Yngsviken/Stora Alsjön.

facilities.name: Mölnbo IP / Bergabadet toilet (verify)
facilities.description: OSM lists a free wheelchair-accessible toilet near Mölnbo IP/Bergabadet. Official trail sources do not confirm all-hours public access; Bergabadet municipal toilets are seasonal.

facilities.name: Stora Kobäcken continuation shelter
facilities.description: Stage 12 continuation service about 1.1 km east of the 12:1 junction: shelter, fireplace, benches, tent context, and nearby Vattgruvsmossen toilet/parking. Bring your own wood and treat water.

facilities.name: Vattgruvsmossen continuation toilet/parking
facilities.description: Stage 12 continuation/reserve access east of the junction, useful if route-building toward Vattgruvan/Järna rather than stopping at the connector junction.

facilities.name: STF Långbro Gård

sections.name: Stage 13: Yngsviken to Djupviksängen
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 13, Yngsviken to Djupviksängen.
utilities: Official area: Gnesta kommun, Södertäljes kommun.

Yngsviken has official stage-start parking, but capacity appears limited in trip reports and OSM only weakly maps the parking geometry. Djupviksängen is an endpoint/access point, but stage 14 sources explicitly say there is no parking at the etappstart.

No strong direct public transport was verified at Yngsviken or Stora Envättern; Södertälje/Naturkartan context says public transport is missing there. For rail-based access, use connected stages or the 13:1 Gnesta and 13:2 Nykvarn connectors, which meet stage 13 at/near Djupsjön.

Closest practical bus context near the Djupviksängen/Djupviken side is Alsjötorp on the Läggesta-Laxne-Gnesta corridor, about 2.5 km west of Djupviken; it is not a simple trailhead stop and service can be sparse.

Stora Envättern reserve parking gives a useful side access/loop point from the road toward Römossen, and Friluftsfrämjandet describes parking on both sides of the road at Yngsviken. Recent Naturkartan context warns that access roads can be poor after nearby forestry traffic.

A toilet is mapped at Stora Envättern reserve parking by OSM/Naturkartan, while Länsstyrelsen text still says no toilet / construction planned or underway. Treat it as newly mapped or unverified until checked in the field.
Myssjö Gård is a nearby sponsored lodging/food context east of Yngsviken, but it is off the main Stage 13 line and should be shown as a detour service rather than a trail facility.
Källsvik 30 on the 13:2 connector has a stronger year-round tap, but it belongs to an optional Nykvarn connector rather than the core Yngsviken-Djupviksängen stage.
waterSources: Official water points include the spring after 2 km, the 13:2 connector spring north of Djupsjön, Stora Kvarnsjön, and Djupvikssjön. Treat all as natural/untested water even where OSM labels a point drinking water; the early spring and Stora Kvarnsjön are short side markers rather than pins directly on the walking line.
A July 2023 official trail comment said the last water source was completely dry, and blogs note some sources may not look fresh. Carry backup water even though several natural sources are mapped.
No treated tap was confirmed on the stage. Djupsjön and Fräkensjöberget are overnight nodes, not potable-water guarantees.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 15 km; Naturkartan agrees, while OSM relation 2390726, Äventyrligare, and AllTrails commonly measure about 14.5 km. Keep the official distance for planning and treat the measured line as approximate; OSM's geometry is useful but has stale/typo destination text.

For route drawing, use the official Yngsviken-to-Djupviksängen identity and the shared Stage 14 endpoint around 59.156016,17.228880. OSM relation 2390726 has a destination typo and mixed way-member orientation, so order geometry graph-wise from Yngsviken to Djupviksängen rather than trusting member order.

True wilderness stretch: steep climb from Yngsviken, easier forest toward Stora Envättern, then lakes, bogs, ridges, shelters, and reserve land. Recent reviews describe the first 10 km as demanding, rocky/scrambly, wet/slippery in places, and generally well marked.

Official warning: scattered bark-beetle damaged spruce can fall suddenly, especially in wind or bad weather. Stora Envättern and Holmsjöskogen reserve context repeats the warning, and some reviews report blowdown without treating it as an official closure. Avoid resting under dead spruce and avoid the route in strong wind.
Hiker reports and reviews describe wet, muddy, and slippery sections after rain, spring thaw, and late autumn; poles and waterproof footwear are useful despite the moderate official difficulty.
The stage passes through or near Stora Envättern, Holmsjöskogen, Lugnet, and Djupviken reserves. Reserve rules override allemansrätten; use prepared fire sites and check local restrictions.
Stora Envättern reserve: fires only at designated fireplaces, fishing prohibited, dogs leashed, no cycling except on constructed road, and tenting is limited to at most two consecutive nights.

Holmsjöskogen, Lugnet, and Djupviken reserve contexts prohibit damaging live or dead wood and protected flora. Holmsjöskogen roads are gated and access is best via Sörmlandsleden; Lugnet has no suitable parking. Holmsjöskogen allows only small fires from loose dry twigs where otherwise permitted, while Stora Envättern is stricter with designated fire sites only.

Djupsjön is the best verified overnight/service node on this stage because it combines shelter, fireplace, dry toilet/bin context, and branch access. Fräkensjöberget is the second key shelter/viewpoint node and has no reliable water at the shelter.

The 13:1 Gnesta and 13:2 Nykvarn branches connect at separate OSM nodes about 10 m apart near Djupsjön; show one route-builder hub but keep exact geometry nodes separate. Add those branches only once this part of the main route is selected. 13:1 has a June 2025 reroute near Frustuna/Jagbacken; 13:2 has the Källsvik tap and the spring north of Djupsjön.
General Sörmlandsleden shelter guidance says not to expect bins, but the Stage 13 maintainer note specifically mentions dry toilets and bins at Djupsjön and Holmsjön. Pack out trash regardless.

facilities.description: OSM maps a shelter near the Stora Envättern entrance/parking, but official Stage 13 lists only Djupsjön and Fräkensjöberget as shelters. Treat as map-sourced rest context until field-verified.

facilities.name: Alsjötorp bus context
facilities.description: Closest verified bus-corridor context for the Djupviksängen/Djupviken side, about 2.5 km west via local roads/trails. Check Sörmlandstrafiken line 543/live traffic before relying on it.

sections.name: Stage 13:1: Gnesta to Etapp 13
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 13:1, Gnesta to Etapp 13.
utilities: Official area: Gnesta kommun, Södertäljes kommun.

Gnesta station is the official start and the strong access/service node, with SL commuter rail, Mälartåg/regional trains, buses, town services, and parking around the station area. Check live traffic because rail replacement buses and timetable changes can occur.

Gnesta station parking is verified in several station-area lots, and Sörmlandstrafiken maps bus bays, kiosk, restaurant, taxi, waiting room, and station parking nearby. Local rules vary: Gnesta kommun notes free central parking with P-disc/24 h weekday rules in places, so check signs before leaving a car.
Gnesta has the strongest resupply on the connector, with ICA, Coop, visitor/tourist information, and other town services within a short walk of the station.

Klämmingsbergsbadet is the main mid-route service node, but most services are seasonal. Municipality/Campcation sources place the rental/visitor-service period roughly 1 June-30 September, with full service strongest in summer; the Kattnäs road barrier is reported open 1 May-30 September.

Gnesta municipality plans Klämmingsbergsbadet upgrades from 2026, including toilets, kiosk, parking, showers/changing rooms, washing-up places for campers, and service improvements. Treat facility layout and availability as potentially changing during works.
Frustuna and Kattnäs church areas provide useful toilet/parking context near the route, but these are church/visitor services rather than official Sörmlandsleden trail utilities.
No Sörmlandsleden shelter was verified on 13:1 itself. The nearest confirmed shelter/fireplace/toilet cluster is Djupsjön on the Stage 13 continuation east/northeast of the connector junction.
waterSources: No reliable year-round potable trail tap was confirmed along the connector.

Klämmingsbergsbadet likely has seasonal drinking water while the bathing/camping service is open based on a hiker comment and service-building context, but municipality sources do not explicitly guarantee a public drinking-water tap. Treat it as seasonal/unverified.
Klämmingen and other lakes are bathing/natural water only; filter/boil/treat if used.
The nearby Stage 13 / 13:2 spring north of Djupsjön is continuation/branch context, not core 13:1 water, and can be seasonal or dry; carry enough water from Gnesta or confirmed seasonal services.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.
Official distance is 13 km; Naturkartan agrees and AllTrails/Äventyrligare are close at about 13.2 km.

Official route changed in June 2025 after Frustuna kyrka, with a new alignment over Jagbacken via the scout hut before the Södertuna road/cycleway section. The official map was updated 2025-06-11; OSM relation 6620044 was later surveyed/edited in November 2025 and appears continuous, but older GPX/app caches and comments can still conflict, so use current official/Naturkartan geometry as canonical.

For route drawing, use the official Gnesta start coordinate 59.048333,17.312467 even if OSM relation 6620044 begins about 80 m away at the station-side node. At the north end, connect 13:1 to Stage 13 at OSM node 2819424933 and keep the adjacent 13:2 join about 9 m away as its own exact junction.

Model this as a station-to-forest access connector: Gnesta services, Frustuna/Jagbacken reroute, about 1 km of road/cycleway near Södertuna, farm/field roads toward Kattnäs, Klämmingsbergsbadet, then forest roads, paths, clearcut/overgrowth stretches, and hillier ground toward the main stage.
The actual connector/main-route join is west/southwest of the Djupsjön service node; do not visually snap the whole branch directly to the shelter if route geometry shows a separate join.

Recent/third-party comments mention long road/cycleway sections, clear-cut feeling sections, tall grass, branches, and the 2025 reroute. Official page reported no active fault reports at the time of research.

User reports generally treat 13:1 as a useful transit connector rather than a showcase stage: easy-to-moderate overall, but with long gravel/asphalt/field-road stretches, summer heat/bugs/ticks, and a hillier forest finish after Klämmingsbergsbadet.
Use only confirmed public fire/grill places such as Klämmingsbergsbadet and Djupsjön; Frustunaby/Jagbacken scout hut is a rentable/group facility, not a public shelter, toilet, tap, or fireplace.
Frustunaby/Scoutgården is a private/group-rental property with its own guest rules; the trail passes outside the entrance, so do not map it as public trail infrastructure.

Gnesta local order rules matter around public places: alcohol is banned at public bathing places, camping is banned at public bathing places except arranged/paid camping, dogs must be leashed in covered public areas and kept off public bathing places 15 May-15 September except assigned dog-bathing areas, and dog waste must be picked up.

Klämmingen fishing requires a valid Gnestaortens FVOF permit, and ordinary rules include hand-gear limitations, pike-perch size/limit rules, and no fishing within 100 m of private jetties or boat places.

Adjacent Stage 13 reserve context matters if continuing beyond the connector: Stora Envättern has dead-spruce/bark-beetle fall risk in wind, fires only at designated sites, no fishing, dogs leashed, no off-road cycling, and max two consecutive tent nights.

facilities.description: Between Södertuna, Kattnäs, and Klämmingsbergsbadet the route uses farm/field roads. Stay on marked trail, avoid yards/tomtmark, do not damage crops, close gates if used, and avoid disturbing residents or livestock.
