facilities.description: Municipal bathing/camping area with seasonal service building, changing rooms, kiosk, cabins/camping, caravan/camper places, dog-bathing area, grill, and beach access. Road barrier at Kattnäs is reported open 1 May-30 Sep.

facilities.name: Klämmingsbergsbadet parking
facilities.description: Parking near the bathing/camping area; access and payment/signage should be checked locally, especially outside the May-September road-gate season.

facilities.name: Klämmingsbergsbadet toilets/showers
facilities.description: Seasonal toilets/showers/service building; strongest confirmed mid-route toilet context, but verify opening period before relying on it.

facilities.description: Prepared grill/fireplace at the bathing area, with benches/table and beach context. Grillplatser notes a small shelter, but it is not suitable for overnighting; check fire bans.

facilities.description: Seasonal paid camping/cabins/camper area. Gnesta context lists four small cabins and camper/caravan places bookable roughly 1 Jun-30 Sep, with service levels strongest in summer.

facilities.description: Local-rule marker: public bathing-place alcohol and camping restrictions apply; dogs must use the assigned dog-bathing area and are otherwise restricted from public bathing places 15 May-15 Sep. Bathing/jetties are at your own risk, children need supervision, and fire is only at prepared places when allowed.

sections.name: Stage 13:2: Nykvarn to Etapp 13
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 13:2, Nykvarn to Etapp 13.
utilities: Official area: Gnesta kommun, Nykvarn.

Nykvarn station/centrum is the official access cluster, with the stage board about 100 m west of the railway station at Maskinförarvägen/Holländarvägen. Nykvarn has rail/bus access plus town services before the low-service connector begins.

Official parking options are Nykvarn centrum, Jägarskogens naturreservat, and Sandtorpsbadet. Nykvarn kommun lists several station-area/central parking options, but also says there is no municipal long-term parking; check signs and avoid assuming multi-day parking.
SL bus 780/780X serves the Södertälje-Nykvarn/Sandtorp corridor, but schedules and deviations should be checked live rather than hardcoded. The Djupsjön end still has poor direct public transport.
Nykvarn-area resupply and lodging are start-side only: ICA/centrum services are close to the stage board, while Turinge Hotel and Vidbynäs are off-route lodging options north/east of the start.

No verified public toilet was found at Nykvarn station or Sandtorpsbadet. Use Nykvarn town services before starting; the nearest mapped toilets are at Djupsjön near the connector end, and those should be treated as Stage 13/end-area context.
The Djupsjön/Stage 13 end has poor direct public transport. For transit-based trips, continue via the 13:1 Gnesta connector or arrange pickup rather than assuming a bus stop at the junction.
waterSources: Källsvik 30 has the strongest refill: an official year-round tap outside the carport. It is trail-listed but private-property-adjacent; be quiet, use only the listed tap, and do not camp, cook, wash, leave trash, block driveways, or enter yards/buildings.

The spring north of Djupsjön is an official natural source about 800 m north of Djupsjön; treat/filter and field-check flow. Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water access or quality, and dry-period source reports exist nearby.

Yngern, Gullsmorasjön, and Djupsjön are natural lake water only. Yngern is often described as very clean and Nykvarn planning material supports high water-quality context, but none of the lakes are verified potable refill points.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 17 km; Naturkartan agrees, while GPS/third-party traces commonly show about 15.8-16.6 km and the local map geometry measures about 16.6 km. Keep official distance for planning, with a drawn-distance caveat around 16 km.

OpenStreetMap relation 7604344 is useful context but is explicitly tagged 'Leden 13:2 ej komplett', has inconsistent distance metadata, measures around 16.1 km, and appears to start about 0.5 km short of the official Nykvarn start. Do not use it as the sole route authority; preserve the official start coordinate and branch status.
The connector opened in September 2017 and links Nykvarn into the Sörmlandsleden system at Djupsjön, where 13:2 and 13:1 meet the main stage 13 planning area.

Route character: town start, old forest toward northern Yngern, Sandtorpsbadet, Vargberget views, more road/gravel than the official prose makes obvious, then Sjöslingan along Yngern toward the Yngern/Gullsmorasjön passage.

Official suitable tent places are Sandtorpsbadet and Anderså. Sandtorpsbadet should be shown as an official trail-suggested tent/bathing area with local-sign verification required, because Nykvarn local order rules generally ban camping on bathing places except where specifically arranged/permitted.
Jägarskogen reserve forbids tenting, caravans/campers, damaging dead or living wood, and allows fires only at prepared places; do not treat the reserve shelter or firepit as camping permission.

Nykvarn local guidance warns of grill restrictions at municipal bathing places; do not show Sandtorpsbadet as a fire site unless a specific prepared fireplace is verified and current fire rules allow use. Outdoor fire remains the visitor's responsibility even at prepared places.

Yngern fishing requires appropriate permit coverage; do not imply free fishing. Gullsmorasjön fishing rights were not verified in this pass, so hikers should check local fishing rights before fishing.

Official page reported no fault reports at the time of research. Main planning risks are sparse guaranteed services after Nykvarn, road/gravel-road segments after Vargberget and around Herrvik/Källsvik, early wayfinding around Nykvarn/Jägarskogen, wet roots/puddles after rain or winter thaw, overgrown forestry/skidder-path sections in summer, natural-water uncertainty, and nearby Stage 13 bark-beetle/dead-spruce hazards.

sections.name: Stage 14: Djupviksängen to Fredriksberg, väg 223
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 14, Djupviksängen to Fredriksberg, väg 223.
utilities: Official area: Gnesta kommun, Strängnäs kommun.
Djupviksängen is the official start but has no parking at the etappstart. Use connector planning, bus context, or the Björndalsbergen/Gullsmedsmoravägen access instead.

Fredriksberg/road 223 has only limited roadside parking for a few cars where the trail crosses the road. The old Fredriksberg bus stop is no longer a dependable stop; use nearby Svinsjö gård/Adolfsberg context and live-check rural departures.

No verified toilet, shop, or wind shelter was found directly on stage 14. The only stage water is the Lövviken natural spring; nearby bus stops such as Alsjötorp, Lilla Hammarbosäter, Svinsjö gård, and Adolfsberg need live timetable checks before relying on them.
Björndalsbergen/Gullsmedsmora parking is the best reserve/loop access; the loop road crossing may fit only a single car and should not be treated as primary parking.
waterSources: The official spring shortly after the road to Lövviken is the only explicit stage water source. OSM maps the same source as Källa/drinking_water, and 2016/2024 hiker reports found good/cold/fresh water, but Sörmlandsleden source quality is not routinely guaranteed; treat/filter unless current quality is verified.
Glådran and Klämmingen are natural lake water only and should not be treated as potable refill points.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 6.5 km; Naturkartan and OSM relation 3808981 agree, while measured geometry and GPS/app traces are around 6.3-6.6 km. Older 8 km references appear stale and should not override the current official length.

Short but fairly demanding stage: steep climb from Djupviksängen up Lövviksbergen, views over Klämmingen, then hällmark and forest toward Ulvsättersbergen and Glådran. AllTrails-style elevation figures around 224-228 m ascent are plausible for difficulty context.

Active official warning dated 2025-11-14: forestry work on the northern part from Glådran to road 223 has left timber piles across the trail, muddy machine ruts/ditches, difficult passage, and markings that may need review after felling. Treat this as a live safety caveat until the official page removes it.

The Björndalsbergen/Glådran loop is a useful related option: official loop is 3.5 km, starts at the Björndalsbergen access, and adds about 1 km if used instead of the direct main-route line. In the route builder, present it as a selectable alternate between the south split near 59.168746, 17.215879 and the rejoin near 59.173224, 17.215308, not as an independent through-stage.

For geometry, OSM relation 3808981 is the correct Stage 14 relation but is stored mostly north-to-south; reverse/order it for the official Djupviksängen-to-Fredriksberg direction. The measured relation is about 6.36 km, compatible with the official 6.5 km.

Glådran is the best verified overnight/rest area on the stage, with official tenting guidance and confirmed north/south fireplaces. Southwest Glådran is officially preferred for tents, but 2024 reports note limited truly flat ground; northeast also works and has a table/simple fireplace context. Use prepared fire sites only and check current fire bans.

Björndalsbergen reserve rules prohibit damaging living/dead trees and collecting protected plants/fungi; berries, edible mushrooms, and flowers for personal use are allowed. Bring your own fuel rather than collecting reserve wood, and get permission for organized camps/competitions.
Use leash/close-control as the practical dog default in the reserve and around wildlife, especially during the national 1 March-20 August sensitive period.
Do not imply free fishing at Glådran or Klämmingen. Gnesta fishing-card rules apply to Klämmingen/Frösjön and related waters, while Glådran-specific public fishing permission was not verified.
Rural bus service around Laxne, Lilla Hammarbosäter, Svinsjö gård, and Adolfsberg is sparse and pattern-dependent; show these as access context, not guaranteed trailhead service.

sections.name: Stage 15: Fredriksberg, väg 223 to Skottvångs gruva
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 15, Fredriksberg, väg 223 to Skottvångs gruva.
utilities: Official area: Gnesta kommun, Strängnäs kommun.
Fredriksberg/road 223 has limited parking at the former bus-stop/road pocket; the Fredriksberg bus stop has been removed, so use Svinsjö gård as the closest bus context and check live timetables.

Skottvång is the strong service endpoint with parking, restaurant/cafe/pub/event service, seasonal museum, toilet, shower, sauna, tap water, simple lodging, and nearby shelters, but opening, firewood, and booking conditions vary.

Public transport to Skottvång is weak. Bus 543 can be used to Svinsjö gård/Skottvångsvägen context with a road walk, and Sörmlandstrafiken complementary traffic may cover Skottvång on limited pre-booked days; live-check before planning around it.
Road access via Mariefred/Läggesta/väg 223 may be affected by planned autumn 2026 road works around Kärnbogatan/Mariefred access; this is approach logistics rather than a forest-stage closure.
waterSources: The first official spring after about 1.2 km has poor/uncertain supply in summer; carry backup.
The Marvikarna/Långaedet spring before Marviken is an official natural source; treat/filter unless freshly verified.
Skottvång tap water is available through the bystuga/bybastu/service facilities when accessible; treat it as service-linked rather than a guaranteed outdoor public tap.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 10.5 km; Naturkartan agrees, Gnesta municipality rounds to 11 km, and third-party traces are close at about 10.1-10.6 km, with AllTrails-style traces around 10.6 km and roughly 370 m ascent. Naturkartan GPX can export in reversed/segmented pieces with tiny artifacts, so normalize direction as Fredriksberg to Skottvång before ingesting geometry.

OSM relation 3806515 is the correct main Stage 15 geometry, tagged 10.5 km and measuring about 10.29 km by summed member geometry, but its member order is reversed relative to the official Fredriksberg-to-Skottvång direction. The OSM endpoint is within about 2 m of official Fredriksberg and about 12 m of official Skottvång.

Moderate, hilly and sometimes rocky day stage with forest, cultural remains, springs, steep Marvikarna/Långaedet terrain, Stenhuggarmon viewpoint/tower, old ore-railway embankment, and Skottvång mining heritage. In wet, snowy, or icy conditions, expect slower progress than the distance suggests.

The official Stage 15 fault-report field currently says no submitted faults, but an official-page public comment from 2025-08-20 reports many fallen trees near the end toward Skeppsmora-Skottvång and suggests the road for the last about 2 km if needed. Stage 15:2 separately has an official 2025-06-02 fallen-tree warning around Millsjön, where biotope protection limits clearing.
Långaedet reserve has bark-beetle affected spruce that can fall, especially in wind. Reserve rules prohibit damaging living/dead wood except collecting small loose dry twigs for a small fire.

Marvikarna/Krampan rules are stricter: Marvikarna prohibits camping and fires; Krampan allows fires only at designated places and tenting only at marked places for up to two nights. Dogs/pets must be leashed or caged, fishing needs the relevant local permit, and Klövberget/Falkberget bird-protection areas are closed 1 February-15 August.
Mellan-Marviken is a shared hiker/canoe shelter node with two shelters, tent context, toilet, fireplace, bathing, and unknown-quality natural water; it can be busy and firewood is not guaranteed.

Route-builder handling: show 15:1 access only when the selected route reaches the Långaedet junction node 2908209697, and show 15:2 only when the selected route reaches the Mellan-Marviken split node 2908209630 or the southern reconnect node 2298697773. A standalone 15:2 route must include the shared Stage 15 tail from node 2298697773 to Skottvång.

sections.name: Stage 15:1: Läggesta to Långaedet, etapp 15
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 15:1, Läggesta to Långaedet, etapp 15.
utilities: Official area: Strängnäs kommun.

Läggesta station is the only strong utility node on 15:1 itself, with rail/bus access, paid parking, three toilets including accessible WC, waiting-room/kiosk context, taxi, lifts, bike parking, and locked cycle garage. Terminal-map bus context includes lines 303, 305, 306, 543, 642, 646, and 841; live-check departures.

Läggesta parking is paid rather than ordinary free trail parking: station zone 18853, currently 30 SEK/day or 340 SEK/month, with a maximum 7 consecutive days on paid outdoor/garage spaces; long-stay/gravel-area rules should be checked locally.

After leaving Läggesta, no confirmed on-connector shelter, campsite, fireplace, toilet, shop, or reliable potable trail tap was verified. Treat Långaedet/Mellan-Marviken services as nearby continuation context, not core 15:1 facilities.
Långaedet is a trail junction into stage 15, not a public-transport trailhead. Naturkartan finds no useful stops there; train-based trips should use Läggesta unless continuing through.
waterSources: No reliable potable trail water was confirmed on 15:1 before the main-route junction; carry water from Läggesta unless continuing to known Stage 15 sources.

The official water note points to a cold spring a short distance after joining Stage 15 toward Stage 14. It is roughly 160 m straight-line from the 15:1 junction and about 300 m by trail context; OSM maps drinking_water nearby, but hiker reports describe missed/dry springs in this broader area, so treat/filter and do not count it as on-connector water.
Laketorpsån is scenic stream/rest context, not a drinking-water refill; older Sörmlandsleden material explicitly warns hikers not to drink from the brook.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 6 km; Naturkartan/Äventyrligare and measured GPX are about 6.15-6.2 km, while AllTrails-style traces can show 6.6-6.8 km with about 200 m ascent. Use official distance for planning and mapped distance for geometry.

OSM relation 3806868 is the correct 15:1 connector and measures about 6.163 km. The official direction is Läggesta to Långaedet, but raw member order can behave as junction-to-Läggesta; route builders should orient from OSM node 2234456923 near Läggesta to node 2908209697 at the Stage 15 junction.

Treat 15:1 as an access connector, not part of the main Stage 15 chain. Offer it only when the selected route includes the Långaedet junction node 2908209697 or when the user explicitly selects Läggesta/15:1.

Access connector from Läggesta station to Långaedet/Stage 15: roughly the first kilometre follows asphalt/road 223 near E20 and then passes under the motorway, with road noise/sun exposure. Several hiker reports say the route does not feel properly off-road until around Ådals kvarn after about 3 km. Walk left where no footway/shoulder exists, use visibility in low light, and do not enter E20 ramps or shoulders.

After Ådals kvarn the route improves: it follows Laketorpsån through a leafy ravine, passes Laketorp meadow/rest context, then uses old path/forest toward a steep descent into Långaedet. Hiker reports consistently treat Ådals kvarn as the mood shift from transport walking to real trail.

Official 15:1 page had no fault reports at research time, but hiker reports note the road/noise/sun-exposed opening, possible muddy/riding-path wear around Ådals/Laketorp, and the descent toward Långaedet can be steep, slippery, icy, or rope-assisted in poor conditions. In winter/thaw, poles or traction can matter more than the short distance suggests.

Långaedet reserve has bark-beetle damaged spruce that can fall, especially in wind. Do not damage living/dead trees; only small loose dry twigs may be collected for a small fire. No designated campsite was verified on the connector; camp only where suitable and permitted under allemansrätten and current fire restrictions.

Do not imply broad camping/fire permission around Långaedet/Marvikarna. Nearby Marvikarna/Krampan continuation has stricter designated-site rules, fishing-card assumptions for inland waters, pet-control rules, and bird-protection closures; keep those as continuation context.

facilities.name: Läggesta trail start

facilities.name: Läggesta station

facilities.name: Läggesta station toilets
facilities.description: Station toilet context: municipal station information lists three toilets, including accessible WC; exact indoor pin not exposed.

facilities.name: Läggesta station kiosk/snacks
facilities.description: Limited snack/kiosk context near the station; OSM and parcel-service listings confirm the shop but opening hours differ, so verify current hours and do not rely on it as full resupply.

facilities.name: Läggesta bike parking/garage
facilities.description: Covered bike-parking context plus municipal locked bike-garage subscription; useful for train-bike access but verify current availability.

facilities.name: Läggesta Nedre heritage railway

facilities.name: Sörby bus context

facilities.name: Road/E20 noise section

facilities.name: Road walking safety
facilities.description: Road 223/E20 approach: use the trail underpass, do not enter E20/ramp shoulders, walk on the left where there is no footway or shoulder, and use high visibility in low light.

facilities.name: Ådalskvarns vägskäl bus context
facilities.description: Nearby bus-stop context for the early road section; check live Sörmlandstrafiken.

facilities.name: Ådals kvarn / Laketorpsån bridge
facilities.description: Historic mill/stream point; official text mentions an old mill pond and remains of a silversmithy above the dam. Hiker reports mark this as the mood shift from transport walking to forest/stream path.

facilities.name: Laketorps skola bus context
facilities.description: Possible mid-connector road/bus context near the trail corridor; not a guaranteed frequent stop, so check live Sörmlandstrafiken before relying on it.

facilities.name: Laketorpsån valley
facilities.description: Scenic incised stream valley and deciduous ravine; natural stream context only, not a water refill. Older Sörmlandsleden material warns not to drink from the brook.

facilities.name: Laketorp rest meadow
facilities.description: Official text says the meadow at Laketorp can be used as a rest spot.

facilities.name: Laketorp seasonal mud/riding-path wear
facilities.description: User reports describe the path after Ådals kvarn/Laketorp as a proper but sometimes muddy path also used by riders; treat as a seasonal soft-ground caution.

facilities.name: Stavtorp bus context
facilities.description: Possible road bailout east of the trail corridor, not directly on trail and likely infrequent. Check live planner before relying on it.

facilities.name: Old pack trail / steep descent
facilities.description: Route becomes more forested and descends steeply toward Långaedet; hiker reports mention rope/support usefulness and icy/slippery conditions in winter.

facilities.name: Långaedet / Stage 15 junction

facilities.name: Långaedet picnic site

facilities.name: Långaedet dry toilet

facilities.name: Långaedet fireplace/picnic

facilities.name: Nearby stage 15 spring

facilities.name: Nearby Bronze Age cairn
facilities.description: Nearby Stage 15 cultural-history context by Långaedet/Marviken narrows; useful if continuing from the connector.

facilities.name: Nearby Mellan-Marviken shelter
facilities.description: Continuation facility south on adjoining stage 15/15:2, not on the 15:1 connector: two shelters, toilet, fireplace/grill, tent context, bathing, and unknown-quality water.

facilities.name: Nearby Mellan-Marviken dry toilet
facilities.description: Dry toilet at/near Mellan-Marviken shelter area, within the useful planning buffer but not on the 15:1 connector itself.

facilities.name: Nearby Mellan-Marviken fireplace
facilities.description: Grill/fireplace context at the Mellan-Marviken shelters, confirmed by shelter/fireplace map sources. Use only if reserve rules and current fire conditions allow.

facilities.name: South Mellan-Marviken picnic/firepit
facilities.description: Nearby OSM picnic/firepit south of the main shelter cluster; off the 15:1 connector and should be treated as continuation context.

facilities.name: Långaedet reserve warning
facilities.description: Bark-beetle affected spruce may fall. Do not damage living/dead wood; only small loose dry twigs may be collected for a small fire. Check current fire bans and posted reserve boards.

facilities.name: Marvikarna/Krampan continuation rules
facilities.description: Continuation south of the 15:1 junction has stricter rules: Marvikarna prohibits camping and fires, Krampan allows fires only at designated places and tenting only in marked areas for up to two nights, dogs/pets leashed or caged, bird sanctuary closure applies 1 Feb-15 Aug, and fishing requires a local permit.

facilities.name: Klövberget/Falkberget continuation closure
facilities.description: Nearby continuation cliffs in the Marvikarna/Krampan reserve are closed to entry from 1 February to 15 August every year for bird protection.

facilities.name: Marvikarna water and ice safety
facilities.description: The Marvikarna/Långaedet lake system is steep and used for paddling, bathing, and winter skating. Use life jacket on water and follow Swedish ice-safety practice with knowledge, equipment, and company on natural ice.

facilities.name: Stage 15:2 Millsjön continuation warning
facilities.description: If continuing via 15:2, official 2025-06-02 warning reports fallen trees along the Millsjön west-side part; passable but awkward, and biotope protection limits clearing.

sections.name: Stage 15:2: Mellan-Marviken, etapp 15 to Skottvångs gruva
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 15:2, Mellan-Marviken, etapp 15 to Skottvångs gruva.
utilities: Official area: Gnesta kommun, Strängnäs kommun.
Mellan-Marviken is a strong overnight/rest node with shared shelters, dry toilet, prepared fireplace/grill, tent space, bathing, and lake water of unknown quality.

Skottvångs gruva is the endpoint service cluster: parking, accessible/toilet context, shower, sauna, tap water, restaurant/cafe/pub, museum, shop/event context, and bookable lodging are nearby, but most services are opening-hour, event, or booking dependent.
No shop, toilet, potable tap, or road access was verified between Mellan-Marviken and Skottvång on the core 15:2 connector.

Direct public transport to Skottvång is weak. Treat Skottvång as the practical car-access endpoint, and use current planners for sparse Skottvångsvägen/Svinsjö gård or book-ahead complementary traffic options; older/current material points to Thursday prebooked service for Skottvångs gruva but it must be verified.
waterSources: No reliable all-hours potable trail water was confirmed on 15:2 itself; carry water or refill at Skottvång/bybastun only when services or booked access are confirmed.

Mellan-Marviken and Millsjön are natural lake water only, and the Mellan-Marviken shelter listing describes water quality as unknown. Treat/filter/boil before use; do not treat lake access as a drinking-water refill.
The Marvikarna spring north of the start belongs to the nearby stage-15 continuation rather than the core connector; it is still natural water and should be treated.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official stage 15:2 is a short alternate/connector from Mellan-Marviken to Skottvångs gruva. Sörmlandsleden lists 4 km; Naturkartan/Äventyrligare and OSM relation-only geometry list about 3.6 km, while longer AllTrails-style traces usually combine stage 15, Fornborgsrundan, Millsjön runt, or Stenhuggarmon options.

OSM relation 3806869 is the correct alternate branch but is stored Skottvång-to-Mellan-Marviken, opposite the official direction, and measures about 3.587 km because it ends at the southern reconnect node 2298697773 instead of continuing to Skottvång. For a standalone official 15:2 route, append the shared Stage 15 tail via ways 220781792, 286933800, and 286933795; this gives about 4.0 km to the Skottvång shelter context.

Route character: follows the Mellan-Marviken area south for just under 1 km, then mixed forest, wetland/boardwalk-prone ground, and Millsjön before rejoining stage 15 shortly before Skottvång. Treat Skottvång shelter/service coordinates as endpoint facilities and keep the southern reconnect separate.

Official 2025-06-02 fault report: fallen trees lie across 15:2 and the Millsjön west-side loop/Fornborgsrundan. The route is passable but awkward, and clearing is limited because the area is biotope-protected.

Official/user comments from 2023 report very wet ground, mosquitoes, and a broken boardwalk directly south of Millsjön; a 2024 hiker report found flooding/washed-out boardwalks and turned back, and 2024/2025/2026 reports still mention fallen trees, mud, overgrowth, or difficult access around Millsjön/Fornborgsrundan.
Do not imply free detouring around Millsjön or the biotope area. Stay on the marked route where possible and avoid damaging protected shore and wetland ground.

Loop naming is easy to mix up in this area. Keep 15:2 as the connector/alternate, and present Fornborgsrundan/Millsjön runt and Stenhuggarmon as separate nested options that reuse parts of Stage 15/15:2 rather than as replacement section geometry.

Långaedet and Marvikarna/Krampan reserve rules apply around the connected route system: do not remove or damage deadwood, fires only where permitted/designated, tenting only at marked places in Krampan for normally max two nights, dogs/pets leashed or caged, and Klövberget/Falkberget bird-protection areas closed February 1-August 15.

Mellan-Marviken shelters are shared by hikers and canoeists and can be busy in season; a 2025 comment reported no firewood during one visit, and older blogs also found no firewood at nearby Marviken fire spots. Skottvång food/lodging/water/toilet access depends on opening hours, events, and booking.

Short distance does not always mean easy conditions: spring flooding, wet boardwalks, long summer grass/nettles, snow-covered markings, and recurring fallen trees can make this a slow half-day when combined with Stenhuggarmon or lunch.

facilities.description: Official 15:2 start coordinate at the Mellan-Marviken shelter/Stage 15 area. OSM relation 3806869 attaches to Stage 15 at node 2908209630, with nearby route nodes 2905504798 and 3831461621 closer to the official start.

facilities.name: Stage 15:2 rejoins stage 15
facilities.description: Exact OSM reconnect node 2298697773 where 15:2 rejoins Stage 15 before Skottvång. Standalone 15:2 needs the shared Stage 15 tail via ways 220781792, 286933800, and 286933795 from here.

facilities.name: Nearby stage-15 Marvikarna spring
facilities.description: Nearby natural spring on the stage-15 continuation north of the start, not on core 15:2. Treat/filter and verify seasonal flow.

facilities.name: Fornborgsrundan / ancient fort side route

facilities.name: Millsjön west-side fallen-tree warning
facilities.description: Active official 2025-06-02 warning: fallen trees on 15:2/Fornborgsrundan along Millsjön west side. Passable but awkward; biotope protection limits clearing, so do not clear deadwood or cut new detours.

facilities.name: Millsjön wet ground and boardwalk caution
facilities.description: Official 2023 comments reported very wet ground, mosquitoes, and a broken boardwalk directly south of Millsjön; a 2024 report described flooding/washed-out boardwalks and retreating from the intended branch, and later reviews still mention mud/overgrowth. Carry waterproof footwear and expect slow passage until field-confirmed repaired.

facilities.name: Millsjön natural water and biotope shore

facilities.description: Prepared grill/fireplace in the Krampan facility area; fires only at designated places and only when fire conditions allow.

facilities.name: Krampans badplats

facilities.name: Svinsjö gård bus context
