sections.name: Stage 24:3: Kvarntorp to Svalboviken
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 24:3, Kvarntorp to Svalboviken.
utilities: Official area: Eskilstunas kommun.

Kvarntorp and Svalboviken have parking/access context, but direct public transport is weak. Expect rural road walks from stops and verify Sörmlandstrafiken or prebooked rural traffic before relying on it.

Sandviken is the strongest on-stage facility cluster, with officially listed shelter, dry toilets, rubbish bins, swimming and good tent places. Bodavik is the second strong rest/overnight node with swimming, masonry fireplace, rubbish bin and good tent places, but facilities are confirmed while the exact pin is approximate.

No reliable shop, restaurant, toilet, tap, bin, or direct public transport was verified at Svalboviken. Sörmlandstrafiken line 29-style corridor stops may help with Näshulta/Svalboviken access, but they require road walks and live timetable checks. Österby Camping and Magdakullan are useful off-route seasonal/service contexts rather than trail guarantees.
waterSources: Two official natural springs are listed: shortly after Sandviken and before/near Goffars hage. Sörmlandsleden does not test or guarantee water quality or availability, so filter/boil/treat both and carry backup.

Lake water from Näshultasjön and nearby lakes is natural/untested. A hiker report from 2019 found several springs in this area dry and could not rely on Kvarntorp-area water, so carry enough water in dry periods.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official/Naturkartan distance is 11.5 km. OSM relation 9631289 is tagged distance=11.5 km and relation analysis measures about 11.1 km, while local/third-party tracks can be about 10.6-10.8 km; use official 11.5 km as canonical.

Draw Stage 24:3 as the standalone Kvarntorp-Svalboviken branch. Keep 24:2, stage 24, Kvarntorp parking, Fålludden/Sandviken/Bodavik parking access, Svalbovikens badplats, Trollberget viewpoint spur, Österby Camping, Näshulta kyrka transit and Magdakullan as separate context rather than core stage geometry.
Official difficulty is medelsvår. Treat as moderate but not technical: forest and lake walking, pasture/stiles, gravel sections, ravines/streams, viewpoints and some short climbs.

Official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 pass. A 2026-04-23 official comment reported good signing, easy wayfinding, many lake rest spots, beautiful pastures and only one short clearcut. Older beaver/cattle/gravel observations are seasonal/historical rather than current faults.

The first kilometres pass through Kvarntorp nature reserve. Do not damage trees, shrubs, plants, ground, stones or bedrock, especially by fire, and do not disturb cultural/natural features. No explicit camping ban was found in the page text, but reserve fire/damage rules apply and full legal decisions or posted signs govern details. Eskilstuna showed no formal fire ban during the 2026-04-27 pass, while county pages showed a forest-fire-risk signal, so treat open fires conservatively even without a ban.

Good tent places are officially listed at Sandviken and Bodavik. The route also passes cow pasture after Sandviken and low-volume rural/gravel roads at Fålludden, Heden/Bodavik and near Svalboviken; keep dogs leashed, close gates, give livestock room, and walk visibly on road sections. Do not add a Sandviken fireplace, Bodavik toilet/shelter, Kvarntorp toilet/bin/tap, Svalboviken toilet/bin/tap/shop, or potable tap claim; none were verified from official/OSM/service sources.

sections.name: Stage 25: Lundsjön to Vallmotorp
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 25, Lundsjön to Vallmotorp.
utilities: Official area: Katrineholms kommun.

Parking is possible near the Lundsjön start and at/near Vallmotorp, but the Lundsjön parking is unmapped/forest-road context and Vallmotorp parking is approximate; check local signs before leaving a car.

Myrgryten is the main on-stage overnight/rest node with shelter, dry toilet, fireplace/grill, bench/rest context and lake access. Do not assume bins or firewood. The nearby locked cabin/simple cabin and charcoal hut should be treated as bookable/organized or cultural context, not as guaranteed public shelters.
No shop or restaurant was verified directly on stage 25. Better services are in Katrineholm or by continuing toward Lövåsen on stage 26.

Public transport is weak at both endpoints. Naturkartan found no useful nearby stops for the stage page; use Sörmlandstrafiken live planning, and treat Bie/Ramsta/Björkhaga/Oxlångstorp-style rural stops and K10 complementary traffic as date-dependent access options with extra road walking or advance booking before 16:00 the weekday before travel where required.
waterSources: Official water points are the natural spring about 1 km west of Myrgryten and the spring-fed tap at Mellan-Malmen. Sörmlandsleden does not test or guarantee availability/quality, and hiker reports have found dry/no-flow conditions in this area, so treat/filter and carry enough backup.

The Mellan-Malmen tap is the best-triangulated refill: official coordinate, OSM spring close by, Vardagstur 2022 use, and a 2025 official-page comment reporting fresh usable water. Older Ledsyn/Staffan Sandberg reports still mean it should not be treated as guaranteed.

A May 2025 through-hiker report in the neighbouring 23-27 chain mentioned frog-contaminated and effectively dry spring experiences after the Myrgryten area, without precisely pinning them to Mellan-Malmen. Use it as a carry-extra-water warning rather than as proof that the official Mellan-Malmen tap was dry.
Lake water from Ljusgryten, Myrgryten and Mellan-Malmen is natural/untested; use only with treatment and do not treat bathing access as potable water.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official/Naturkartan distance is 9 km. OSM relation 3925355 is the matching stage relation but has a stale/rounded 10 km distance tag; OSM relation geometry is about 8.7 km and local generated geometry about 8.5 km. Use official 9 km as canonical.

Draw Stage 25 as the continuous Lundsjön-Vallmotorp stage. Local geometry chains exactly from Stage 24 and to Stage 26; OSM relation 3925355 currently orders members Vallmotorp-Lundsjön, so reverse it if importing directly. Keep the official Vigors kyrka 3 km round loop/side route separate, even where it shares geometry, and keep Stage 24 and Stage 26 as their own connected stages.

Route character: relatively easy to easy-moderate forest/lake stage, with roots/rocks, some elevation, occasional clear-cut/rocky forest reports, and limited flat rest spots between facilities. Highlights include the Vigors kyrka boulders, Ljusgryten fishing lake, Myrgryten shelter/lake, Gölstugruvorna mine remains/open-air church, and Mellan-Malmen rest/bathing.

Official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Recent 2025 comments describe the stage as maintained, not crowded, dog-friendly, easy, pleasant, well kept and with good Mellan-Malmen water, but one 2025 comment said the Myrgryten toilet needed emptying.

Use only existing fireplaces and check current Katrineholm/VSR/Södermanland fire rules before lighting anything. VSR reported no formal fire ban during the 2026-04-27 pass but dry/high-fire-risk conditions, so avoid fires in nature where possible. Shelters do not guarantee firewood or rubbish service.

No stage-specific nature-reserve camping restriction was found. Use normal allemansrätten low-impact tenting principles, avoid private plots around Mellan-Malmen, and prefer durable ground near established rest/overnight areas.
Warm-season user comments mention possible algae/slippery gubbslem conditions at Myrgryten; treat as a bathing comfort/irritation caveat, not a formal closure.

facilities.description: Approximate wider mine-hazard context: old water-filled shafts/spoil heaps can be deep, slippery or fenced. Stay on marked paths and do not climb into shafts.

sections.name: Stage 26: Vallmotorp to Knorranvägen
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 26, Vallmotorp to Knorranvägen.
utilities: Official area: Katrineholms kommun.

Stage 26 is an easy semi-urban connector rather than a wilderness stage: a short paved-road start from Vallmotorp, forest and old track to Häggsjön shelter, then road/cycleway and Lövåsen/Katrineholm service edge before Knorranvägen.

Häggsjön is the main on-stage facility cluster. Official text lists shelter, toilet and jetty/brygga; OSM and shelter sources strongly confirm the shelter/fireplace, while toilet/jetty condition should still be checked on arrival. Treat the jetty as lake access, not an official bathing site.

Lövåsen is the practical resupply strip near the route, with grocery, restaurants, fuel/shop and bus access. ICA Maxi, Willys, MatPiraten/Coop context and restaurants/cafes are nearby; toilets should be treated as customer/business-dependent rather than standalone public toilets. Katrineholm station/centrum is the stronger transit/service fallback via town/connector options.

Public transport is much better near Lövåsen/Laggarhult/Katrineholm than at Vallmotorp. Vallmotorp-area rural service may require prebooking/complementary traffic; verify with Sörmlandstrafiken for the actual date.
waterSources: No official potable spring or tap is listed on stage 26. Carry water from the start or refill at Lövåsen/Katrineholm services.
Häggsjön is lake water only. Sörmlandsleden does not test or guarantee water quality, and lake water should be boiled/filtered/treated if used.
Do not confuse the reliable stage-25 Mellan-Malmen water point with stage 26; once south of Vallmotorp, the stage has no listed trail water source.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official/Naturkartan distance is 8.5 km. OSM relation 3925356 is tagged 8.5 km and measures about 8.46 km; Naturkartan prose sometimes rounds to about 9 km and Äventyrligare is around 8.36 km. Use official 8.5 km as canonical.

Draw Stage 26 as one continuous Vallmotorp-Knorranvägen route. The OSM relation is topologically complete but raw member order starts mid-route and can create large jumps; sort by connectivity and reverse for Vallmotorp-to-Knorranvägen display if importing directly. Keep Katrineholmsetappen, Stage 27:1, Ramsjöhultsslingan and facility-access paths separate from the main line.

Official difficulty is easy, with mixed forest, old track/forest road, asphalt road and cycleway sections, shopping-area edge, and a final short forest path to Knorranvägen. Expect a town-edge/transport-stage feel: practical reports describe a 600 m to 1.5 km road start from Vallmotorp, forest/old road, about 1.5 km near busy väg 55/57, and several kilometres of asphalted pedestrian/cycleway.
Official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass.

Fishing at Häggsjön is explicitly not allowed. Treat the jetty as rest/lake-access context rather than a monitored or official bathing place; a hiker report mentions a rough bathing ladder, but this is user-reported and own-risk.

Use only prepared fireplaces and check current Katrineholm/VSR/MSB fire-risk information before lighting anything. Länsstyrelsen/Katrineholm showed no formal fire ban during the 2026-04-27 pass, but current road/fire-risk services should still be checked on departure day. Shelters do not guarantee firewood or rubbish bins.
No designated tent site was verified on this stage. Shelter use is first-come, shared and non-bookable; tenting should follow ordinary low-impact allemansrätten away from homes and sensitive ground.

Current access caveat: Trafikverket/Katrineholm roadworks on väg 55 between Katrineholm and Valla started 2026-04-13 and are planned through week 26, 2026. Eastbound road closure and major bus reroutes run 2026-04-13 to 2026-05-04; after that, expect traffic control, possible later detours and bus impacts. The walking/cycle path was reported unaffected, but bus access should be checked live.

sections.name: Stage 27: Knorranvägen to Strångsjövägen
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 27, Knorranvägen to Strångsjövägen.
utilities: Official area: Katrineholms kommun.

Stage 27 is an official 15.5 km Knorranvägen-Strångsjövägen stage. It is mostly easy forest/track walking with road crossings, Skirtorpssjön reserve landscape, Forssjö bruk context and some wetter/working-forest sections.
Skogen, also tied to Ramsjöhultslingan, is the main overnight/rest node with shelter, fireplace, dry toilet shortly after the shelter and nearby spring.

Forssjö/Bruksholmen is the main service area: restaurant/event food, unmanned 24Food/shop context and water refill are reported by the stage maintainer, but Bruksholmen low-season opening is event-calendar dependent and day-of access should be checked.

Access is practical by car at Knorranvägen, road 52/Forssjö area and Strångsjövägen. Public transport exists nearby, but not as clean point-to-point transit; verify named stops such as Glysas grav, Rökstorp, Forssjö bruk and Spökbacken with Sörmlandstrafiken live planning.
waterSources: Official springs are listed near Skogen and at Skirtorpsmossen/Mo Källa. Treat/filter/boil both: Sörmlandsleden does not test or guarantee quality or flow.

The Skirtorpsmossen/Mo Källa source is better triangulated by OSM drinking-water data near the official coordinate, but a late-summer hiker report described it as barely dripping. The Skogen spring is official but less independently mapped. Carry backup.
Bruksholmen/Forssjö is a reported refill/service option when open or accessible, but it is maintainer-reported and business-dependent; it should not replace carrying enough water for the full stage.
Do not add the OSM-only drinking-water point near/after Strångsjövägen as reliable until independently confirmed.

Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official/Naturkartan distance is 15.5 km. OSM relation 3925149 is tagged 16 km and summed geometry is about 15.37 km, while local generated geometry is about 15.1 km and AllTrails about 15.3 km; use official 15.5 km as canonical.

Draw Stage 27 as the continuous Knorranvägen-Strångsjövägen mainline, including the shared Ramsjöhultsslingan segment to Skogen. Keep Stage 27:1/Stora Djulö connector, Katrineholmsetappen, Ramsjöhultsslingan loop beyond the shared segment, Rundslinga Forssjö/Stage 28:1, Ceres bicycle overlaps and facility/service spurs separate.

Official difficulty is lättgången/easy, but the stage is long enough to feel moderate for a day hike. Expect forest paths, gravel/road sections, working forest, reserve terrain, and older/mid-aged user reports of muddy, rutted or wet passages after rain.

Official page showed no current formal fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Official comments reported the road-55/56 underpass water-filled in 2024 and April 2025; planks were reported installed on 2025-05-27. Keep it as a possible wet-footing risk, not a current confirmed closure.

A 2025-05-30 official comment reported many wasp nests starting at Skogen shelter, but the latest research pass did not find independent corroboration. Treat as seasonal/inspect-on-arrival rather than a standing defect.

Skirtorpssjön reserve rules verified online include not damaging esker formations by extracting stone, gravel, sand or soil. Länsstyrelsen also warns bark-beetle-damaged spruces may fall. Do not invent additional reserve-specific camping/fire bans; posted signs and general fire restrictions still apply.
Suitable tent places are officially named at Skirtorp and Trollholmen/Forssjö. Present them as trail-maintainer-suitable spots, not serviced campsites.

No bin or waste facility was verified on Stage 27 itself; carry out waste. VSR/Katrineholm showed no formal fire ban during the 2026-04-27 pass, but VSR and Länsstyrelsen/SMHI signalled dry/high fire-risk conditions, so use only prepared fireplaces where present and prefer skipping open fire unless day-of conditions clearly allow it.

sections.name: Stage 27:1: Stora Djulö to Etapp 27
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 27:1, Stora Djulö to Etapp 27.
utilities: Official area: Katrineholms kommun.
Short access connector from Stora Djulö toward stage 27, useful mainly for Katrineholm/Stora Djulö access rather than as a wilderness hike.

Current Sörmlandsleden text says the connector joins stage 27 at/near the road 52 and 55/56 roundabout area; Glysas grav is a nearby heritage POI and older endpoint reference, not the canonical current endpoint.

Stora Djulö/Djulöbadet is the strong service cluster: parking, STF hostel, manor/cafe, museum/recreation area, paid camping, beach, toilets and seasonal/customer-dependent food. Many food/museum services are summer-season or opening-hours dependent.
Public transport should be checked live with Sörmlandstrafiken. Useful nearby stop contexts include Djulöbadet, Svartbäcksvägen, Djulö kvarn and Glysas grav, but route numbers differ between sources.
Katrineholm Central is the main rail access point for the connector; it is useful trip context but sits well away from both route endpoints, so use bus, bike, taxi or a road walk from town.
waterSources: No reliable public drinking-water point is listed on stage 27:1 itself. Carry water from Katrineholm/Stora Djulö or use customer/service refills at STF, Stora Djulö cafe or Djulö Camping when available.
Djulösjön lake water is natural/untested and should be treated if used. Stage 27 springs are beyond the connector and should not be presented as 27:1 water points.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 4 km; Naturkartan and the 2025 Sörmlandsleden long-distance passport list 4.5 km, AllTrails reports 2.5 mi, OSM relation 9632259 is tagged 4 km but can measure about 4.3 km depending on members, and the local official-GPX-derived line is about 3.8 km.

Route character: easy access/transport walk through Stora Djulö recreation area, hostel/manor/museum context, Djulö allé, asphalt/residential edge, Gatstuberg/Skogskapellet, a hilltop shelter/bench viewpoint over Djulösjön, then road/forest connector toward the stage-27 road 52/55-56 join. Team Vildmark's November report described long asphalt and road-parallel stretches with traffic noise rather than a destination wilderness feel.

Older Naturkartan, OSM/Pacer-style listings and some blogs still say Glysas grav; use the current official page for endpoint wording. Old reports around the road-52 crossing mention confusing signs/fencing near the former Glysas grav alignment, so follow current orange waymarks rather than stale map text.

Geometry caveat: Naturkartan site 5083 line starts near 58.972249, 16.208894 and ends near 58.970988, 16.263086, while OSM relation 9632259 shares the current Stage 27 join node near 58.970568, 16.264670. Naturkartan's 27:1 line stops roughly 100 m short of the Stage 27 line and OSM has a small component gap near the Skogskapellet/forest turn; treat both as source-geometry caveats, not intentional route gaps.
Official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass.
The hilltop shelter/benches are confirmed by official/community sources, but no reliable exact coordinate was found. Treat the pin as approximate and do not assume overnight-shelter quality.

No marked free tent site was verified on this connector. Katrineholm local rules put camping inside Djulö fritidsområde at the formal camping site only; do not present the Stora Djulö/Djulöbadet public recreation cluster as free tenting.

Use prepared fire/grill places only where present, and check current Katrineholm/VSR fire risk before lighting anything. At the 2026-04-27 check VSR had no formal Katrineholm/Vingåker ban but still warned of high fire risk; the Djulö grill place has no verified woodshed or wood supply.

Djulöbadet/Naturkartan and Katrineholm local rules restrict smoking and dogs at ordinary municipal bathing places; use the designated dog bathing area and current signs. Katrineholm also requires dogs on public places to be leashed, and national 1 March-20 August wildlife rules still apply.

Djulösjön fishing normally requires a fishing permit except for specific simple pole-fishing allowances in local material. Verify current permits locally before fishing or relying on Djulö Camping/card-sales information.
No verified Stage 27:1 bin/waste point was found during the 2026-04-27 pass. Carry out waste unless a staffed service explicitly accepts it.

sections.name: Stage 28: Strångsjövägen to Viggaren
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 28, Strångsjövägen to Viggaren.
utilities: Official area: Katrineholms kommun.
Stage 28 is an official 10 km Strångsjövägen-Viggaren stage through easy forest paths/roads, moraine ground, eskers, Hönstorpasjön, Sundstugan/Solbacken context and Glindranåsen reserve.
Parking is very limited: official text says 2-3 cars at both ends and a few cars mid-stage near the Sundstugan/gravel-road crossing. Treat these as small pull-offs rather than formal lots.
Hönstorpasjön area is the main on-stage rest/facility area: first the lake-view rest section, then roughly 1 km later the bathing/shelter/grill/toilet cluster.
Solbackens småbruk near Sundstugan can be useful for seasonal self-pick/cafe context and occasional water/fika when open, but it is private/seasonal and should not be treated as guaranteed.

Public transport is weak at the trailheads. Use Sörmlandstrafiken live planning and expect road walk, taxi, bike, car, or book-ahead rural/complementary traffic rather than a simple bus-to-trailhead hike. Strångsjö and Glindran stops are wider-area access contexts, not close trailhead stops.
waterSources: The current official stage water point is the Glindraåsen spring/source at about 7.5 km. It is also mapped in OSM, but Sörmlandsleden does not test or guarantee quality/flow; filter/boil/treat and carry backup.

Older/third-party and OSM sources list an early drinking-water point near Strångsjövägen. A 2022 hiker report describes a cold concrete well with a wooden lid and clear but slightly brown water after awkward clearcut/brush access, but the current official stage page lists only Glindraåsen; show it only as unverified/seasonal legacy context.

Hönstorpasjön and Viggaren are natural lake water only. Treat surface water and do not present lake access as potable refill. Hönstorpasjön water has been described as brown/humic and poor-tasting even after filtering.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 10 km; local official-GPX geometry is about 9.6 km, Naturkartan metadata is about 9.8 km, OSM relation 3924910 geometry is about 9.8 km, while older/Naturkartan prose/OSM relation distance tag/Grillplatser can show about 11.5 km. Use 10 km official and treat 11.5 km as stale or loop-derived metadata.

Official difficulty is lättgången/easy. Expect managed forest, forest roads, some uneven/stony or vehicle-rutted patches, lake views, pasture/juniper landscape and a gravel-road finish along Viggaren. Team Vildmark's 2020 report described it as pleasant but not very wild, with fine torp sites, Storsjön/Hönstorpasjön views and nice ending terrain near Glindranåsen/Viggaren.

Official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass; Länsstyrelsen Glindranåsen showed no current reserve news but did display a current Södermanland forest-fire-risk notice. VSR had no formal Katrineholm/Vingåker fire ban at check time but warned of high/large fire risk, so use fixed fireplaces only after day-of checks.

Glindranåsen/Glindraåsen naming varies by source. Reserve rules found online are minimal but include not extracting gravel/stone/sand/soil from the esker; protected-area signs and fire bans override general guidance. The current online reserve rule set did not list a separate camping ban, so apply allemansrätten unless local signs say otherwise.

No designated tent site is listed for stage 28. Use the Hönstorpasjön shelter as the practical overnight/rest point, or low-impact one-night tenting only where appropriate under allemansrätten and local signs.

User reports since 2015 mention uneven/stony first kilometers, cycle ruts, planted forest, clearcuts and forestry debris; Forssjö-loop comments overlapping/shared with Stage 28 mention heavy forestry impact in 2023/2025 and high vegetation in 2024. Treat these as trail-character/seasonal-maintenance cautions, not current official closures.

Related Forssjö loop comments mention a 2025 deteriorated/overgrown rest spot at Viggaren/Gustav Höglunds stuga. Treat as local caution, not an official stage-28 closure; do not rely on maintained seating there.

Do not merge or draw the Forssjö loop/OSM relation 8309519 into Stage 28. OSM shows it sharing only a few Stage 28 ways and official text says the loop is partly on Stage 28; treat overlap as coincident route membership, not a Stage 28 branch.

OSM relation 3924910 is topologically continuous with Stage 27 at about 58.928796, 16.267331 and Stage 29 at about 58.876279, 16.351303. Snap drawn route continuity to shared OSM nodes while keeping official Sörmlandsleden endpoint labels.

No official railway crossing was found for Stage 28. Road hazards are ordinary live-road/gravel-road sections, especially the road-following segment near Viggaren, the Sundstugan gravel-road access and the Strångsjövägen endpoint.
In early spring, dead grass can dry quickly before new growth. Check SMHI/MSB Brandrisk Ute and local fire bans before using grills or stoves.

Do not assume free fishing in Hönstorpasjön or Viggaren. Hönstorpasjön appears in Ericsberg's listed fishing waters; Viggaren permit status was not verified, so confirm fishing-right holder/permit rules locally before fishing.

facilities.description: Related Forssjö-loop comments in 2025 reported the Gustav Höglunds stuga/Viggaren rest spot as deteriorated or overgrown. Scenic context, but do not rely on maintained seating; this is a caution rather than a closure.

facilities.name: Strångsjö village services
facilities.description: Off-route Strångsjö village service cluster at Strångsjövägen 1: Nobless Grillen, 24food shop, ATM, DinX fuel/customer parking per Nobless site. Restaurant says Tue-Sun 11-20, Monday closed. About 3.9 km from the Stage 28 line; do not present as trailhead service.

facilities.name: Strångsjö wider bus access
facilities.description: Wider-area Strångsjö bus context around line 483, roughly 5 km by road from the Stage 28 start. Not a close trailhead stop; verify Sörmlandstrafiken live and expect weekday/sparse service.

facilities.name: Glindran wider bus access
facilities.description: Wider-area Glindran bus context around line 484, roughly 4 km from the Viggaren end. Very sparse service; verify Sörmlandstrafiken live before relying on it.

facilities.name: No verified Stage 28 bins
facilities.description: No waste bin was verified at Strångsjövägen, Hönstorpasjön, Sundstugan/Solbacken, Glindraåsen, Glindranåsen or Viggaren. Carry out all waste.

sections.name: Stage 29: Viggaren to Djupviksvägen
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 29, Viggaren to Djupviksvägen.
utilities: Official area: Katrineholms kommun.

Official distance is 9.5 km from Viggaren to Djupviksvägen. Naturkartan also lists 9.5 km but its prose says about 9 km, OSM relation 3114035 is tagged 9 km and measures about 9.4 km, the local official-GPX-derived line is about 9.1 km, and Äventyrligare reports about 9.24 km; keep 9.5 km as canonical.

Expect a moderate mixed forest/lake stage with old infields, Mossängen old-forest context, Hjulbo/Hålvetten bathing opportunity, climbs after Hjulbo, a viewpoint before Näsnaren, then Näsnaren/Fagerön facilities.

Näsnaren shelter has the key trail overnight cluster: shelter, fireplace, dry toilet, nearby official source, bathing/rest context, and suitable tenting. Reports suggest hammock use is easier than tenting and there may only be room for about one tent.

Fagerön is the best service node near the end: municipal bathing place, shelter/Arknat context, toilets, grill/fireplace, benches/tables, bins, jetty, and nearby parking. It is still a day-use public beach setting, not a serviced campsite.

Nearby off-route services include Fridhem Outdoor near Hjulbo/Näsnaren/Fagerön, listed by Sörmlandsleden with lodging/food/sauna/canoe by arrangement, and Djupviks kursgård context near the next-stage access. Verify bookings/current operation before relying on either.

Public transport is weak. OSM and regional maps show Fagerön, Djupviksnäs, Djupvik, Källvik vägskäl and Nytorp contexts, and bus 483/Djupvik-Katrineholm or Strångsjö-Djupvik material, but service is sparse; check Sörmlandstrafiken live before planning a transit-only hike.
waterSources: Two official natural water points are mapped: the mid-stage source at 58.852317, 16.331217 and the Näsnaren source at 58.838150, 16.327650. Both should be treated/filtered/boiled; Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee availability or quality.

Fagerön and Näsnaren lake water are bathing/natural water contexts, not potable taps. Fagerön bathing samples in 2025 were tjänligt with no algal bloom, and the 2026-season classification is excellent; this is bathing-water context, not drinking-water approval.

Näsnaren has a PFAS/PFOS fish-consumption warning from Katrineholm/Länsstyrelsen; official advice is not to eat fish from the lake. Treat this as a fish-consumption warning, not a published bathing closure, but do not rely on Näsnaren lake water as casual drinking water. Ordinary boiling/filtering for microbes should not be presented as PFAS treatment.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official page showed no current fault reports for stage 29 during the 2026-04-27 research pass. The stage-30 bark-beetle/windfall warning starts beyond this stage and matters only if continuing south.

Official suitable tent spots are Fagerön and by the Näsnaren shelter. Katrineholm's local public-order rules classify Fagerön bathing place as public place and restrict camping on public places, so do not present the municipal beach/lawn as a tent site; use posted signs and only low-impact allemansrätt ground clearly outside restricted public bathing-place areas.

Use established fireplaces only and check current fire restrictions/brandrisk before lighting. Sörmlandsleden says shelter fireplaces do not guarantee firewood, Fagerön has no verified firewood supply, and VSR had no formal Katrineholm/Vingåker ban at check time but advised against outdoor fires/grilling in nature because it was dry/high risk.

Fagerön is a Katrineholm municipal bathing place; smoking and dogs are prohibited at ordinary municipal bathing areas according to Naturkartan/Katrineholm guidance, and dogs must be leashed on public places.

Sörmlandsleden says a site-specific Arknat shelter opened near Fagerön on 2025-07-09. The separate Arknat/Hefna website coordinate appears far from Fagerön/Näsnaren and should not be used for navigation; use Sörmlandsleden/map signage and treat it as bridge/Fagerön context.
There is no parking exactly where stage 29 becomes stage 30. Use the bridge/Fagerön parking context or other signed/roadside options without blocking access.

Older 2020 hiker notes about fallen trees between Fagerön and Näsnaren, attributed to wind and beaver activity, and 2015 notes about beaver/wet brush near Näsnaren are useful route texture, but not current condition reports. No strong current Stage 29 mud-hole or waymarking-confusion report was found.

Do not add OSM relation water-source/viewpoint spur members, Fagerön parking, Fridhem, Djupviks kursgård, or the Hålvetten lake-centroid as route-builder geometry. Draw the continuous Viggaren-Djupviksvägen mainline and keep services/water as separate markers.

Topology caveat: Naturkartan's Stage 29 line ends about 50 m east of the OSM/official Stage 30 continuity point. For stitching to Stage 30, snap to the official/OSM shared Djupviksvägen node around 58.824786, 16.342178.

facilities.name: Viggaren stage start
facilities.description: Official stage start by Lake Viggaren and junction with stage 28. Parking is limited/roadside context rather than a large formal trailhead.

facilities.name: Stage 29 mid-stage spring
facilities.description: Official natural source after about 4 km, matched by OSM spring/drinking-water data near 58.852320, 16.331230. Treat/filter/boil and verify flow before relying on it.

facilities.name: Glindran-Strångsjö road crossing
facilities.description: Road crossing/short road-section context near the mid-stage spring and possible parking. Use caution around pickup/dropoff and do not block the road.

facilities.name: Hjulbo / Hålvetten swim-rest context
facilities.description: Hjulbo / Hålvetten bathing/rest opportunity mentioned by Sörmlandsleden. Pin is moved to route-adjacent Hjulbo/Hålvetten context rather than the lake-centre point; no toilet/shelter was verified and this is not a drinking-water point.

facilities.name: Näsnaren spring/source
facilities.description: Official natural source west/northwest of the Näsnaren shelter; OSM spring/drinking-water data matches nearby at about 58.838182, 16.327674. Treat/filter/boil and expect seasonal variation.

facilities.name: Näsnaren viewpoint/rest detour
facilities.description: Viewpoint/rest context before descending toward Näsnaren, matching Sörmlandsleden route text and OSM viewpoint/bench context.

facilities.name: Näsnaren shelter
facilities.description: Official shelter by Näsnaren; Naturkartan/OSM align closely. Main rest/overnight node on the stage. Older access notes mention rough/private/gated road complications by car, so approach it as a trail shelter rather than a drive-up facility.

facilities.name: Näsnaren shelter fireplace
facilities.description: Mapped fireplace/firepit at or near the shelter. Use only when current fire restrictions allow; do not assume firewood.

facilities.name: Näsnaren dry toilet
facilities.description: Pit toilet behind/at the Näsnaren shelter area. OSM maps the toilet separately from the shelter; verify condition on arrival.

facilities.name: Näsnaren suitable tent area
facilities.description: Officially suitable tenting by the shelter. Reports suggest space may be tight, possibly about one tent, while hammock trees are easier; use low-impact one-night camping and keep shoreline/toilet hygiene careful.

facilities.name: No bin at Näsnaren shelter
facilities.description: OSM marks no bin at the Näsnaren shelter and Sörmlandsleden generally expects hikers to carry out waste from shelters.

facilities.name: Fagerön-Näsnaren windfall caveat
facilities.description: Older hiker reports describe many fallen trees between Fagerön and Näsnaren, attributed to wind and beaver activity. Official page currently has no fault report, so treat as a historically recurring-prone spot rather than a confirmed current blockage.

facilities.name: Fagerön municipal bathing place
facilities.description: Municipal natural bathing place with jetty, benches/tables, grill/fireplace, shelter, toilet and bins. 2025 samples were tjänligt with no algal bloom and classification for the 2026 bathing season is excellent; this is not a potable-water claim.

facilities.name: Fagerön shelter and Arknat context
facilities.description: Fagerön has shelter context from Naturkartan/municipal data, and Sörmlandsleden separately reports a new Arknat shelter/rastplats near the bridge/parking from 2025-07-09. Use local signage/Sörmlandsleden maps rather than the inconsistent third-party Arknat coordinate.

facilities.name: Fagerön grill/fireplace
facilities.description: Municipal grill/fireplace. Naturkartan notes no wood shed; check current fire rules and bring fuel only if allowed.

facilities.name: Fagerön bathing-place toilet
facilities.description: Mapped toilet at the Fagerön bathing/service area. Naturkartan confirms toilet category, but availability may be seasonal or condition-dependent.

facilities.name: Fagerön bridge-side toilet
facilities.description: Second mapped toilet near the bridge/parking side of Fagerön. Verify seasonal opening and condition.

facilities.name: Fagerön bridge-side waste basket
facilities.description: Mapped waste basket at the Fagerön bridge/parking side. Pack out waste if bins are full, removed or seasonal service is absent.

facilities.name: Fagerön tenting caveat
facilities.description: Sörmlandsleden lists suitable tenting at Fagerön, but Katrineholm local rules restrict camping/tenting on public places and Fagerön bathing place is municipal public space. Do not tent on the maintained beach/lawn; follow signs and use only appropriate ground clearly outside restricted public-place areas.

facilities.name: Fagerön bathing-place rules
facilities.description: Katrineholm/Naturkartan rules prohibit smoking and dogs at ordinary municipal bathing places, and dogs must be leashed on public places. Follow current signs.

facilities.name: Fagerön bridge parking
facilities.description: Practical parking near the bridge/Fagerön service area. Naturkartan/Stage 30 describe parking about 600-800 m from the bathing/stage-transition area; check local signs and avoid blocking access.

facilities.name: Fagerön bus-stop context
facilities.description: OSM maps a Fagerön Sörmlandstrafiken stop near the Djupviksvägen/route-end area; service appears sparse and Naturkartan found no convenient nearby stops. Check Sörmlandstrafiken live.

facilities.name: Fagerön opposite bus context
facilities.description: Opposite-side Fagerön stop context near the stage end. Verify current line 483/related service before relying on it.

facilities.name: Djupviksnäs bus context
facilities.description: Nearby west-side Sörmlandstrafiken access context. Service is sparse; verify live departures and walking route.

facilities.name: Djupvik bus context
facilities.description: Farther west / complementary-access Sörmlandstrafiken context. Treat as off-route access planning only.

facilities.name: Nytorp bus context for Viggaren
facilities.description: Nearest mapped bus context for the Viggaren start, roughly 1.7 km straight-line with longer walking likely. Verify live Sörmlandstrafiken service before relying on it.

facilities.name: Fridhem Outdoor off-route services
facilities.description: Sörmlandsleden lists Fridhem Outdoor AB near Hjulbo/Näsnaren/Fagerön, about 1-1.5 km off trail, with 5 rooms/12 beds, food by arrangement, wood-fired sauna and canoe/rowing-boat rental. Verify by SMS/phone/booking before relying; pin is approximate/off-route.

facilities.name: Stage 29 OSM spur caveat
facilities.description: OSM relation 3114035 includes short dangling spur members to a water point and a viewpoint/rest point. Keep these as markers/spurs, not part of the through route line.

facilities.name: Djupviksvägen stage transition
facilities.description: Official Stage 30 start and OSM shared Stage 29/30 node align here within a few metres. Naturkartan's Stage 29 line stops slightly east; use this point for route stitching. Official guidance says there is no parking exactly where stage 29 becomes stage 30.

facilities.name: Djupviks kursgård service context
facilities.description: Sörmlandsleden still lists Djupviks kursgård as nearby stage-29/30 lodging/service context about 700 m by shortcut or 1.5 km from the stage board, but business-register pages suggest historical/inactive uncertainty. Keep only as verify-before-use/book-by-phone context, not dependable open service.

facilities.name: Näsnaren PFAS fish warning
facilities.description: Katrineholm/Länsstyrelsen advise not eating fish from Näsnaren after PFAS/PFOS findings. Treat as a fish-consumption warning, not a published bathing closure; avoid relying on Näsnaren lake water as casual drinking water, and do not imply ordinary boiling/filtering removes PFAS.

facilities.name: Näsnaren fishing permit context
facilities.description: Fishing in Näsnaren requires a fishing card/rights-holder permission; Jönåkers Häradsallmänning lists fishing-card context and Djupvik boat places. This does not override the PFAS fish-consumption warning.

sections.name: Stage 30: Djupviksvägen to Åbo
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 30, Djupviksvägen to Åbo.
utilities: Official area: Katrineholms kommun, Nyköpings kommun.

Official distance is 11 km from Djupviksvägen to Åbo; the local official-GPX route is about 10.5 km, Äventyrligare reports 10.74 km, OSM relation 3117090 sums to about 11.1 km including short spurs but is tagged 13 km, and Naturkartan prose/older imports can still say about 13 km. Use 11 km official and treat 13 km as stale metadata.

The stage has a remote, self-sufficient character with no settlements on-route: Djupviksberget/Stenstorps hagkärr reserve context, Rudgölen/Övre Ålsjön rest/swim/tent context, Vikitteln, Vikittelns minikanjon, Vensbrinksberget/Skogsbyås tower, rolling/hilly forest terrain and the Åbo transition.

Vikitteln is the only main shelter/rest cluster on stage 30. It has shelter, several fire/grill places, simple bathing/jetty context and a dry-toilet context supported by Skogsbyslingan/OSM rather than the stage-30 icon list.

Parking is better south of Fagerön bridge, at Djupvik/Stenstorps hagkärr, Skogsbyås/Skogsbyslingan, or cautiously at Åbo than exactly at the stage boundary. The stage 29/30 transition itself is not a guaranteed trailhead parking place.

Public transport is weak. Djupvik/Fagerön bus context may help near the north end when running, Skogsbyås has no regular bus connection, and Åbo mainly has pre-booked complementary traffic or onward access by continuing to Stavsjö.
waterSources: The source about 1 km northwest of Åbo at 58.781283, 16.359550 is official but explicitly marked uncertain quality; filter/boil/treat.
The Åbo cold spring at 58.775700, 16.366800 is official and near the stage end/stage 31 start. Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or flow, so treat/filter/boil.
Lake water at Rudgölen, Övre Ålsjön and Vikitteln is natural/bathing water only, not a potable refill.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official stage warning remains published: bark-beetle/windfall risk between Skogsby/Skogsbyslingan parking and Vikitteln shelter, with trees over/near the trail and trees that may fall easily. Avoid this area during or shortly after strong wind.
Stenstorps hagkärr reserve forbids camping and fires; dogs must be leashed and plants may not be picked except berries/edible mushrooms.

Djupviksberget protects living/dead standing or fallen trees, shrubs, plants, fungi and lichens, with limited own-use berries, edible mushrooms and flowers allowed. Organized camps/competitions may require Länsstyrelsen permission.

Skogsbyås does not list a general individual tent/fire ban online, but protects living/dead trees, shrubs, plants, fungi and lichens and requires permission for organized camp activity/competitions. At Skogsbyås/Vikitteln, bring your own legal fuel/wood if fire is allowed; dead or living wood may not be taken and fire bans/brandrisk override prepared fireplaces.

A few tents can fit at Rudgölen/Övre Ålsjön according to official text. Vardagstur's 2022 report describes a small point/islet rest spot with fire ring, a couple of flat tent spots and hammock trees but no wood box. Treat as an informal low-impact tent/rest option, not a maintained campsite; no shelter, toilet, bin or official fire facility is guaranteed there.
Vikitteln shelter is free/first-come and cannot be booked. Reports mention useful grill/cooking tools, but do not assume tools/pans, trash bins, supplied firewood or empty shelter space.

User reports add practical cautions: meltwater was reported in February 2024 but passable, Åbo-side clearcuts/bark-beetle terrain can make path/waymark finding harder, and Vensbrinksberget/Skogsbyås has rocky exposed footing where poles may help.

Åboravinen on the continuation into stage 31 has a separate stronger reroute/windfall warning; it is beyond stage 30 but important for through-hikers and should not be treated as a Stage 30 on-route hazard.

Do not import Skogsbyslingan, parking connectors, water-source stubs, Åbo spring micro-spurs, the Skogsbyslingan parking stub or the Rudgölen/Övre Ålsjön access stub into the Stage 30 main route. Draw the continuous Djupviksvägen-Åbo line only.

OSM relation 3117090 connects cleanly to Stage 29 near 58.824786, 16.342178 and Stage 31 near 58.776228, 16.365952, but contains several non-mainline stubs. Snap the through-line to those shared nodes for continuity while keeping official labels and water/service markers separate.
AllTrails and some translated services may render Åbo as Turku; this is Åbo near Stavsjö in Sörmland, not Åbo/Turku in Finland.

facilities.name: Djupviksvägen stage start
facilities.description: Official stage start. Do not assume parking exactly at the stage 29/30 transition; use nearby signed/roadside options such as Fagerön bridge or Djupvik/Stenstorps hagkärr.

facilities.name: Fagerön bridge parking for stage 30
facilities.description: Practical parking south of the Fagerön bridge, about 800 m back along stage 29 from the stage 30 start. Check signs and avoid blocking access.

facilities.name: Djupvik / Stenstorps hagkärr parking
facilities.description: Alternative reserve parking about 1.5 km west/northwest of the stage start; Länsstyrelsen reports about five cars and bus access to Djupvik. Useful for Djupviksberget/Stenstorps hagkärr access, not exactly the trailhead.

facilities.name: Fagerön / Djupvik bus context
facilities.description: OSM maps paired Fagerön stops at the stage-start road and a confirmed Djupvik stop near the reserve parking; Länsstyrelsen confirms bus access from Katrineholm to Djupvik. Treat as limited and verify live Sörmlandstrafiken service.

facilities.name: Fagerön bridge access services
facilities.description: Off-stage/access cluster near the Stage 30 parking/backtrack approach: OSM maps toilet and waste basket nearby, with beach/rest/firepit context farther north on Fagerön. Do not treat as a core Stage 30 facility.

facilities.name: Djupviksberget reserve warning
facilities.description: Reserve/Natura 2000 highlight with limestone conifer forest, orchids and rare flora/fungi. Do not damage living/dead standing or fallen trees/shrubs, or collect/damage plants, fungi or lichens except limited own-use berries, edible mushrooms and flowers; organized camps/competitions may require permission.

facilities.name: Stenstorps hagkärr rules
facilities.description: Reserve context on/near the early stage: no camping, no fires, dogs leashed, and no plant picking except berries/edible mushrooms.

facilities.name: Rudgölen rest/swim context
facilities.description: Rudgölen lake/rest/swim context from official Stage 30 text. Natural lake water only, not a potable source; no verified shelter, toilet or bin.

facilities.name: Övre Ålsjön tent/rest context
facilities.description: Official text says Rudgölen/Övre Ålsjön have rest/swim opportunities and room for a few tents. A 2022 hiker report describes a small rest point with fire ring, a couple of flat tent spots and hammock trees, but no wood box. Treat as informal low-impact tenting, not a maintained campsite; check exact reserve boundary and avoid Stenstorps hagkärr.

facilities.name: Övre Ålsjön swim/rest context
facilities.description: Informal lake swim/rest context confirmed by official text and trip reports. Not a municipal bathing place or drinking-water point.

facilities.name: Övre Ålsjön firepit
facilities.description: OSM-mapped firepit near Övre Ålsjön. Not listed as an official Stage 30 fireplace; use only if current fire rules allow, and do not assume firewood.

facilities.name: Vikitteln shelter
facilities.description: Vikitteln shelter/rest cluster. Official stage text places the shelter after about 6.5 km and gives a coordinate slightly east; OSM names the actual shelter node slightly west at this pin. Free/first-come shelter; no booking, guaranteed firewood, tools/pans or trash service.

facilities.name: Vikitteln fireplace/grill
facilities.description: Prepared fire/grill cluster by Vikitteln; Skogsbyslingan text says several grill places. Bring your own firewood if fire is allowed; Skogsbyås reserve forbids taking dead or living wood, and fire bans override use.

facilities.name: Vikitteln dry toilet
facilities.description: Dry toilet by the Vikitteln shelter cluster, supported by Skogsbyslingan toilet icon and OSM/local context rather than the Stage 30 icon row. A 2024 wasp-nest comment was later reported removed; verify condition on arrival.

facilities.name: Vikitteln toilet wasp note resolved
facilities.description: Official comments reported bees/wasps at the toilet on 2024-08-10/11; the stage manager replied on 2024-09-13 that the nest was removed on 2024-09-12 and the toilet was usable again. Keep as historical inspect-on-arrival context only.

facilities.name: No verified Vikitteln bin
facilities.description: No bin was verified at Vikitteln or elsewhere on the Stage 30 core route. Pack out all waste; do not borrow Fagerön beach bins into the on-stage shelter model.

facilities.name: Vikitteln bathing/rest
facilities.description: Simple lake bathing/rest by the shelter area. Not a municipal sampled beach or potable-water source.

facilities.name: Vikittelns minikanjon
facilities.description: Geological mini-canyon/cave area roughly 500 m after Vikitteln and near Skogsbyslingan. Approximate OSM/Mapcarta-aligned pin.

facilities.name: Skogsbyås windfall warning
facilities.description: Official warning area between Skogsby/Skogsbyslingan parking and Vikitteln shelter: bark-beetle-damaged spruce, trees over/near the trail, and trees that may fall easily. Länsstyrelsen also notes bark-beetle attacks in Stenstorps hagkärr, Djupviksberget and Skogsbyås. Avoid during or shortly after strong wind.

facilities.name: Vensbrinksberget / Skogsbyås tower
facilities.description: Södermanland's highest point, 123 m above sea level, with a 12 m observation tower. Strongly confirmed by Sörmlandsleden, Länsstyrelsen and OSM; tower can feel exposed in wind.

facilities.name: Skogsbyås / Skogsbyslingan parking
facilities.description: Reserve/loop parking for Skogsbyslingan, Vikitteln, minikanjon and Vensbrinksberget. Länsstyrelsen says there is no bus connection and easiest access is by car/gravel road from Stavsjö/E4.

facilities.name: Skogsbyås viewpoint after parking
facilities.description: Official stage text mentions a fine viewpoint about 900 m after Skogsby tower parking; OSM has a viewpoint node in this direction. Optional viewpoint marker, not a facility.

facilities.name: Åbo-side clearcut wayfinding caveat
facilities.description: A 2022 hiker report described Åbo-side clearcut/bark-beetle terrain where both path and markers sometimes needed searching. Use offline map/GPS and current orange markings.

facilities.name: Stage 30 meltwater caveat
facilities.description: Official 2024 comments reported much meltwater on trail/stream but passable despite trees over the path. Treat as seasonal wet-footing context, not a current closure.

facilities.name: Stage 30 OSM stub caveat
facilities.description: OSM relation 3117090 contains non-mainline stubs for Åbo spring/water, Skogsbyslingan parking, Rudgölen/Övre Ålsjön and the Åbo approach source. Keep these as markers/spurs, not part of the continuous route line.

facilities.name: Spring 1 km northwest of Åbo
facilities.description: Spring about 1 km northwest of Åbo. Official coordinate is 58.781283, 16.359550 and explicitly says uncertain quality; OSM spring node is about 20 m away at this app pin. Treat/filter/boil and carry backup.

facilities.name: Åbo stage transition/info board
facilities.description: Practical stage-end/stage-31-start context near the OSM information board. Official stage 31 start coordinates align nearby.

facilities.name: Åbo cold spring
facilities.description: Åbo cold spring near the stage 30/31 transition. Official coordinate is 58.775700, 16.366800; OSM spring node is about 20 m away at this app pin. Natural untreated source; verify flow and treat/filter/boil.

facilities.name: Åbo parking context
facilities.description: Official stage text says parking exists at Åbo, but capacity/formality is unclear. Länsstyrelsen Åboravinen says parking is along the road where the trail crosses and larger parking is planned. Treat as roadside/local parking and check signs.

facilities.name: Åbo complementary transit context
facilities.description: No reliable turn-up-and-go transit found at Åbo. Sörmlandstrafiken complementary traffic lists the Skogsby, Fridhem, Åbo, Kråkviken, Lövdalen and Stavsjö area; book by 16:00 the weekday before via Sörmlandstrafiken.

facilities.name: Djupviks kursgård off-route lodging
facilities.description: Official Sörmlandsleden lodging listing still includes Djupviks kursgård for Etapp 29/30, about 700 m by shortcut or 1.5 km from the stage board. Verify before relying; do not infer public all-hours toilet, tap, bin or food service.

facilities.name: Åboravinen continuation warning
facilities.description: Beyond stage 30 on the stage-31 continuation: official/Länsstyrelsen warning and reroute context for bark-beetle/windfall risk. Important for through-hikers continuing south.

sections.name: Stage 31: Åbo to Stavsjö
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 31, Åbo to Stavsjö.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Stavsjö.

Official distance is 11 km from Åbo to Stavsjö. Secondary/OSM-derived sources often show about 9.5-9.6 km because they appear to stop near Stavsjö trafikplats rather than continuing to the old inn/stage-32 start area; use the official 11 km endpoint.

Naturkartan's current route object for Stage 31 is a single 332-vertex MultiLineString from about 58.776197, 16.365988 to 58.724559, 16.417115 and reports 10576 m. OSM relation 3693024 shares the Åbo node with Stage 30 but stops around Stavsjö Klint/E4, so do not use OSM alone for the drawn official finish.

The stage is partly demanding: old forest near Åbo, Åboravinen, high bedrock and steep hills, Uvberget/Uvbergsgrottorna, Björnsjön shelter/beach, Asptorp pump and croft, charcoal-burning remains, E4/Stavsjö Klint services, then the final Stavsjön/old inn approach.

Stavsjö is the practical service and transit end, with Stavsjö Krog & Kafé, Circle K/service shop, customer toilets/water context during opening hours, parking, bus 563/564 context, and lodging around the old inn/Herrgårdsflygel/Kolmården Apartments area. Treat water/toilets as customer/opening-hour dependent.

Åbo access is much weaker: roadside parking where the trail crosses the road, planned larger parking noted by Länsstyrelsen, and at most pre-booked complementary transport context rather than normal hiker-friendly transit.

Björnsjön is the main rest/overnight node with shelter, fireplace, toilet and swim/beach context. Recent reports still support it as a good rest/camp stop, but mention wind exposure, bring-your-own toilet paper, uncertain small-stream water, and earlier litter/overgrowth, so treat it as a rustic lakeside node rather than a maintained bathing place.
waterSources: Åbo spring at 58.775700, 16.366800 is official and matched by OSM nearby. It is a natural source; Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee availability or quality, so treat/filter/boil.

Asptorp pump at 58.745583, 16.377633 is an official pump about 100 m east of the trail/croft and closely matched by OSM. Existence is well supported, but day-of function and quality are not guaranteed.

Do not assume potable water at Björnsjön shelter itself. Björnsjön/Stavsjön lake water is natural water only and should be treated if used; user reports specifically warn that nearby tiny streams can be muddy or unreliable.

Stavsjö Krog/Circle K may provide customer water/toilets during opening hours, but this is not a public trail water facility. Circle K also lists air/water service for vehicles; do not treat that as guaranteed hiker drinking water.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Current official warning dated 2024-12-17: Åboravinen is rerouted/avoidance-advised until further notice due bark-beetle-killed spruce and falling-tree risk. Follow the marked/snitslad road detour/red-dot map route and treat older GPX tracks through the ravine as potentially stale; a 2025 hiker report also found parts of the ravine impassable.

Draw the permanent official line, but show a temporary Åboravinen detour/closure overlay. The detour appears to leave near Åbo, follow road via the Sägartorp/Kalvik side, and rejoin near Kalvik/Uvberget; exact temporary geometry should be field/digitization checked.

Åboravinen reserve rules include not damaging living/dead trees or shrubs, not collecting plants/moss/lichens/fungi except berries/edible mushrooms/flowers for personal use, no off-road motor vehicles, and no organized camps/competitions without permission. No blanket one-night small-tent ban was found, but reserve signs and sensitive ground override general assumptions.
The official Uvberget route has harder/easier alternatives. The main Uvberget view is reported limited by regrowth, while a blue-marked spur after the alternatives rejoin gives a better wide view.
Björnsjön shelter is free/first-come and cannot be booked; shelters must be shared if space remains. No bins or firewood should be assumed, and user reports say to bring toilet paper.
No verified public trail bin exists at Åbo, Björnsjön, Asptorp, Halsbråten or Uvberget. Pack out trail waste; settlement waste/recycling in Stavsjö is off-route context only.
Use only prepared fireplaces and check Brandrisk Ute/SMHI/municipal fire bans. Never light fires on bare rock.
The E4/Stavsjö Klint area and the temporary Åboravinen road detour are road/interchange contexts, not quiet forest trail; keep children/dogs close and expect traffic.
Informal small-scale tenting may be possible at Björnsjön under allemansrätten where appropriate, but it is not an official campsite and reserve signs/fire rules override general guidance.
AllTrails and some translated services may render Åbo as Turku; this is Åbo near Stavsjö in Sörmland, not Åbo/Turku in Finland.

sections.name: Stage 31:1: Halsbråten, etapp 31 to Skjutgropen, etapp 32
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 31:1, Halsbråten, etapp 31 to Skjutgropen, etapp 32.
utilities: Official area: Norrköpings kommun, Nyköpings kommun, Stavsjö.
Official distance is 8.5 km from Halsbråten/stage 31 to Skjutgropen/stage 32; Naturkartan gives 8613 m and the OSM relation geometry is about 8.6 km, while the OSM tag itself rounds to 8 km.

Naturkartan site 73447 draws a 222-point line of about 8.59 km from near Halsbråten to near Stage 32; topologically stitched OSM relation 9631248 is about 8.60 km from the exact Stage 31 shared node to the exact Stage 32 shared node.
This is a connector/extraslinga, not part of the main linear Sörmlandsleden route. Keep the main sequence as Stage 31 to Stavsjö to Stage 32, and expose 31:1 as an optional branch/loop component.

Character is forest paths and minor roads with some wet/marsh sections, E4 noise/underpass context, Gullvagnen lake, Götas grav/Koleragrav, Jättegryta, Långa Längan, Krokeks ödekyrka/Vårfruklostret, Hagsätter spring and Tranmossen.
There is no confirmed official shelter or toilet on 31:1 itself. Nearby shelter/toilet options belong to adjacent stages: Björnsjön on stage 31 and Lövsjön on stage 32.

Practical access and services are best handled via Stavsjö rather than the branch endpoints; Stavsjö has bus, parking, food/service and lodging contexts from adjacent stages, while Krokeks ödekyrka and the Gullvagnen/E4 area offer local parking context only.

The Krokeks ödekyrka/Långa Längan/Götas grav area is in Norrköpings kommun/Östergötland, while the northern Stavsjö-Halsbråten side is tied to Nyköping/Södermanland. Fire, dog and public-place rules can therefore differ along the connector.
waterSources: Hagsätter spring after Krokeks ödekyrka at 58.707017, 16.379233 is the only official water source on 31:1; OSM maps a spring within a few meters.
Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee source flow or water quality and does not test water. Treat/filter/boil the spring water and carry backup.

Gullvagnen is a small natural bathing lake/swim opportunity, not a potable water source or monitored municipal bathing place. For monitored bathing-water context nearby, use off-route Stavsjöbadet rather than Gullvagnen.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official 31:1 page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. The adjacent stage-31 Åboravinen reroute/windfall warning matters only when approaching via stage 31 or walking Stavsjörundan.

The Skjutgropen name is slightly ambiguous: the practical 31:1/stage-32 junction is around 58.710121, 16.418001, while the OSM named locality Skjutgropen is east of the route around 58.709696, 16.426384. Do not snap the route endpoint to the locality marker.
The branch crosses/overlaps local Östgötaleden context. OSM currently shares Stage 31:1 ways with Östgötaleden relations; treat that as overlap metadata, not new Sörmlandsleden geometry.

Do not duplicate Stavsjörundan over Stage 31:1: the loop reuses existing Stage 31, Stage 31:1 and Stage 32 pieces. Skiren runt belongs to Stage 32/Skiren and should not be followed as Stage 31:1 continuation.
Långa Längan is a rest/fireplace/heritage point. Historical/local text mentions overnight use, but it is not verified as current bookable lodging or an official shelter.

Use Långa Längan's established fireplace only when current fire bans/brandrisk allow. Check both Norrköping/Östergötland and Nyköping/Södermanland channels where relevant; during tightened fire bans even fixed fireplaces can be closed.

Krokeks ödekyrka/Vårfruklostret is protected cultural heritage and cemetery context. Stay on paths, do not climb on ruins or walls, do not move stones, dig, build fire rings, metal-detect, disturb graves, or pitch tents on ruin/cemetery ground.
No official tent site is listed on 31:1. Use allemansrätten carefully, avoid cultural remains and sensitive/grazed land around Krokeks ödekyrka/Långa Längan, and follow any local signs.
Dogs need extra supervision from March 1 to August 20 and are safest leashed near cultural sites, roads, bathing places, cemetery ground and possible grazing land.

Community reports broadly support good route character and clear marking, but mention vegetation-obscured or messy sections and wet low terrain around mosses. Keep an offline map and stay on boardwalk/plank crossings around Tranmossen.
Stavsjörundan text warns that motorway-adjacent gravel-road sections may need future relocation because of Ostlänken; keep GPX/official maps fresh.

facilities.description: Motorway-adjacent underpass/road section. Expect traffic noise and keep to the signed route; official Stavsjörundan text notes this corridor may be affected by future Ostlänken relocation pressure.

facilities.name: Långa Längan / former guesthouse
facilities.description: Restored remnant of Krokeks gästgivargård. Heritage/local text mentions past overnight use, but this is not verified as current lodging, an official shelter, or a bookable hut.

facilities.name: Långa Längan fireplace/rest area
facilities.description: Official/rest-area fireplace, with OSM picnic/fireplace data and Stavsjörundan noting fireplace under roof. Use only when current fire rules allow; during tightened fire bans even fixed fireplaces may be closed.

facilities.name: Krokeks ödekyrka / Vårfruklostret
facilities.description: Church/monastery ruin and cemetery cultural site, also linked to Klosterleden. Protected heritage/cemetery context: stay on paths, do not climb on ruins/walls, move stones, dig, build fire rings, metal-detect, disturb graves or camp on the ruin/cemetery ground.

facilities.name: Krokeks ödekyrka parking
facilities.description: Parking near the ruin is mapped in OSM and mentioned by local/loop sources. Useful mid-route access, but check local signs and do not block access.

facilities.description: Nearby bus-stop context west of Götas grav/Koleragrav, mapped in OSM/Sörmlandstrafiken cache. Useful for bailouts/access, but check live line 564/other service before relying on it.

facilities.description: Wetland/marsh area passed toward Skjutgropen; blogs/loop notes mention boardwalk/spång and wet terrain, with older reports calling the boardwalk solid and newer mixed reports mentioning messy/overgrown sections. Stay on marked route/boards and expect wet footing.

sections.name: Stage 32: Stavsjö to Lövsjöns sydspets
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 32, Stavsjö to Lövsjöns sydspets.
utilities: Official area: Norrköpings kommun, Nyköpings kommun, Stavsjö.

Official distance is 11.5 km from Stavsjö to Lövsjöns sydspets; secondary GPS/map sources range about 10.3-12.0 km. Use official 11.5 km as the headline and treat drawn/OSM geometry as planning support.

Use the official/Naturkartan Stage 32 line as the main route, reversed into the named Stavsjö-to-Lövsjön direction. Naturkartan site 73422 measures about 10.3 km/10315 m while the catalog distance is 11.5 km; OSM relation 3692978 measures about 11.9 km but has small disconnected chains near Stavsjö.

Easy to moderate forest stage: Skiren shore and early swim/rest options, mixed forest and clearcut, connection with 31:1 at Skjutgropen after about 4 km, the old Nunnebanan rail embankment, long mire/boardwalk sections, then Lövsjön's west and south shore.
Stavsjö is the practical northern service point with bus 563 context, parking, food/service at Stavsjö Krog/Circle K, and nearby lodging whose current booking status should be verified.

Lövsjön shelter is the main overnight/rest node with shelter, fireplace/grill, dry toilet and lake access. Östgötaleden describes floor space for about 4-5 people; no booking, bins, firewood or toilet paper should be assumed.

Kolmårdens djurpark connects to the south end via stage 32:2, a blue-marked gravel-road connector. This is often the stronger transit/parking access at the southern end than trying to rely on the small Lövsjön endpoint parking.
waterSources: Lugnet spring at 58.712000, 16.403383 is the only official water source for stage 32 and is about 600 m off the main trail after roughly 5 km. Treat/filter/boil and carry backup.
Do not merge the official Lugnet spring with unrelated OSM spring pins near the route; the official source is an off-route detour and no recent independent flow report was found.
Skiren and Lövsjön are natural lake/bathing water only, not potable refills. Official text describes Skiren as clear/fine bathing water, but that is not drinking-water proof.
Do not mark the Lövsjön shelter as a potable water point just because secondary facility imports list water/shoreline. Official drinking-water listing is Lugnet.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.
Official stage 32 page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass.

Current-condition caveat: route-specific reports through March 2025 still describe the long bog boardwalk as present and passable, though slippery in snow/slush and with an older rotting bench beside a newer one. Separate reports about rotten boardwalks/repairs in the wider Hjortronmossen/Lövsjöstigen area should be treated as condition warnings, not an official Stage 32 closure unless confirmed.
Nearby-loop caveat: Länsstyrelsen says Lövsjöstigen in Fjällmossen is closed during 2026 due fallen trees and poor boardwalks. This is a nearby loop, not confirmed as a stage 32 closure.

Southern Lövsjön/Fjällmossen context has reserve/Natura 2000 rules: no tenting/camping or caravans, dogs leashed, no off-road driving/parking, do not damage living/dead trees or shrubs, and fires only where signs/rules permit. Apply the strictest posted rule locally.
Hjortronmossen/Nävsjömossen reserve context includes leashed pets, no collecting mosses/lichens/wood fungi, no disturbing wildlife, and fires only at arranged grill sites.

Kokärrets gammelskog is nearby/side-access context rather than a main-stage facility. If entering the reserve, pets must be leashed and fires, camping, plant/wood removal and wildlife disturbance are restricted; the reserve has no visitor facilities.
Erikslund/Nunnebanan reserve context near the route has strict fire/camping restrictions and only tiny parking context by the old railway; do not present it as a service stop.
Sörmlandsleden shelters are free, first-come, non-bookable and must be shared if space remains. No bins or firewood should be assumed.

Use prepared fireplaces only when current fire bans/brandrisk allow. During stricter fire bans even fixed public grill sites can be prohibited; check Krisinformation/MSB Brandrisk Ute and current municipal/county pages.

Fishing in Skiren/Stavsjön and parts of Lövsjön requires a local permit. Source links conflict slightly between Sörmlandsleden/iFiske and Nyköping/Naturkartan/Stavsjö Krog references, so users should verify the correct water before buying.
Skiren and Lövsjön swim spots are informal lake access only. No matching authority bathing-water listing was verified for these Stage 32 spots; avoid claiming sampled bathing quality.

Recent non-official reports describe clear signage, including at the 31:1 junction and blue-marked 32:2 connector, but wet/slippery footing can occur around the bog boardwalk and Lövsjön. Multiple nearby alternatives mean users should watch signs for Skiren runt, 31:1, 32:2 and Kokärret side paths.

Endpoint geometry varies by source around Lövsjöns south tip and the 32:2 junction. Stage 33's official start near 58.680200, 16.477983 and OSM's common junction near 58.679192, 16.477323 are close enough for planning but should be treated cautiously for precise navigation.
