facilities.description: Official text describes several early swim/rest opportunities along Skiren and very clear water. No municipal bathing-water sample point was verified here; fishing requires permit.

facilities.name: Skiren south benches/rest
facilities.description: Benches/picnic stop by Skiren, confirmed by recent hiker report and OSM picnic-table data. Good early break point but exposed in poor weather.

facilities.name: Skiren / Lövsjön fishing permit warning
facilities.description: Fishing in Skiren/Stavsjön and parts of Lövsjön requires a local permit; fishing is not covered by allemansrätten. Sörmlandsleden/iFiske and Nyköping/Naturkartan/Stavsjö Krog sources are not perfectly aligned, so verify the exact water before buying.

facilities.name: Lugnet spring
facilities.description: Official water source about 600 m off the main trail after roughly 5 km; stage maintainer recommends the detour. Treat/filter/boil and verify flow.

facilities.name: Skjutgropen / stage 31:1 junction
facilities.description: Stage 32 meets connector 31:1 after about 4 km from Stavsjö. Use this route junction, not the named Skjutgropen locality east of the trail.

facilities.name: Nunnebanan rail embankment
facilities.description: Historic rail-bank section after the 31:1 junction, built after nun moth damage in the early 1900s. Cultural/route-character marker rather than a facility.

facilities.name: Kokärrets gammelskog side context
facilities.description: Nearby/side-access reserve around Nöden/Kokärret, not a main-stage service stop. Länsstyrelsen notes no trails, parking or visitor facilities; pets leashed, no fire, no camping, no damaging/removing vegetation/wood/fungi/moss/lichen, and avoid disturbing wildlife.

facilities.name: Erikslund / Nunnebanan reserve context
facilities.description: Reserve/old-railway context near Nunnebanan. Länsstyrelsen mentions only tiny parking by Nunnebanan and reserve rules prohibit fire and camping; do not present as a trail service.

facilities.name: Hjortronmossen boardwalk condition
facilities.description: Long wetland/boardwalk area. Route-specific reports through March 2025 still found the boardwalk usable, though slippery in snow/slush; wider 2025-2026 reports about rotten boardwalks/repairs should be treated as a condition warning unless an official Stage 32 closure appears.

facilities.name: Bog boardwalk bench/rest
facilities.description: Long bog boardwalk with a bench/fika spot from OSM and recent blogs. 2025 reports note a new/stable bench and an older rotting bench beside it; footing can be slippery in snow/slush and waterlogged near the boards.

facilities.name: Lövsjön shelter
facilities.description: Official shelter on Lövsjön's west shore after about 9.5 km; Naturkartan/OSM/Vindskyddskartan align closely. Östgötaleden describes floor space for about 4-5 people. Free, first-come, non-bookable and shared when space remains.

facilities.name: Lövsjön shelter fireplace
facilities.description: Prepared fire/grill context at the shelter. Use only when current fire rules allow; no firewood guarantee and no trash bins.

facilities.name: Lövsjön dry toilet
facilities.description: Dry toilet beside/near the Lövsjön shelter, confirmed by official text, Östgötaleden and OSM. Bring paper/sanitizer and verify condition on arrival.

facilities.name: Lövsjön facility-cluster alternate pin
facilities.description: Secondary Grillplatser/Nyköping imported shelter/fire/toilet/swim coordinate is offset about 100-150 m from the official shelter. Treat as same facility cluster, not a separate shelter.

facilities.name: Lövsjön swim/rest shore
facilities.description: Lake-shore rest/swim context near the shelter and along the southbound continuation. Natural lake water only, not potable.

facilities.name: Lövsjön south informal tent/rest caveat
facilities.description: Recent reports and forum notes say flatter lake-view rest/tent spots may exist a few hundred metres south of the shelter, while the shelter area itself is stony/sloping. This is not an official campsite; Fjällmossen no-camping rules, local signs and sensitive ground override allemansrätten.

facilities.name: Lövsjön southern fire/rest point
facilities.description: Mapped picnic/fireplace point south of the shelter near the route continuation. Reserve/fire rules apply.

facilities.name: Fjällmossen reserve rules near Lövsjön
facilities.description: Southern Lövsjön/Fjällmossen context: no tenting/camping, dogs leashed, fires only at designated places, and do not damage living/dead trees. Follow posted signs.

facilities.name: Lövsjöstigen nearby-loop closure
facilities.description: Länsstyrelsen says nearby Lövsjöstigen is closed during 2026 because of fallen trees and poor boardwalks. This is not confirmed as a stage 32 closure.

facilities.name: Lövsjöns sydspets stage end
facilities.description: Official stage-33 start coordinate and best shared endpoint for stage 32. Official text says small parking and rest/swim possible; exact parking pin varies by source.

facilities.name: Lövsjön common route junction
facilities.description: OSM common endpoint for stage 32, stage 33 and connector 32:2; useful for topology but coordinate differs slightly from official stage-33 start.

facilities.name: Lövsjön/Fjällmossen parking east
facilities.description: Länsstyrelsen/OSM parking context east of Lövsjön from the Kolmården/Fjällmossen direction. Not the same as the small stage-end parking.

facilities.name: Kolmården connector 32:2 access
facilities.description: Official start of the blue-marked 1.5 km connector from Kolmårdens djurpark to Lövsjöns sydspets. Strong transit/parking access via Kolmårdens Djurpark stop, but park/hotel services are seasonal/opening-hour dependent and bus tickets may cross operators/zones.

facilities.name: Kolmårdens djurpark parking
facilities.description: Paid visitor parking/EV charging context for accessing 32:2 and southern stage 32. Check current Kolmården parking fees and opening context.

sections.name: Stage 32:2: Kolmårdens djurpark to Lövsjöns sydspets, etapp 32
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 32:2, Kolmårdens djurpark to Lövsjöns sydspets, etapp 32.
utilities: Official area: Norrköpings kommun.

Kolmårdens djurpark gives strong bus/parking access to this blue-marked connector, but zoo/park services are seasonal, ticketed or customer-dependent. Treat toilets, food and water there as available only when open and accessible.

This is easy gravel-road access on Fjällmossevägen/Dammkärrsvägen rather than a standalone forest-trail stage. OSM labels the relation orange, but the official Sörmlandsleden page says the connector is blue-marked; user reports in 2019, 2020 and 2025 agree it is simple gravel-road access.
No toilet, shelter, tap, campsite, shop, power or waste facility was verified on connector 32:2 itself. Nearby useful facilities are on adjacent stage 32, around Lövsjön, or at Kolmården.
waterSources: No verified drinking-water source on the 1.5 km connector. Use Kolmården services only when open/accessed, or carry water.
Nearby water sources are not on 32:2: Lövsjön is surface water only, Ålkärrsdrogen is on stage 33 about 3 km from Lövsjön, and Lugnet spring is far away on stage 32. Treat/filter natural water.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official connector is 1.5 km from Kolmårdens djurpark to Lövsjöns sydspets, blue-marked and mostly/effectively gravel-road walking on Fjällmossevägen/Dammkärrsvägen. Naturkartan/OSM geometry measures closer to about 1.84 km and AllTrails about 1.8 km; use official 1.5 km as canonical.

Official Sörmlandsleden page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Nearby Lövsjöstigen in Fjällmossen is temporarily closed in 2026 because of fallen trees and poor boardwalks; this is a nearby loop warning, not a confirmed 32:2 closure.

Fjällmossen/Lövsjön reserve context near the north end: no tenting/camping or caravans, dogs leashed, fires only at designated places, no damaging trees/dead wood, and motor vehicles/parking only where permitted.

Kolmården parking is paid and operationally separate from trail access: main parking was listed as 149 SEK/day or 40 SEK/started hour, night parking can be expensive, and Apans parking may be gated after zoo closing. Vildmarkshotellet parking/entrance is for hotel/Safari Camp guests with permit.

Use Östgötatrafiken line 420 as the primary current bus context for Kolmårdens Djurpark; line 902 is limited school-day rural traffic. Older blog references to bus 433 should be treated as stale unless a live planner shows it.
Trips that combine Kolmården and Stavsjö may cross Östgötatrafiken/Sörmlandstrafiken boundaries; use Resrobot or both operators' planners and do not assume one ticket covers everything.
Topology: keep 32:2 as a separate access spur. The shared route junction is OSM/Naturkartan node context near 58.679192, 16.477323; do not continue the main Sörmlandsleden south-west to Kolmården.

facilities.name: Kolmården 32:2 stage board
facilities.description: Official start by Kolmårdens djurpark parking/stage board. Blue-marked connector begins here and follows Fjällmossevägen toward Lövsjön; Naturkartan's geometry start is offset slightly west around 58.667247, 16.462047.

facilities.name: Kolmårdens Djurpark bus stop
facilities.description: Closest bus access near the connector start. Use Östgötatrafiken line 420 as primary current access; line 902 is limited school-day rural traffic. Verify live departures and cross-operator tickets.

facilities.name: Gruvstugan backup bus stop
facilities.description: Backup bus-stop context west of the official trailhead, also on line 420. Useful if live routing suggests it, but it is not the named official access point.

facilities.name: Kolmården station transfer context
facilities.description: Kolmården station is not walk-close to 32:2; use bus transfer or live planner. Kolmården and Östgötatrafiken describe bus links from station/Norrköping to the zoo entrance.

facilities.name: Kolmården main parking
facilities.description: Large paid zoo parking near the connector start. Current checks found 149 SEK/day or 40 SEK/started hour, APCOA-listed night parking at 400 SEK 21:00-05:00, 24 EV charging points, and ANPR/payment rules; verify current terms.

facilities.name: Apans parking gate caveat
facilities.description: Kolmården FAQ says Apans parking closes 60 minutes after park closing. Do not rely on zoo parking for late-return or overnight trail logistics without checking current rules.

facilities.name: Kolmården visitor services
facilities.description: Toilets, kiosk/shop/food, lockers, guest services and similar visitor facilities are nearby but depend on park opening, ticket/access or customer status. Do not treat as guaranteed public trail facilities.

facilities.name: Kolmården entrance toilets
facilities.description: OSM-mapped toilet near the Kolmården visitor/entrance area. Access may depend on park/entrance operations, so do not treat as a reliable early/late trail toilet.

facilities.name: Tropicarium paid-service context
facilities.description: Nearby Tropicarium/zoo-area service context with separate admission/opening rules. Useful landmark, not a guaranteed free trail toilet or food stop.

facilities.name: Kolmården EV charging
facilities.description: EV chargers in the zoo parking area. Parking/payment rules likely apply; verify current operator terms.

facilities.name: Vildmarkshotellet services context
facilities.description: Hotel/restaurant/lodging context near Kolmården, about 1-1.2 km from the connector start. Verify access, booking and opening; hotel parking is not general trail parking.

facilities.name: Fjällmossevägen / Dammkärrsvägen connector
facilities.description: Short easy blue-marked gravel-road connector; useful access rather than a standalone hiking objective. No facilities documented along the road.

facilities.name: Lövsjöns sydspets junction
facilities.description: Shared OSM/Naturkartan route junction with stages 32, 32:2 and 33. Official Stage 33 start/parking coordinate is about 100-120 m away; use this for topology and local signs for exact parking.

facilities.name: Lövsjön south-end fire/rest point
facilities.description: Mapped picnic/fireplace near the north end of the connector. Use only where reserve rules and current fire-risk/fire-ban status allow.

facilities.name: Lövsjön south-end bathing/rest
facilities.description: Lövsjön south/southeast shore rest and bathing context. Surface water only, not a verified drinking-water refill.

facilities.name: Lövsjön shelter/toilet nearby
facilities.description: Adjacent stage-32 shelter/toilet about 0.8-1.5 km north of the connector junction, useful if continuing on stage 32. Not on 32:2 itself.

facilities.name: Lövsjön dry toilet nearby
facilities.description: Dry toilet by the adjacent stage-32 Lövsjön shelter cluster. Not on connector 32:2 itself.

facilities.name: Fjällmossen/Lövsjön reserve rules
facilities.description: Reserve context near Lövsjön: no tenting/camping/caravans, dogs leashed, fires only at designated places, do not damage living/dead trees, and park/drive only where allowed. Same-day fire bans override fireplaces.

facilities.name: Lövsjöstigen nearby-loop closure
facilities.description: Nearby Fjällmossen loop warning: Länsstyrelsen says Lövsjöstigen is closed during 2026 due to fallen trees and poor boardwalk condition. This is not confirmed as a 32:2 closure.

sections.name: Stage 33: Lövsjöns sydspets to Brytsebo
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 33, Lövsjöns sydspets to Brytsebo.
utilities: Official area: Norrköpings kommun.

Parking exists at Lövsjöns sydspets and at Brytsebo/Skvättan; Länsstyrelsen lists about 7 spaces at the reserve entrance. Transit is most practical via Kolmårdens djurpark plus connector 32:2, or sparse school-day line 902 near Marielundsvägen for the Brytsebo side; check Östgötatrafiken live before relying on it.

No shop, tap, power, or endpoint toilet was verified directly on stage 33. Nearby services are seasonal/conditional at Kolmården/Vildmarkshotellet and Kvarsebo via connector 33:1; do not treat zoo/hotel/cafe facilities as guaranteed public trail services.
waterSources: Ålkärrsdrogen is the only confirmed named trail water source on stage 33. Sörmlandsleden calls it good spring water, and OSM maps the same spring, but the association's general water guidance says sources are not quality-tested or guaranteed; treat/filter and carry backup.
Do not use Bråviken as drinking water; it is a Baltic inlet. Lövsjön/lake water and the Skyttholmens brygga shelter area are not verified drinking-water refill points.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official stage is 8 km in Norrköpings kommun/Östergötland. Naturkartan's embedded/API geometry measures about 7.7 km and is stored reversed from Brytsebo to Lövsjön, while OSM relation 3690246 is a clean single component around 8.0 km; use 8 km as the catalog/planning distance.

The first 700 m are gravel road, then mixed forest; the final Bråviken section is one of Sörmlandsleden's most demanding with steep descent/ascent, viewpoints, bathing, old pine forest, and a signed shortcut around the steepest section.

Official Sörmlandsleden pages showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Bråvikenbranten had no authority-posted reserve news item at check time, but that is not a guarantee of trail condition; fire risk/fire-ban status is time-sensitive and must be checked same day.

In Bråvikenbranten reserve: tenting is allowed max two consecutive nights in the same place, dogs/pets must be leashed, fires only at Länsstyrelsen-signposted grill places, no damaging living/dead trees or rock/ground, no collecting mosses/lichens/non-edible fungi, and climbing requires permit.

The Bråviken/Skyttholmens brygga shelter cluster is reached by an approximately 600 m side trip near the end. It is first-come/shared and has shelter, fireplace/grill, benches, picnic/rest function, firewood context, dry toilet, and no verified potable water; Bråviken is brackish inlet water.

Keep core stage 33 distinct from connector 33:1: Rövargrottan, Högudden, blue side paths to bathing cliffs/jättegrytor and the Kvarsebo/Säter ferry are mainly 33:1 or side-route material, not the direct Lövsjön-to-Brytsebo stage.
Östgötaleden relation 6124617 overlaps all OSM Stage 33 way members. Treat Östgötaleden as a named overlay/label stack, not duplicate physical route geometry.

Connector 33:1 links Brytsebo with Kvarsebo/Säter ferry and Östgötaleden. Older official text mentions bus 432, but current checks point to line 902 on school days only; always verify live timetable and ferry status.

facilities.name: Lövsjöns sydspets stage start
facilities.description: Official start and small parking/access point. Also the junction with connector 32:2 from Kolmårdens djurpark; map sources vary by roughly 50-130 m around the south-tip road/parking node.

facilities.name: Ålkärrsdrogen source
facilities.description: Official cold spring about 3 km from Lövsjön; described as good water, but not quality-tested or guaranteed. OSM maps the same spring but not as a serviced drinking-water tap. Treat/filter and carry backup.

facilities.name: Bråvikenbranten reserve rules
facilities.description: Reserve rules near the Bråviken section: dogs leashed, tent max two nights in same place, fires only at signed grill places, no damaging trees/dead wood/rock/ground, no collecting mosses/lichens/non-edible fungi, climbing needs Länsstyrelsen permit. Check current fire risk.

facilities.name: Bråviken steep section / shortcut
facilities.description: Official text calls the Bråviken end one of Sörmlandsleden's most demanding parts; a signed shortcut bypasses the steep descent/ascent and bathing/viewpoint loop. User reports describe this as more climbing/scrambling than ordinary hiking in places.

facilities.name: Skyttholmens brygga / Bråviken shelter
facilities.description: Shelter on an approximately 600 m spur near Bråviken. Sources report about 4 sleeping places, benches, picnic/rest function, fireplace/grill, dry toilet and firewood context. No verified potable water; Bråviken water is brackish.

facilities.name: Skyttholmens brygga fireplace
facilities.description: Prepared fireplace/grill at the shelter spur. Use only if current fire rules allow; Bråvikenbranten permits fires only at signed grill places.

facilities.name: Skyttholmens brygga dry toilet
facilities.description: Dry toilet mapped near the Bråviken shelter cluster; no drinking water, handwashing or paper guarantee. No toilet verified at the stage endpoints.

facilities.name: Skyttholmen lower beach/rest spot
facilities.description: Small Bråviken beach/rest spot below the shelter with mapped fire/rest context. Treat as informal bathing/rest, not a municipal sampled bathing place or drinking-water source.

facilities.name: Bråviken bathing/rest area
facilities.description: Official stage text highlights Bråviken bathing/rest and viewpoints near the steep option; this is sea/inlet water, not a drinking-water refill, and no exact municipal bathing-water sample point was verified.

facilities.name: Rövargrottan side-trip caveat
facilities.description: Cave/side-route context near Stage 33:1/Skvättan, not the core Stage 33 line. Enter at own risk, bring a light, and avoid solo/inexperienced cave visits.

facilities.name: Kopparbogrottan safety caveat
facilities.description: Bråvikenbranten cave context west of the main Stage 33 line. Länsstyrelsen warns of deep cracks, narrow passages and water and does not recommend it for inexperienced visitors; never go alone.

facilities.name: Östgötaleden overlap warning
facilities.description: OSM Östgötaleden relation 6124617 overlaps Stage 33's OSM ways. Show as an overlapping named route, not duplicate geometry or an extra connector.

facilities.name: Skvättan/Bråvikenbranten parking
facilities.description: Reserve parking near Brytsebo/Bråvikenbranten, about 7 spaces with information boards and picnic table. Do not assume roadside overflow parking.

facilities.name: Brytsebo stage end
facilities.description: Official shared end of stage 33/start of stage 34. Use this as the main route-node coordinate; nearby parking is at Brytsebo/Skvättan, but exact parking pins vary by source.

facilities.name: Marielundsvägen bus access
facilities.description: Closest researched bus access for the Brytsebo/Skvättan side. Länsstyrelsen describes school-day Krokek-Kvarsebo service with about 600 m walk; current line 902 timetable is school-day Monday-Friday only in the checked 2025-12-14 to 2026-06-14 PDF. Do not use stale bus 432 references.

facilities.name: Kolmårdens djurpark connector access
facilities.description: Main practical public-transport approach to Lövsjön via blue-marked connector 32:2, about 1.5 km from Kolmårdens djurpark to the stage 33 start.

facilities.name: Kvarsebo/Säter ferry connector context
facilities.description: Connector 33:1 starts at Kvarsebo/Säter ferry and links to Brytsebo/Östgötaleden. Check Trafikverket Skenäsleden status and current bus service; older bus 432 references are likely stale.

facilities.name: Vildmarkshotellet/Kolmården services
facilities.description: Nearby lodging/restaurant/service context for the Kolmården access side, but opening/admission and seasonal access vary. Not directly on stage 33.

facilities.name: Qvarsebo seasonal cafe context
facilities.description: Kvarsebo village/ferry-side seasonal cafe/shop context for connector 33:1 access. More than 2 km from stage 33; verify opening hours.

sections.name: Stage 33:1: Kvarsebo färja to Brytsebo
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 33:1, Kvarsebo färja to Brytsebo.
utilities: Official area: Norrköpings kommun.

Kvarsebo/Säter ferry landing has parking and seasonal cafe context; Brytsebo/Skvättan has reserve parking with about 7 spaces. Public transport is sparse: current checks point to Östgötatrafiken line 902 on schooldays only, while the official stage-page bus 432 note appears stale.

No grocery, reliable drinking-water refill, or guaranteed year-round service was verified directly on the stage. Cafe Säterdalen and Qvarsebo/Kvarsebo village services are seasonal or opening-hour dependent; do not treat them as dependable resupply without a live check.
waterSources: No official potable water source on stage 33:1. Carry water.

Skyttholmens shelter has shelter/fire/toilet context but no verified potable water, and the mapped dry toilet explicitly has no drinking-water tag. Bråviken is brackish sea/inlet water, not a drinking-water source.
The nearest official trail spring is Ålkärrsdrogen on stage 33, not on this access connector and not convenient for a short 33:1 trip.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 4 km. Naturkartan renders about 3.6 km, AllTrails about 3.7 km, and OSM relation 3696342 measures about 3.8 km. If you continue from the 33:1/33 junction to the Stage 33/34 Brytsebo board, add about 0.37 km along Stage 33, giving roughly 4.2 km.

This is an access/connector stage from Kvarsebo/Säter ferry to the Stage 33 junction near Brytsebo, linking Sörmlandsleden with Östgötaleden/Europaled 6. It should not be treated as a mainline continuation or as directly sharing a node with Stage 34.

Short does not mean easy: the route is steep/rocky with several brants, hällmark, major Bråviken views, blue side spurs to bathing cliffs/jättegrytor, Rövargrottan, and a demanding initial climb from the ferry that older trip reports found slightly hard to follow in lush growth. A 2023 user comment described the stage as very nice and well maintained, so keep the route-finding note as seasonal/older evidence rather than a current fault.

Official Sörmlandsleden page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Recent official comments describe the route as very hilly but beautiful; older trip reports mention route-finding/overgrowth near the ferry, not confirmed as a current fault. A nearby 2021 group walk around Kvarsebo/Klint also supports the hands-on steepness with rope/ladder context in the local terrain.

Skenäsleden ferry is free across Bråviken between Skenäs and Säter/Kvarsebo, but time it carefully. Trafikverket says be present at the scheduled Skenäs departure time even from the Säter/Kvarsebo side; if nobody is waiting at either landing, the ferry may not run. Check Trafikverket/Färjerederiet live status.

Bråvikenbranten reserve rules: tenting max two consecutive nights in the same place, dogs leashed, fires only at Länsstyrelsen-signed grill places, no damaging living/dead trees or rock/ground, no collecting mosses/lichens/non-edible fungi, and climbing requires permit. There was no regional fire ban in checked official sources on 2026-04-27, but RTÖG showed a same-day forest-fire incident in Norrköping, so always check live fire risk and emergency status.

Östgötaleden is messy here: official Östgötaleden text says it follows Sörmlandsleden 31:1, 32, 33 and 33:1 to the Säter/Kvarsebo ferry, while OSM relation 6124617 uses Stage 33 plus road/ferry geometry and does not include all Stage 33:1 forest-path ways. For this app, draw the Sörmlandsleden 33:1 forest connector and treat Östgötaleden as an overlapping/variant label rather than duplicate physical trail.

Rövargrottan cave entry is at your own risk; bring a flashlight/headlamp and avoid wet/icy or solo entry, heavy packs, and small children. Nearby Kopparbogrottan is more serious and not recommended for inexperienced visitors.

Literary context: official material references Almqvist and Hans Lidman's I Tintomaras spar for the Kolmården/Bråviken landscape. Treat generated/geographic claims about Kvarsebosjön or Brytsebosjön as unreliable; the route context is Bråviken.

facilities.name: Kvarsebo/Säter ferry landing
facilities.description: Official stage start by the north/Säter side of Trafikverket's Skenäsleden ferry. Parking and seasonal cafe context nearby; check ferry live status before planning around it.

facilities.name: Säter ferry terminal
facilities.description: OSM ferry terminal at the Kvarsebo/Säter side. Hiking sources often call this Kvarsebo färja, while Trafikverket names the route Skenäsleden, Skenäs-Säter.

facilities.name: Skenäsleden ferry
facilities.description: Free road ferry over Bråviken between Skenäs and Säter/Kvarsebo, about 1020 m and roughly 5 minutes. Be present at the scheduled Skenäs departure time even from the Säter side; if nobody waits at either landing, the ferry may not run.

facilities.name: Skenäs-side ferry toilet
facilities.description: OSM-mapped toilet on the south/Skenäs side of the ferry, across Bråviken from the 33:1 trail start. Useful for ferry logistics, but opening/condition is not guaranteed and it is not on the 33:1 trail side.

facilities.name: Kvarsebo ferry parking
facilities.description: Parking at/near the ferry landing; verify local signs and ferry/cafe seasonal traffic.

facilities.name: Cafe Säterdalen
facilities.description: Seasonal cafe by the ferry area; opening hours not reliably verified, so do not rely on it without checking.

facilities.name: Säterholmsvägen bus access
facilities.description: Useful bus access for the start-side/mid-route area. Current checks point to line 902, valid timetable period 2025-12-14 to 2026-06-14, schooldays only and no weekend service in the PDF; verify live departures.

facilities.name: Kvarsebo affär bus access
facilities.description: Kvarsebo village bus access, but about 2 km from the route/start area. Current line 902 service is sparse/schooldays; older bus 432 text appears stale and should not be used without live-planner confirmation.

facilities.name: Qvarsebo Kaffe seasonal context
facilities.description: Roastery/cafe/local-shop context in Kvarsebo village, more than 2 km from much of the route and with variable seasonal opening. Useful context, not dependable route resupply without checking.

facilities.name: Högudden / Bråviken viewpoint
facilities.description: High scenic viewpoint area over Bråviken; official text highlights the brants and broad views.

facilities.name: Högudden cape
facilities.description: Named cape/locality below the main Högudden viewpoint. Use the viewpoint marker for the main bench/view stop.

facilities.name: Jättegrytor side trail
facilities.description: Blue-marked side trail to giant-kettle geology near Högudden; slippery/exposed rock possible. Exact side-spur line should be treated as approximate.

facilities.name: Bråvikenbranten cliff bathing spot
facilities.description: Small cliff-bathing side spot along the Bråvikenbranten stretch, reported by local outdoor guide sources. Access is steep/advanced and this is not a serviced beach or drinking-water point.

facilities.name: Rövargrottan cave

facilities.name: Kopparbogrottan safety caveat

facilities.description: Small shelter/rest point near Bråviken, about 4 sleeping places. Sources report benches, fireplace/grill, dry toilet nearby, picnic/rest function and firewood context, but current condition and firewood availability are not guaranteed.

facilities.description: Dry/bucket toilet near the shelter; mapped as no drinking water, with no handwashing or paper guarantees.

facilities.name: Skyttholmens brygga fireplace

facilities.description: Second mapped lower beach/firepit/rest context below the shelter. Treat as a local rest/fire point only if signed on site and current reserve/fire-ban rules allow.

facilities.name: Bråvikenbranten reserve rules
facilities.description: Reserve rules: tent max two nights in same place, dogs leashed, fires only at signed grill places, no damaging trees/dead wood/rock/ground, no collecting mosses/lichens/non-edible fungi, climbing needs permit, and check fire risk.

facilities.name: Skvättan/Bråvikenbranten parking
facilities.description: Reserve parking near the Brytsebo end, about 7 spaces with information boards/picnic context. Also useful for stage 33/34 access; do not assume overflow roadside parking.

facilities.name: Stage 33:1 junction near Brytsebo
facilities.description: Topological end of OSM Stage 33:1 where it meets Stage 33. To reach the Stage 33/34 Brytsebo board, continue about 0.37 km along Stage 33 toward 58.651099, 16.551060. Nearby parking is at Brytsebo/Skvättan, not necessarily at this junction.

facilities.name: Brytsebo Stage 33/34 board
facilities.description: Stage 33/34 shared Brytsebo board area, reached from Stage 33:1 by adding a short Stage 33 connector of about 0.37 km. Use this marker for continuation to Stage 34, not as the raw 33:1 relation endpoint.

sections.name: Stage 34: Brytsebo to Holmtorp
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 34, Brytsebo to Holmtorp.
utilities: Official area: Norrköpings kommun, Nyköpings kommun.

Parking is available at/near Brytsebo/Skvättan and at Fjällmossen main parking northwest of Vrångsjön; Holmtorp itself has no reliable public parking, so use Vrångsjön/Fjällmossen parking about 1.5 km before Holmtorp or arrange pickup.

Public transport is weak: Marielundsvägen is the closest researched bus stop to Brytsebo with sparse school-day line 902 service, while Holmtorp has no close stop within 2 km. Kolmården station is the nearest rail node but is far from the stage and requires bus, taxi, bike or pickup logistics.
waterSources: Official natural sources: Lilla Göljen cold spring and a second source about 1.5 km east of Lilla Göljen. Treat/filter/boil unless current signs confirm potable water; Sörmlandsleden says trail water is not routinely tested or guaranteed.
No shops, cafes, lodging, potable taps, or dependable resupply were found within 2 km of the stage; carry food and water capacity.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden/Naturkartan distance is 13 km and difficulty is medium. The corrected drawn line uses OSM relation 3690159 because the official full-network GPX shortest path was truncated to about 9 km and missed the Fjällmossen/Lilla Göljen arc; secondary current measurements include 12.5 km in the 2025 Sörmlandsleden pass and about 12.4 km in OSM geometry.

Fjällmossen reserve has confusing blue markings; follow orange Sörmlandsleden marks carefully because blue dots mark Länsstyrelsen reserve trails. The Fjällmossen loop reuses a long part of Stage 34 and should be shown as a separate local loop overlay, not merged into the through-stage line.

The route passes remote forest, hills, rocky ground, productive forestry/clear-cuts, wet sections, and long boardwalks over Fjällmossen. Lilla Göljen/Fjällmossen is the main highlight and is consistently praised by hikers, but older trip reports also mention clear-cuts, machine ruts, roots, rocks, wet ground, and slippery descents after rain.

Skvättsjön is the early official swim/rest option after about 300 m; Vrångsjön has swimming possibilities later. Lilla Göljen is beautiful but Sörmlandsleden does not recommend it as a normal bathing lake, and reserve/loop material explicitly mentions blood leeches.

No official stage-34 faults were shown on the Sörmlandsleden page as of 2026-04-27. Nearby Lövsjöstigen in Fjällmossen is temporarily closed in 2026 due to fallen trees and poor boardwalks; this is a nearby-loop warning, not a confirmed stage-34 closure.

Fjällmossen reserve rules: no tenting or caravan setup, dogs leashed, do not damage living/dead trees, pick only berries/mushrooms, and make fires only at signed/designated places where permitted while checking current fire bans and signs. The Södermanland reserve page has stricter no-fire wording, so avoid broad fire-allowed claims. Fire-ban checks on 2026-04-27 showed no ban in Norrköping or Nyköping, but this must be checked day-of.

Lilla Göljen has two shelters and is the overnight/rest node, but this is not a legal tenting area; shelters are first-come/shared and condition/capacity/firewood can change. Firewood is reported about 400 m away near the parking/road turnaround.

Access is car/bike-shuttle oriented. Naturkartan found no nearby public-transport stops for the stage; trip reports used bike shuttle logistics, and practical one-way options are two cars, bike shuttle, taxi, or pickup at Brytsebo/Vrångsjön/Holmtorp by arrangement.

facilities.name: Marielundsvägen bus access

facilities.name: Kolmården station

facilities.name: Skvättsjön swim/rest

facilities.name: Pigans Plågosten side sight

facilities.name: Fjällmossen bog boardwalks

facilities.name: Lilla Göljen lake
facilities.description: Scenic lake by the shelter cluster. Do not market as a normal bathing lake: Sörmlandsleden says it is not a good bathing lake, while local material mentions blood leeches.

Södermanland reserve wording is stricter on fire; follow local signs and check Norrköping/Nyköping fire status day-of.

sections.name: Stage 35: Holmtorp to Nävsjön
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 35, Holmtorp to Nävsjön.
utilities: Official area: Norrköpings kommun, Nyköpings kommun.

No parking at Holmtorp; official guidance says to park about 1.5 km earlier on stage 34 near Vrångsjö. Nävsjön has hiker/reserve/fishery parking, dry toilet context, pump, fishing permit machine, and several shelters/rest points, but fishing-association parking inside the fishery area requires a valid fishing permit.

Public transport is weak at both ends: Västanåvägen is about 2.5-2.9 km from Holmtorp, Nävsjövägen bus stop on line 561 is several km from Nävsjön by road/trail, and the useful train anchors are distant Kolmården or Nyköping C with bus/taxi/bike/pickup logistics.
waterSources: Official water: Svartsjön spring after about 7-7.5 km and Nävsjön pump near the stage end. Treat/filter/boil and verify all water; Sörmlandsleden says trail water is not routinely checked or guaranteed.

A 2024-11-23 public comment on the official stage page reported dead frogs in the Svartsjön spring and advised bringing water, so treat that source as unreliable until rechecked on site and carry backup water.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 12 km and the local official-GPX route geometry measures about 11.9 km, so the drawn route is plausible. Naturkartan shows 12.0 km / 12,171 m, OSM relation 3696285 measures about 12.06 km, and Naturkartan public geometry about 12.14 km; avoid implying exact metre-level distance.
Stage 35 crosses county/reserve contexts: Naturkartan lists the stage under Östergötland, while Nävsjön reserve rules are from Södermanland and nearby Nävsjömossen rules from Östergötland.
Near Holmtorp, grazing cattle may occur in pasture; keep dogs controlled and handle gates/fences carefully.

When the trail leaves the road early in the stage, an official 200 m side path reaches Vrångsjön's eastern shore with swimming and a possible tent spot on rock. Verify signs and boundaries before tenting, and do not generalize this to protected Nävsjön reserve areas.

The route passes mixed forest and agricultural land, modern forestry/clear-cut areas, then improves around Svartsjön and Nävsjön with lake, mire, boardwalk, older-pine, and shelter/rest character. Despite Naturkartan's green/simple label, user reports describe wet vegetation, rutted/flooded tracks, young birch hiding the tread, overgrown cultural land, roots, slippery boardwalks and tick-season concerns after rain.

No official stage-35 fault reports were shown on the Sörmlandsleden page during the 2026-04-27 research pass, but the page comments include the 2024 Svartsjön spring warning. Treat no formal fault report as a status snapshot, not a guarantee.

Nävsjön reserve rules are strict: no tenting, no fires, dogs leashed, no damaging living/dead wood, and no plant picking except berries/mushrooms. In nearby Nävsjömossen, keep dogs leashed, protect plants/wildlife, and use only arranged grill places where allowed.

Nävsjön shelters are not all equivalent: the west/north shelter is primarily for fishers, the south-bay shelter is mainly Nävsjön-runt context, and map-source condition/capacity notes should be treated as current-condition caveats rather than guarantees.

Fishing at Nävsjön requires a permit and local fishery rules apply, including one hand tackle with max one hook/lure, max three salmonids per permit, no live/dead bait fish and no sonar/electronic fishing equipment. Fishing prices and boat/cabin details can change, so link users to Nävsjön Sportfiske rather than hard-coding a trip budget.

At Nävsjön, Stage 35, Stage 36, Stage 36:1 and Nävsjön runt all meet or share physical ways. Use the complete Nävsjön runt loop relation for loop display, not the partial duplicate arc, and avoid drawing duplicate lines over the shared Stage 35/36 sections.

facilities.description: Nävsjömossen context: keep dogs leashed, protect plants/wildlife, boardwalks can be slippery when damp, and use only arranged grill places where allowed; do not build new fire rings.

sections.name: Stage 36: Nävsjön to Nävekvarn
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 36, Nävsjön to Nävekvarn.
utilities: Official area: Nävekvarn, Nyköpings kommun.

Nävsjön has parking before the fishing association area, about 200 m from the trail, plus pump/fishery access. Nävekvarn has Gula Kvarn parking, bus 561 toward Nyköping, camping/guesthouse, summer tap, toilets, Parkbadet, harbor food/service, grocery/deli, and lodging options.

Public transport is practical at the Nävekvarn end via bus 561. Nävsjön is weak by transit; Nävsjövägen bus access is several km from the lake, and Nyköping C is the practical rail anchor for the Nävekvarn side.
waterSources: Official water: Nävsjön pump at the start and the spring south of Nävsjön after about 2.5 km. Sörmlandsleden explicitly says trail water is not routinely checked, so verify/treat/filter.
In summer, water can be fetched from a tap at Nävekvarn camping; mapped drinking water near the camping/harbor should still be treated as seasonal/service-dependent.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 11 km. Secondary sources such as AllTrails and Äventyrligare are around 10 km, and OSM relation 3821815 measures about 10.2 km. Keep 11 km as the planning distance but describe the drawn geometry as about 10-11 km rather than exact.

The older local/Naturkartan-derived geometry exposed a stale 7767 m line and missed the Bråviken/Vibberholmen/Nävekvarns klint arc. Stage 36 should be drawn from OSM relation 3821815, with the official Gula Kvarn endpoint used for stage chaining.

Official fault status showed no reported faults as of 2026-04-27. Nearby warnings on Stage 36:1, including the Bötesberget powerline passage and 2026 Stora Bötet conservation burn notices, should not be applied to Stage 36 unless the user selects that branch.

The stage is relatively easy overall but varied: lake/forest by Nävsjön, sparse conifer forest, hällmark/rocky knolls, mining/cultural-history points, ravine descent, Bråviken coast, and the steep Nävekvarns klint climb/descent before Nävekvarn. Hiker reports caution that the repeated small rocky ups/downs can feel more tiring than the official wording suggests, especially in heat or late in a long day.

Wet weather makes the Bråviken/Nävekvarns klint side more demanding, with slippery rocks, polished roots, boardwalks, mud and coastal rock reported by hikers. Older reports also describe forestry/logging damage on parts north of the gravel-road middle section, so current trail condition can matter.
Camping/tenting may be possible around Nävsjön only outside the nature-reserve parts; do not present Nävsjön reserve itself as a tenting or fire area.

Nävsjön reserve: no tenting, no fires, dogs leashed, no damaging living/dead wood, and no plant picking except berries/mushrooms. Nävsjömossen allows fires only at arranged grill places and no new fire rings; Nävekvarns klint requires bringing your own firewood and forbids taking live or dead reserve wood.

Do not present the early shelters as guaranteed comfortable overnight infrastructure: the west Nävsjön shelter is primarily for fishers, the Nävsjön Öst shelter is small, and recent OSM/community notes flag Kolarkojan as fire-damaged/charred.

Stage 36 has several overlapping local route options near Nävekvarn. Keep Skäret and Nävekvarnsslingan/Nävekvarns klint as optional loops or side variants; do not merge them into the linear Stage 36 unless the itinerary explicitly asks for a scenic loop.

sections.name: Stage 36:1: Nävsjön to Gälkhyttan
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 36:1, Nävsjön to Gälkhyttan.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.

Nävsjön has parking before the fishing association area, about 350 m to the stage board, plus pump, toilet/fireplace context, fishing permit machine, and bathing. Gälkhyttan has small parking/access, bathing possibility, and continuation to stage 36:2.

Public transport is poor at both ends: Nävsjövägen is several km from Nävsjön, Lilla Brakärr/Harsta-side stops are around 3 km from Gälkhyttan, and Nyköping C is the distant practical rail anchor. Gälkhyttan may have sparse pre-booked complement traffic, not normal walk-up transit.
waterSources: Official water on the stage is the Nävsjön pump at the start. Treat/verify because Sörmlandsleden water is not routinely quality checked.
No reliable refill is documented between Nävsjön and Gälkhyttan; treat natural lake/stream water as untreated and carry enough water.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 9 km; Naturkartan, Äventyrligare, AllTrails and OSM cluster around 8.45-8.53 km, including Naturkartan's 8,534 m and OSM relation 3696287 at about 8,531 m. Keep 9 km as the planning label while describing the measured drawn route as about 8.5 km.

Use OSM relation 3696287/Naturkartan for the main Stage 36:1 line. The OSM relation is a clean two-endpoint line but ordered Gälkhyttan to Nävsjön, so reverse it for official direction and snap topology to the shared Nävsjön node at 58.663211,16.734525 and Gälkhyttan node at 58.692472,16.809794; the official signed/access coordinate at Gälkhyttan is about 67 m away.

The 0.8 km Naturkartan 'alternativ väg' at Bötesberget/Stora Bötet is an internal route choice, not a separate branch in the trail catalog. The canonical OSM/Naturkartan main line uses the upper Bötesberget route; keep the lower ski-track route as an optional local alternative only when this stage is selected.

The branch is wildlife-rich and mostly easy mixed forest, but Bötesberget and Stora Bötet are harder: mire/boardwalk sections can be very wet in spring, autumn, or after rain, and the lower Bötesberget route had many fallen spruce reported in 2026. The Stora Bötet trail is a managed access corridor through wet reserve terrain; outside the marked line there may be no boardwalks and movement can be difficult.

Official current warnings as of 2026-04-27: limited passage under the powerline near Bötesberget from 2025-02-13, a dangerous rotten broken spruce near Tyskdammen from 2026-04-22, and planned Stora Bötet conservation burn/smoke during suitable weeks 18-44 in 2026.
Route sequence: Nävsjön, early Nävån industrial remains, storskog, Tyskdammen, Stora Bötet/Bötesberget upper-lower option, Gälkhyttedammen, Gälkhyttan.

Stora Bötet reserve rules include no damaging living/dead trees, no collecting plants/mosses/fungi/lichens except ordinary berries/edible mushrooms/personal-use flowers where allowed, no off-road motor vehicles, no disturbing wildlife, and organized camps/competitions require permission.

No food, potable water, toilet, or shelter was verified at the Gälkhyttan endpoint itself. The Överdammen shelter/toilet/fireplace is a Stage 36:2 or Gälkhyttan loop continuation, about 4 km away, and Pilthyttedammen reserve forbids tenting.

Gälkhyttan has N14 complementary/on-demand traffic toward Nyköping in some timetable patterns, but it is not walk-up transit: current researched notes point to Wednesday service, booking by phone before 16:00 the weekday before, and a four-person capacity limit. Always use the live planner for the travel date.

facilities.name: Nävsjön stage start
facilities.description: Official start of stage 36:1 and junction with stages 35 and 36. Parking is before the fishing association area, about 350 m from the stage board.

facilities.name: Nävsjön pump

facilities.name: Nävsjön hiker/fishery parking
facilities.description: Parking before/near the fishery area and permit machine. Parking inside the fishing association area requires a valid fishing permit; non-fishing visitors should use the free car parking in the slope outside the large parking and follow local signs.

facilities.name: Nävsjön reserve parking

facilities.name: Nävsjön access road warning

facilities.name: Nävsjön toilet/fireplace context

facilities.name: Nävsjön fishing permit machine
facilities.description: Fishing permits are sold at the north parking/fishery area. Permit required for stocked fish; current local rules restrict tackle, catch limits, bait fish and electronic aids, so check Nävsjön Sportfiske before fishing.

facilities.name: Nävsjön Sportfiske stuga
facilities.description: Bookable simple cabin near the start, typically for up to four people. Water is from a marked spring about 100 m away but is not quality-guaranteed; verify booking, access and rules.

facilities.name: Nävsjön Norröst shelter context
facilities.description: Fisher-oriented worn lean-to context near Nävsjön, not a guaranteed comfortable official overnight stage facility. Capacity/firewood/condition should be field-checked.

facilities.name: Nävsjön Öst shelter context

facilities.name: Nävsjön kolarkoja context
facilities.description: Kolarkoja near the Nävsjön/Nävsjömossen side. Recent OSM/community notes report fire damage/charred interior and very limited capacity; verify before relying on it.

facilities.name: Nävsjövägen bus access
facilities.description: Fixed-route line 561 corridor stop for Nävsjön access, but still a poor trailhead: about 4.7 km road/approach walk from the lake and no shelter mapped. Verify live service.

facilities.name: Nyköping C train access
facilities.description: Distant rail anchor for both endpoints, roughly 13-18 km away depending on side; combine with bus, taxi, bike, or pickup.

facilities.name: Nävån industrial remains
facilities.description: Early-route cultural cluster near Nävån/Övershyttan: linbråkargrop, unique stone cold-smoke oven, smithy remains, waterfall, and 1500s ironworks context.

facilities.name: Tyskdammen dam wall

facilities.name: Rotten spruce hazard near Tyskdammen

facilities.name: Bötesberget route choice

facilities.description: The lower 'skidspår' option should not be treated as reliably easy: a 2026-03-11 stage-page comment reports many bark-beetle-felled spruces and awkward passage, though passable with detours.

facilities.name: Bötesberget alternative route

facilities.name: Bötesberget powerline works

facilities.name: Stora Bötet mire crossing
facilities.description: Large mire/boardwalk area and managed trail corridor through a wet reserve with rich birdlife. Can be very wet in spring/autumn or after rainy periods; older trip reports describe boardwalks under decimetres of water, so waterproof boots may be needed.

facilities.name: Stora Bötet conservation burn notice
facilities.description: 2026 notice: planned conservation burn about 1 km west of the trail during suitable weeks 18-44. Smoke may be noticeable on the burn day and afterwards, but the official note says the burn should not prevent hiking.

facilities.name: Stora Bötet reserve rules
facilities.description: Do not damage living/dead trees, collect plants/mosses/fungi/lichens beyond allowed berries/edible mushrooms/personal-use flowers, drive off-road, or disturb wildlife; organized camps/competitions require permission.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttedammen grill/rest
facilities.description: Official grill/rest point about 200 m before Gälkhyttan with a fine view over the dam. Use only established fireplaces, bring fuel, and check current fire bans.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttan bathing possibility
facilities.description: Official bathing possibility at/near Gälkhyttan; approximate pin by Gälkhyttedammen.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttan access
facilities.description: Very limited Gälkhyttedammen/Stora Bötet parking and Stage 36:2 continuation point. Länsstyrelsen says about 3 cars; have a backup plan and follow local signs.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttan industrial history
facilities.description: Historic mill/works area attested from the 1500s, with copper works, blast-furnace and water-powered hammer context between Gälkhyttedammen and Gälkhyttemossen.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttan no services caveat
facilities.description: No verified potable water, toilet, shelter or food was found at the Gälkhyttan endpoint itself. Överdammen facilities are a Stage 36:2/loop continuation, not on core 36:1.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttan N14 complement traffic
facilities.description: Possible on-demand/complementary traffic toward Nyköping, not normal spontaneous bus service. Research pass found Wednesday-only pattern, phone booking by 16:00 the weekday before, and max four travellers; verify live timetable.

facilities.name: Överdammen off-stage shelter context
facilities.description: Nearest verified shelter/toilet/fireplace continuation from Gälkhyttan, on Stage 36:2 / Gälkhyttan runt Överdammen roughly 4 km away. Pilthyttedammen reserve forbids tenting and permits fires only at the prepared shelter fireplace.

facilities.name: Lilla Brakärr bus access
facilities.description: Closest researched fixed-route stop to Gälkhyttan, about 2.9-3 km away. Sparse line 663/weekday-pattern context and no shelter mapped; verify live service before relying on it.

facilities.name: Äventyrskompaniet Gälkhyttan
facilities.description: Gårdshus lodging listed by Sörmlandsleden at/near Gälkhyttan with 6+2 beds; verify availability before relying on it.

facilities.name: Lasätter Gård
facilities.description: Lodging/event/catering venue listed by Sörmlandsleden about 2.5 km from Gälkhyttan. Treat as book-ahead off-route planning context, not a trail-side shop.

facilities.name: Planned Stage 36:1 shelter
facilities.description: Nyköping has announced a designed shelter planned for Stage 36:1, with completion/inauguration around late June 2026. Do not count it as available until verified built/open.

sections.name: Stage 36:2: Gälkhyttan to Fada kvarn
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 36:2, Gälkhyttan to Fada kvarn.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Gälkhyttan has small parking/access at the start. Fada kvarn has parking for a few cars and the Fada bus stop at the end, but official notes say buses stop at Fada less often.

Tunakorset is usually the more useful Fada-side bus access, about 1-1.5 km by road. Gälkhyttan-side public transport is weak: Lilla Brakärr is about 2.9 km from the start, while Nyköping C is the distant rail anchor.

Nearby lodging/service options include Äventyrskompaniet at Gälkhyttan, Lasätter Gård off-route from Gälkhyttan, Broby B&B on the Fada/Kiladalen side, and seasonal Palstorps Hage/Skogsby; verify opening and exact pickup/access before relying on them.
waterSources: No verified potable water source was found on stage 36:2. Gälkhyttedammen, Överdammen/Pilthyttedammen and Fadadammen are natural or reservoir water only; treat/filter/boil if used.
Överdammen/Vindskyddskartan-style water references should be treated as unknown-quality shoreline water, not a drinking-water tap or tested spring. Carry enough water from a reliable source.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden planning should treat 36:2 as one stage with two same-endpoint alternatives: a shorter/northern route listed as 7 km and a longer southern/eastern route listed as 9 km via Pilthyttedammen and Överdammen shelter.

The short/northern option should use OSM relation 3696288's main connected component only, about 6.58 km mapped, from the shared 36:1 node at 58.692472,16.809794 to the shared 36:3 node at 58.728950,16.841419. Exclude floating OSM way 889021104; drawing the raw relation naively creates a small disconnected dyke segment near Överdammen.

The long/eastern Överdammen option is not cleanly encoded by OSM relation 3696288. Reconstruct it by replacing the direct way 671203754 between nodes 6088173873 and 914038009 with the eastern loop segment from OSM relation 18434805 (Rundslinga Gälkhyttedammen), giving about 8.65 km mapped and matching the official 9 km planning label.

Naturkartan's 5.1 km geometry appears incomplete for endpoint routing because it does not reliably terminate at Fada kvarn. Keep Sörmlandsleden as authority for the two official alternatives and planning distance.

No current official fault report was found on the stage page during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Adjacent Stage 36:1 has current warnings, but they should be presented as through-hike context rather than Stage 36:2 faults.

The shorter route goes more directly through forest and partly afforested former farmland. The longer route follows Gälkhyttedammen, houses, an old railway embankment, Pilthyttedammen reserve, Överdammen shelter, and a small viewpoint over the dam landscape. The longer/eastern option can be wetter and slower than the distance suggests, but carries the shelter/toilet/fireplace services.

Pilthyttedammen reserve: no tenting; fires only at the prepared fireplace by Överdammen shelter; pets must be leashed; do not damage living or dead trees or shrubs; do not pick plants except berries and edible mushrooms; avoid disturbing wildlife within 100 m of nests/dens.

Stora Bötet is adjacent access context at Gälkhyttan rather than the core 36:2 corridor. No explicit public tenting ban was found on the current Stora Bötet rule page, but group camps/competitions require permission and the general no-damage/no-disturbance reserve rules apply.

Fadadammen and Fada kvarn are the main end-of-stage rest/cultural nodes. Fadarundan says one tent can fit at Fadadammen, but use this cautiously as a single small rest/tent possibility, not a campsite: verify signs, stay outside prohibited reserve areas, and follow allemansrätten.
No verified potable water source was found on Stage 36:2. Gälkhyttedammen, Överdammen/Pilthyttedammen and Fadadammen are natural/reservoir water only and should be treated/filtered/boiled if used.
Older trip reports mention wet grass, overgrowth, mud and slippery boards/rocks around Strogen/Fadadammen/Fada after rain. Treat as seasonal practical caution rather than a current closure.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttan parking

facilities.name: Gälkhyttan firepit
facilities.description: OSM-mapped firepit near the start by Gälkhyttedammen; not listed as the official stage fireplace. Verify locally and observe fire bans.

facilities.name: Gälkhyttedammen natural water
facilities.description: Lake/reservoir water by the start; Naturkartan also marks bathing/ice activity nearby. Not a verified potable source; treat/filter/boil if used.

facilities.name: Stage 36:2 route options
facilities.description: Stage 36:2 has two official alternatives: shorter/northern about 7 km / 6.6 km mapped and longer southern/eastern via Pilthyttedammen/Överdammen about 9 km / 8.7 km mapped. Attach Överdammen facilities as on-route only when the long variant is selected.

facilities.name: Stage 36:2 OSM variant caveat
facilities.description: OSM relation 3696288 represents the short connected route plus a disconnected 46 m dyke way. For the long route, combine with Rundslinga Gälkhyttedammen relation 18434805 and replace direct way 671203754 between nodes 6088173873 and 914038009.

facilities.name: Stage 36:2 map-source caveat
facilities.description: Naturkartan's public 5.1 km geometry appears incomplete for Stage 36:2 because it does not terminate at Fada kvarn. Do not use it as endpoint-routing authority.

facilities.name: Överdammen shelter
facilities.description: Official shelter on the longer Pilthyttedammen/Överdammen alternative, not on the short option. Official loop sources and OSM/Vindskyddskartan context report fireplace, dry toilet and firewood nearby; a 2024 group report used it as a coffee-break stop.

facilities.name: Överdammen fireplace
facilities.description: Prepared fireplace by the shelter; this is the only permitted fire site inside Pilthyttedammen reserve. Current fire bans still override use.

facilities.name: Överdammen dry toilet
facilities.description: Dry toilet by the Överdammen shelter area on the longer route option.

facilities.name: Överdammen / Pilthyttedammen natural water
facilities.description: Nearby dam/reservoir water only; user shelter maps list water of unknown quality and hiker reports describe lake water rather than a spring. Treat/filter/boil and carry backup.

facilities.name: Pilthyttedammen reserve rules
facilities.description: No tenting in the reserve; fires only at the prepared shelter fireplace; dogs/pets must be leashed; do not damage living or dead wood; plant picking is limited to berries and edible mushrooms; avoid disturbing wildlife within 100 m of nests/dens.

facilities.name: Pilthyttedammen dam caution
facilities.description: Historic regulated dam-water landscape from early iron-working. Treat sluices, dam edges and winter ice as caution points; do not present Fadadammen or Pilthyttedammen ice as safe without current local checks.

facilities.name: No verified Stage 36:2 drinking water
facilities.description: No potable tap or tested spring was verified on Stage 36:2. Bring water or treat/filter/boil natural water.

facilities.name: Strogen/Fada wet overgrowth caution
facilities.description: Older trip reports mention wet grass, overgrowth and muddy fields around Strogen/Fada, especially after rain. Treat as seasonal practical caution rather than a current closure.

facilities.name: Fadadammen rest area
facilities.description: Good rest area near the end before Fada kvarn. Natural dam/lake water only; Fadarundan notes that one tent fits here, but treat it as a single small rest/tent possibility, not a campsite, and verify signs/boundaries.

facilities.name: Fadadammen / Fadabäcken natural water
facilities.description: Dam/stream water near Fada rest area and Fada kvarn; not a verified drinking-water source. Treat/filter/boil if used.

facilities.name: Fada kvarn
facilities.description: Historic mill/forge and dam area, stage end, and connection to stage 36:3. Sörmlandsleden describes the waterfall context as a notable Sörmland feature.

facilities.name: Fada kvarn parking
facilities.description: Parking for a few cars by Fada kvarn; official Fadarundan text asks visitors to park diagonally and mentions an alternate gravel parking area about 1 km onward, but no precise coordinate was verified.

facilities.name: Fada bus stop
facilities.description: Closest paired bus stop at the end, essentially at Fada kvarn, but buses stop here less often according to official notes; verify live Sörmlandstrafiken service. North-side paired stop is at about 58.729086,16.841446.

facilities.name: Harsta korset bus stop
facilities.description: Alternative bus access in the Fada/Harsta corridor, around 1.5 km from Fada depending on route choice. OSM maps paired stops here; verify current Sörmlandstrafiken service.

facilities.name: Tunakorset bus stop
facilities.description: More useful official public-transport access for Fada, about 1-1.5 km road walk from Fada kvarn. Verify live Sörmlandstrafiken departures.

facilities.name: Lilla Brakärr bus access
facilities.description: Closest researched mapped stop to Gälkhyttan, about 2.9 km from the start, but service is sparse and not a normal convenient trailhead. Verify live service.

facilities.name: Brakärr bus access
facilities.description: Nearby line-663 corridor stop east of Lilla Brakärr. Useful only with live timetable confirmation and extra road walking from Gälkhyttan.

facilities.name: Nyköping C train access
facilities.description: Nearest major train station, roughly 12.9 km from Gälkhyttan and 9.5 km from Fada; mark as far/off-route context.

facilities.name: Berga kulle nearby reserve
facilities.description: Nearby/off-route reserve with old pine/spruce forest and Kiladalen views. Only show as nearby context unless the selected variant actually approaches it; reserve rules include no camping, no fires and no riding.

facilities.name: Berga kulle parking
facilities.description: Nearby reserve parking, not a core Stage 36:2 trailhead. Mark as off-route/distant unless route-distance checking shows it lies within the selected variant buffer.

facilities.name: Äventyrskompaniet Gälkhyttan
facilities.description: Gårdshus lodging listed by Sörmlandsleden at/near Gälkhyttan with 6+2 beds; verify availability before relying on it.

facilities.name: Lasätter Gård
facilities.description: Lodging/food-fika by arrangement listed by Sörmlandsleden about 2.5 km from Gälkhyttan, so show as off-route planning context.

facilities.name: Broby Bed & Breakfast
facilities.description: Lodging near Kiladalen Golf listed by Sörmlandsleden for stages 36:2/36:3/44. Coordinate is approximate and may be more than 2 km from the endpoint depending on access route.

facilities.name: Palstorps Hage / Skogsby
facilities.description: Seasonal attraction/lodging/service context on the Fada side, not a core trail facility. Verify opening and access before planning around it.

sections.name: Stage 36:3: Fada kvarn to Bergshammar
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 36:3, Fada kvarn to Bergshammar.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.

Fada kvarn has very limited parking for a few cars and a nearby bus stop, but official notes say buses stop at Fada less often. Tunakorset is the more reliable Fada-side public-transport access, about 1-1.5 km by road.

At the Bergshammar end, the practical endpoint is the stage 44 junction rather than Bergshammar village center. Bergshammar kyrka and Bergshammar bus stops are about 1.3-1.4 km north of the trail junction.

Nearby off-route services include Broby Bed & Breakfast and Palstorps Hage on the Kiladalen side, plus Tuna Motell, AutoMat Svalsta and Rasta Nyköpingsbro as farther service options. Treat them as deliberate detours, not stage facilities.
waterSources: No verified potable water source was found directly on stage 36:3. Carry water.
The Bergshammar spring/drinking-water point is on stage 44 about 1 km east of the 36:3 junction; show it only as continuation context and verify/treat before relying on it.
Fada dam/stream water and other natural water along the stage are not verified potable sources.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Current official Sörmlandsleden distance is 5.5 km, Naturkartan lists about 5.3 km, and the local route geometry measures about 5.18 km, so the drawn line looks broadly plausible. Older long-distance-passport, OSM tag and blog sources sometimes list 6.5 km; treat that as stale unless reverified.

This is a Fada-to-Bergshammar connector into stage 44, not a continuation toward the coastal Tunaberg stages. The local endpoint is the stage 44 junction west/southwest of Bergshammar village; snap topology to OSM node 914036955 at 58.729103,16.911059 rather than Bergshammar village center.
No current official fault report was found on the stage page during the 2026-04-27 research pass, and Naturkartan API status did not show a closure or trail-status report.

Route character: short and officially easy, but varied. The stage leaves Fada kvarn through lush Fadabäcken creek ravines, crosses/skirts wet stream features, climbs to Jätteberget, then follows higher ground with views across Kiladalen, Kilaån and toward Bergshammar church.
Jätteberget is described by Sörmlandsleden as 72.5 m above sea level and has World War II air-watch history.

Nya Stigar, Fadarundan comments and local walking notes add useful wet-weather caution: ravines/descents near Fada, steps, bridge/fords and board/plank sections can be muddy, slippery, erosion-prone, awkward with dogs, or affected by beaver activity.
Fada kvarn is a heritage/rest point, but do not imply guaranteed interior access or flowing waterfall: local reports say the mill may be locked and the fall can be dry at times.

No shelter, toilet, fireplace, shop, drinking water, or confirmed campsite was found directly on stage 36:3. Camping follows allemansrätten unless local signs or nearby protected-area rules say otherwise, and fires should not be made on moss, peat, rock slabs or outside safe/permitted places.

No named nature reserve was confirmed on the core Stage 36:3 corridor. Nearby Berga kulle is off-route context only; if shown, keep its stricter rules separate: no tenting, no fires, no riding, no motor vehicles, and no damaging trees/dead wood.

sections.name: Stage 37: Nävekvarn to Lilla Uttervik
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 37, Nävekvarn to Lilla Uttervik.
utilities: Official area: Nävekvarn, Nyköpings kommun.
Nävekvarn/Gula Kvarn has the official start, parking, bus 561 access toward Nyköping, and nearby harbour/camping/food/lodging services. Most services are seasonal or opening-hour dependent.

Lilla Uttervik is a quiet stage junction with stage 38 rather than a service node. The closest researched bus access is north of the endpoint at Laggarbo/Syrtorpsvägen, about 1.8-1.9 km away, and the area may rely on sparse/pre-booked N07 complement traffic rather than reliable walk-up service; Nyköping C is the distant train anchor.
Skeppsvik and Sjöskogen provide useful intermediate access/parking and swimming/rest context, but they should be treated as local access nodes rather than full-service trailheads.

Svartåhällen is the only verified on-stage shelter/rest/fires cluster. The dry toilet is mapped and listed by older route sources, but Länsstyrelsen currently marks the Sjöskogen toilet as closed until a later opening update.
waterSources: No verified potable water source was found directly on stage 37 after leaving Nävekvarn. Carry water.
Nävekvarn harbour/camping has mapped/seasonal service water; verify access and season before relying on it.

Bråviken/coastal water and any small streams are not drinking-water sources. If continuing onto stage 38, the Uttervik water-treatment-plant tap is the next stronger official refill context, beyond stage 37.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden, Naturkartan, and the long-distance passport list stage 37 as 6.5 km, while the current local route geometry measures about 5.8 km, OSM relation 3821822 measures about 5.93 km, and third-party route pages land around 5.8-5.9 km. Keep the official 6.5 km and treat the mapped line as plausible but slightly shorter.
Naturkartan grades the stage red/demanding. Although short, it has road walking, a steep climb toward Fyrberget, rocky/coastal forest, cliffs, crevices, and repeated small climbs through Sjöskogen.

No active official fault report was found on the stage page during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Official comments mention 2024 signage confusion near the road turn toward Fyrberget/Sjöskogen; a 2025 stage-maintainer reply says poles/signage should be present, but the app should still add a map cue when leaving the road.

Some third-party loop/app tracks around Nävekvarn, Stage 37:1 and the larger Nävekvarn-Ålbäck coast loop can disagree with current Sörmlandsleden markings and may route onto old/disused wet or windthrow-affected lines. For the direct Stage 37 hike, follow current orange markings and official signage rather than old loop lines.

Topology: stage 37 connects back to stage 36 at Nävekvarn and forward to stage 38 at Lilla Uttervik. For exact route-builder stitching, snap west to OSM node 469855061 at 58.630521,16.800300 and east to OSM node 2789309812 at 58.622832,16.868308; keep official Gula Kvarn and Stage 38 coordinates as signed trailhead/context points.

Branch stage 37:1 starts from Nävekvarn/Gula Kvarn and should appear as a branch option when the user selects this area. Its OSM start is only about 23 m from the Stage 37/36 junction, but relation 9631219 has a tiny internal break near 58.6413,16.7957 if OSM geometry is used directly.

Sjöskogen has an internal local choice: the coastal path or a northern path around the hill toward Svartåhällen. Model this later as a Stage 37 variant choice rather than a separate hike; both reconnect at/near Svartåhällen.

Fyrberget and Sjöskogen reserve rules prohibit damaging or removing living/dead wood and restrict collecting plants/fungi/lichens, with ordinary berries and edible mushrooms allowed for personal use. Organized camps/competitions require permission.

Fires in Sjöskogen should use the prepared fireplaces at Svartåhällen/the shelter. Länsstyrelsen says to bring your own wood; do not collect dead or living wood in the reserve, and check current fire bans. During stricter fire bans even fixed grill places can be prohibited.
The Sjöskogen/Svartåhällen dry toilet is a known facility, but Länsstyrelsen currently lists the toilet as closed until an opening update. Treat it as status-sensitive, not guaranteed.
No dedicated wild campsite was found on stage 37. Use Nävekvarn camping for certainty; elsewhere follow allemansrätten, local signs, and reserve restrictions.

sections.name: Stage 37:1: Nävekvarn to Kärrgruvorna
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 37:1, Nävekvarn to Kärrgruvorna.
utilities: Official area: Nävekvarn, Nyköpings kommun.

Nävekvarn/Gula Kvarn is the official start, with parking, bus 561 toward Nyköping, and nearby harbour/camping/food/lodging services. Hyttvallen IP/Nävekvarns IP is a useful alternate start-side access point for the rerouted approach.

Kärrgruvorna has parking at/near Blombergstorp, a shelter/fireplace/toilet/water cluster, information boards, and onward connection to stage 37:2. End-side buses are available from Skräddarstugan/Laggarbo/Syrtorpsvägen, but they are not at the shelter and service should be verified.
Nyköping C is the nearest practical rail anchor, far from both ends; use bus, taxi, bike, or pickup for the trailheads.
waterSources: Kärrgruvan spring is the only verified on-stage water source, near the end of the stage. Treat/filter/boil because Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality; a June 2025 hiker report found the level very low.
Nävekvarn harbour/camping water is useful before starting, but it is service/seasonal context rather than an on-trail natural source.
Stordammen, Lilldammen/Nyhyttan and other historic dam waters are industrial/natural water context only; do not list them as potable refills.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden distance is 8 km. Naturkartan shows 7.2 km in visible metadata but also exposes 8466 m, the 2025 long-distance passport lists 7.5 km, third-party/blog sources run around 8.0-8.5 km, and the current local route geometry measures about 6.9 km. Keep the official 8 km while flagging the mapped line as shorter than the currently signed reroute may be.
This is an inland branch from Nävekvarn to Kärrgruvorna, not the coastal main continuation. It connects from the Nävekvarn/stage 37 area to stage 37:2 at Kärrgruvorna.

No current formal fault report was found on the stage page during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Official comments say the stage was partly rerouted in 2023 from Nävekvarn toward Koppartorpsvägen; follow orange arrows from Gula Kvarn via Hyttvallen and Utsiktstornet. Alstorpsdammen is now described as a loop, not the main route.

Third-party GPX/app data can still show the old Nävekvarn/Alstorpsdammen line. A March 2025 user report and wider AllTrails loop reviews describe old/disused lines after Nävekvarn as hard to follow, wet, marshy, and blocked by windthrow/root plates; use current orange markings on the ground.

Geometry/topology: the local app route measures about 6.86 km and OSM relation 9631219 about 7.09 km, shorter than official/Naturkartan/passport values. Keep 8 km as the planning distance, flag the current drawn line as shorter than the signed Hyttvallen reroute may be, and snap the end to OSM node 5486317989 shared with stage 37:2.

If OSM relation 9631219 is used directly, exclude or repair its tiny disconnected 9 m fragment near 58.6413,16.7957. At the start, treat the Nävekvarn/Gula Kvarn area as a shared junction cluster with stage 37 rather than requiring exact node identity.
Route character: mining/cultural-history branch with forest roads/paths, dams and old industrial remains, a steep Kungstorpsberget section, then the shelter and mine-hole landscape at Kärrgruvorna.

Kungstorpsberget has a strenuous climb and exposed viewpoint terrain around Utsiktstornet at about 58.641892,16.819528; official text says to be careful with children. Hiker reports mention steep rope, stair or railing-assisted sections around the tower/descent area.

Kärrgruvorna contains more than 40 old mine openings over roughly 600 x 300 m, plus ruins, spoil heaps, water-filled holes and cultural remains. Stay on marked paths/boards, keep children and dogs controlled, avoid edges, shafts, snow/leaf-covered depressions and degraded covers, and do not disturb heritage features.

Kärrgruvan shelter is the strongest overnight infrastructure on the stage. No separate verified tent site was found; use allemansrätten carefully and avoid homes, farmland, mine holes, ruins, and sensitive cultural remains.

Use only prepared fireplaces. The official page specifically notes that a 2019 forest fire started near the Kärrgruvan shelter, so extinguish completely and check current fire bans before lighting anything. Firewood is not reliable; a June 2025 field note reported none available.
Kärrgruvan runt is a short easy loop at the endpoint and should appear as a local option once the user selects the Kärrgruvorna end area.
