Kärrgruvorna has parking, shelter, fireplace, toilet, and the Kärrgruvan spring at the branch start. Start-side buses are available from Skräddarstugan, Laggarbo, or Syrtorpsvägen, but timetables and service days need checking.

Koppartorp/Tunabergs kyrka is the practical endpoint, with weekday-limited bus access, toilet, seasonal/field-check water, heritage/museum/cafe context, and connections to stages 41 and 42 plus Gruvslingan.
Nyköping C is the nearest practical train anchor but is far from both ends; use bus, taxi, bike, or pickup for trail access.
waterSources: Kärrgruvan spring near the start and Koppartorp tap near the end are the only verified practical water points. Treat/filter spring water, do not assume tested drinking-water quality, and verify seasonal tap availability.
No reliable mid-stage potable water was found. Natural water and old dam/mining water should not be treated as a safe refill.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden distance is 8 km and the 2025 long-distance passport lists 7.5 km, while Naturkartan exposes 6776 m / about 6.9 km, the current local route line measures about 6.83 km, and OSM relation 9631218 measures about 7.23 km. Keep the official 8 km and note that the drawn line is shorter and currently uncertain because of the active reroute.

Current official issue as of the 2026-04-27 research pass: a 2025-10-25 warning for spruce bark-beetle damage has escalated, with maintainers reporting that they no longer dare clear more fallen/falling spruce and that the stage will be temporarily shortened quite substantially. Follow current orange markings, ribbons and signs; older GPX/Naturkartan/AllTrails/local geometry may not match the safe signed route.

Topology: this is the second half of the inland Nävekvarn-Kärrgruvorna-Koppartorp branch, connecting from stage 37:1 at Kärrgruvorna to the Koppartorp hub where stages 41 and 42 also connect. Snap route-builder topology to OSM node 5486317989 at Kärrgruvorna and OSM node 2889617483 at Koppartorp.
Related local options: Kärrgruvan runt at the start, Gruvslingan at Koppartorp, Tunabergsrundan, and nearby Simonberget/Koppartorp/Kummelbergsrundan local walks.

Route character: officially easy/green in normal conditions but culturally dense and stop-start, with mine holes, smelting sites, dam/waterworks remains, rock carvings, Tomtabäcken, and Koppartorp's mining village and church. Older reports describe repeated small ups/downs around mine features; treat pre-2026 reports as condition-stale for routing.

Hazards: many old mine holes and ruins, fenced/open/water-filled shafts, cultural remains that should not be disturbed, a steeper climb after the Koppartorpsristningen/road crossing toward the stoll, some road crossings around Tomta/Koppartorp, and the active bark-beetle temporary reroute. Stay on marked paths, supervise children/dogs, and be extra careful around mine edges in snow, leaves or low light.

Camping: Kärrgruvan shelter at the start is the strongest overnight infrastructure. No dedicated tent site was found on stage 37:2 itself; use allemansrätten carefully and avoid mine holes, ruins, homes, roads, fields, and sensitive cultural sites.

Fire: use only prepared fireplaces at Kärrgruvan and Koppartorp/Storgruvan, check current fire bans, and extinguish fully. Kärrgruvan has known previous fire history nearby, and firewood is not guaranteed.

If extending into Simonberget reserve, tenting is only allowed below Simonberget between the dry toilet and fireplace for up to two nights; fires are only allowed at marked prepared sites; dogs must be leashed; Kummelberget bird-protection area is closed February 1-August 15.

Koppartorp is not a reliable resupply point. The hembygdsgård cafe/museum is seasonal and year-specific; the Koppartorp tap/toilet are useful but service-dependent rather than guaranteed public 24/7 infrastructure; the only dependable grocery context for the larger branch is back in Nävekvarn.

sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 38, Lilla Uttervik to Västra Kovik.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Lilla Uttervik has start access and parking on the stage 37 approach about 200 m before the stage board; the exact parking pin is approximate and should be checked against local signs.

Västra Kovik/Koviksbadet is the main service cluster, with parking, beach, dry toilet, grill/fireplace, benches, bin, and rest/swim access confirmed by Naturkartan, Havs- och vattenmyndigheten, OSM, and Grillplatser.nu.

Public transport is weak. Naturkartan finds no nearby stops for stage 38 or Västra Koviksbadet; fixed bus stops are off-route and complementary traffic can be weekday/advance-booking dependent. Car, bike, taxi, or pickup planning is usually needed.
Nyköping C is the nearest practical train anchor, but it is far from both endpoints and should be shown as off-route context, not as ordinary trail access.
waterSources: Uttervik water-treatment tap at the official coordinate is the only verified year-round potable refill on the stage.
Västra Kovik/Koviksbadet has shore and bathing water only; do not treat the beach/waterfront as a drinking-water refill.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden, OSM tags, and the long-distance passport list stage 38 as 7 km. Naturkartan/AllTrails show about 6.8 km, OSM relation 3822242 measures about 6.70 km, Äventyrligare about 6.67 km, Trail Run Project about 6.0 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 6.06 km. Treat 7 km as the official planning distance and show the mapped-line caveat until the Gullängsberget/variant geometry is refreshed.

Main-route topology is continuous from stage 37 at Lilla Uttervik to stage 39 at Västra Kovik. For route-builder stitching, snap to OSM node 2789309812 at 58.622832,16.868308 and OSM node 2889603613 at 58.618465,16.938396; the official start marker remains nearby as trailhead context.

A shorter northern alternative around Gullängsberget is described by Sörmlandsleden for hikers who do not want the climb. The Gullängsberget loop, northern bypass, and Tunabergsrundan/coastal variants should be modeled as optional local routes only when their geometry is available.

Uttervik nature reserve rules include no damaging living or dead trees/shrubs, no collecting or damaging plants, fungi, or lichens except ordinary berries, edible mushrooms, and flowers for personal use, and no organized camp/activity or competition without permission. Follow posted signs for any additional restrictions.

No official shelter, designated campsite, or verified wind shelter was found on stage 38. Do not market it as an overnight stage; the next official shelter is Viggudden on stage 39, about 2 km after Västra Kovik.

Fires should be limited to confirmed prepared places, especially the grill/fireplace at Västra Kovik/Koviksbadet. Bring your own charcoal/wood, pack out waste, and check current Nyköping/Sörmlandskusten fire-ban status because stricter bans can also prohibit fixed grill-place use.
Länsstyrelsen notes bark-beetle damage in Uttervik reserve, so dead spruces may fall; avoid exposed forest sections in strong wind or heavy precipitation.

Gullängsberget has views, old grave/cairn context, calcareous flora, and nearby Bronze Age/stone-setting heritage. User reports describe the climb as short but technical/rocky and slippery or wet in places; stay on marked routes and do not disturb cultural remains or protected flora.

Local SPF and blog reports note that the cottage-road/stig continuation southeast of Lilla Uttervik can be tricky; watch orange markers carefully through Uttervik's cottage roads because the path-road transition is easy to miss.

The official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass, but older maintainer/user reports show this corridor can be affected by blowdown and forestry debris, so check current trail status before relying on old GPX.

sections.name: Stage 39: Västra Kovik to Dragsviken
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 39, Västra Kovik to Dragsviken.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Västra Kovik/Koviksbadet is the strongest access and service cluster, with parking, bathing, dry toilet, grill/fireplace, benches, and bin at the start.
Viggudden is the main overnight/rest node on the stage, with an official Sörmlandsleden shelter, nearby toilet, and fireplace/grill context. The shelter roof was renovated in April 2026.

Dragsviken is a low-service endpoint and stage 40 junction. Official stage 40 information says there is no parking at the stage start; use Långsjöns fågeltorn/Gäddfabriken parking about 1 km away when exact access fits the itinerary.

Public transport is weak at both endpoints. Naturkartan finds no nearby stops; fixed bus stops are off-route and complementary traffic around Hummelvik/Östra Kovik/Ålbäck can require advance weekday booking.
waterSources: No verified potable refill was found on stage 39. Carry enough water from before Västra Kovik or from the previous verified refill at Uttervik on stage 38.
Vindskyddskartan lists water of unknown quality at/near Viggudden, and an abandoned mapped well near Västra Kovik should not be used for planning. Treat both as non-potable unless verified on site.
Västra Kovik, Viggudden, and the coast offer sea/bathing water only, not drinking-water refill.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden and the long-distance passport list stage 39 as 6 km, while Naturkartan exposes about 5639 m, OSM relation 3822358 measures about 5.8 km, Trail Run Project 5.8 km, Äventyrligare 5.77 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 5.71 km. Use 6 km as the official planning distance with a soft mapped-line caveat.

Main-route topology is continuous from stage 38 at Västra Kovik to stage 40 at Dragsviken. For route-builder stitching, snap to OSM node 2889603613 at 58.618465,16.938396 and OSM node 2889662498 at 58.632850,17.004986. Do not merge the Västra-Östra Kovik/Bråten loop into the main stage; it is an optional local loop.

This is a short but demanding red/krävande coastal stage, described by official and regional sources as one of Sörmlandsleden's longest coastal stretches, with repeated rocky climbs, exposed slabs, roots, and big Bråviken/Baltic views.

Hiker reports describe slow travel despite the short distance, with many ups and downs, steep rock, root/crack handholds, rope-assisted passages in places, and high water demand in warm weather. No reliable Stage 39 ladder report was found.
Official text notes cattle may be present in a pasture inside the bay at Östra Kovik. Keep dogs controlled/leashed, close gates, and pass livestock calmly.

No dedicated campsite was found beyond shelter use at Viggudden, though user reports mention tentable spots nearby. Do not present Västra Kovik beach as a tent spot; Nyköping public-place rules restrict public-place camping to named designated areas. Use normal allemansrätten judgment only where permitted, avoid houses, gardens, pastures, fragile coastal ground, sensitive shore/bird areas, and follow local signs.

Fires should only be at prepared fireplaces/grill places such as Västra Kovik or the Viggudden shelter area, and only when current Nyköping/Sörmlandskusten fire-ban status allows it. Bring fuel and never make informal fires on coastal rock slabs because they can crack.
Viggudden shelter is free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, has no trash service, and firewood is not provided. User reports confirm it is a real overnight/rest node, but it can be occupied.
Ålbäck fishing village is a coastal/cultural landmark on the stage. The route passes the fishing-place area before leaving the coast; use an approximate marker unless field-verified.

The shorter Västra Kovik-Östra Kovik-Bråten loop has a prepared grill place after about 1 km according to official text, but the exact coordinate was not confirmed; show it as an approximate local-option marker only.
The route passes/near cottage areas and Ålbäck fishing settlement; stay on marked trail/roads, avoid private jetties and yards, and keep noise low.
The official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass.

sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 40, Dragsviken to Mellsjön.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Dragsviken is a low-service stage start with no parking at the immediate trailhead. Official and Naturkartan guidance point hikers to Långsjöns fågeltorn/Långsjöns våtmark parking about 1 km away.
Mellsjön is a real overnight/access node at the stage end, with official shelter, tenting possibility, nearby toilet, fireplace/grill context, lake access, and parking nearby.
No shops, restaurants, cafes, or public potable taps were verified directly on this short stage.

Public transport is weak. Naturkartan found no nearby stops, the nearest OSM/Sörmlandstrafiken stops are off-route, and rural access may require Sörmlandstrafiken complementary traffic or a prebooked taxi.
Nävekvarn is the practical nearby service base for linked coastal hikes, with grocery/cafe, harbour food, camping/lodging, and bus 561 toward Nyköping, but it is not on stage 40 itself.
waterSources: No verified potable tap or spring was found on stage 40.
Mellsjön is natural lake water / water of unknown quality only. Filter, boil, or otherwise treat it before drinking, and do not present it as a drinking-water tap.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden lists stage 40 as 4 km, while Naturkartan exposes about 3505 m, AllTrails 3.4 km, Hiking Project 3.1 km, the local app GeoJSON measures about 3.39 km, and OSM relation 3822587 measures about 3.4 km despite a stale 4.5 km distance tag. Use 4 km as the official planning distance with a measured-line caveat.

Main-route topology runs from stage 39 at Dragsviken to stage 41 at Mellsjön. For route-builder stitching, snap to OSM node 2889662498 at 58.632850,17.004986 and OSM node 2889662243 at 58.642033,16.962128; the local route endpoints are within about 20 m of those nodes.

The official page describes a steep start up Dragsberget, then a ravine and ridge, Stora jättekasten cairn/boulder formation, Lilla Torskhult views, Stora Torskhult, and the hollow fruktbarhetseken. Blog reports add that direction matters: starting at Dragsviken puts the steep climb first, while starting at Mellsjön gives easier road/forest walking before the Dragsviken descent and can work well when linking into stage 39.
Stage 40 is easier and more inland than the exposed coastal scrambling on stage 39, but it is still somewhat hilly with hällmark/roots/rock and can be slippery in wet weather.

Mellsjön shelter is verified by Sörmlandsleden, Vindskyddskartan, OSM, Grillplatser, and later hiker reports. A 2016 geocaching note about a collapsed shelter roof appears stale because current sources list and use the shelter as active.

Official text explicitly says tenting is possible at Mellsjön and the toilet is a few minutes away. Apply normal allemansrätten judgment and any local signs; no stage-specific reserve prohibition was found in this pass.

Sörmlandsleden shelters are free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, have no bins, and do not guarantee firewood. A blog report mentioned wood at Mellsjön during one visit, but current wood supply should not be assumed. Pack out waste and verify shelter condition before depending on it overnight.

Use only prepared fireplaces/grill places, especially the Mellsjön shelter/grill area, bring your own fuel if needed, and check current Nyköping/Sörmlandskusten fire-ban status because stricter bans can also prohibit fixed grill places. Do not make fires on rock slabs or hällmark.
The stage can work as a short standalone hike or as part of a roughly 10 km official loop by parking at Mellsjön, using early stage 41 toward Östra Koviken, and returning via stage 39/40 context.

No protected-area or Natura 2000 polygon was found intersecting the Dragsviken-Långsjön-Mellsjön corridor during the 2026-04-27 public-source check, but local signs and general allemansrätten/fire rules still apply. Keep dogs leashed or under very close control around lake-shore wildlife, rural properties, and during wildlife season.

Dragsviken is a weak emergency/access point because there is no parking at the trailhead and public transport is poor. Mellsjön and Långsjöns fågeltorn parking are better practical access/evacuation points.
The official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Adjacent stage 41 still has an older 2023 reroute caveat if continuing west from Mellsjön.

sections.name: Stage 41: Mellsjön to Koppartorp
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 41, Mellsjön to Koppartorp.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.

Parking/access exists at Mellsjön and Koppartorp. Mellsjön-side public transport is weak, while Koppartorp/Tunabergs kyrka has the best endpoint transit but service may be limited or demand-responsive.

Koppartorp is the strong service endpoint, with seasonal summer tap, toilets, bus stop, Tunabergs kyrka, hembygdsgård, seasonal cafe/museum, Koppartorps rastplats, and mining heritage. The cafe/museum is normally a short summer-season service window, not year-round resupply.
Mellsjön shelter/toilet/tenting/fireplace/lake access is just before or near the stage start and is useful for planning, but it is primarily the stage 40 overnight node.
No shop, restaurant, or year-round potable water was verified directly along the middle of stage 41.
For year-round groceries, food, and lodging, Nävekvarn is the practical off-stage base west of Koppartorp; it is useful for linked Tunaberg/coastal hikes but not on this stage.
waterSources: Koppartorp church/hembygd summer tap is the strongest verified potable refill, but it is seasonal and should not be relied on outside summer.
No verified mid-stage potable water was found. Mellsjön and Överbosjön are natural water only; treat/filter/boil if used.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden lists stage 41 as 7 km, the 2025 long-distance pass lists 7.5 km, Naturkartan shows 7.4 km/7375 m, Äventyrligare 7.52 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 7.12 km. OSM relation 3822709 has correct endpoint topology but currently measures only about 5.45 km and diverges by over 1 km from the local/current line in places, so do not use OSM as the drawing source after the 2023 reroute.

Official Sörmlandsleden says a new route was completed on 2023-08-22 after landowner access changed, the old route was removed, and the first part of the text description may lag behind the updated map. Treat pre-August-2023 GPS tracks/blog distances and OSM/app-derived 5.5-6 km tracks as suspect.

Main-route topology runs from stage 40 at Mellsjön to stage 42 at Koppartorp. For route-builder stitching, snap to OSM node 2889662243 at 58.642033,16.962128 and OSM node 2889617483 at 58.645025,16.900148 while keeping the local current route geometry for drawing.
At Koppartorp the route connects to stage 42, stage 37:2, Gruvslingan/Kummelbergsrundan/Simonberget local options, and Tunabergsrundan.

Near Simonberget the route has a choice between a steeper scenic route over the top and an easier route below the southern cliff. Model this as an internal route option, not a separate stage. User reports confirm the high route is steep, rooty/rocky, exposed-feeling and rewarding; the lower route is easier but still not smooth or accessibility-grade.

Recent user reports for the wider Tunaberg/Nyköpingskusten loops warn that AllTrails and Sörmlandsleden can diverge. Follow current orange Sörmlandsleden markings and official/Naturkartan/local current geometry over old GPX/app tracks.

Simonberget/Kummelberget reserve rules are specific: tenting is allowed only below Simonberget between the dry toilet and fireplace, for at most two consecutive nights; fires only at the signed prepared fireplace; bring your own wood and do not take dead or living wood; dogs must be leashed.
Kummelberget bird-protection area is closed to access from February 1 through August 15, and climbing is forbidden there.

The stage crosses cultivated land after Överbosjön; official text says the landowner allows considerate hiking. Stay on the marked route, avoid crop damage, close gates if present, and do not rest or camp on cultivated land.

Blog and book-related reports praise the Simonberget high route as a Tunabergsrundan highlight, but note rocky ground, roots, loose stones, steep ascent, and an exposed cliff-edge feeling near the viewpoint. Hikers with knee, balance, or fitness concerns may prefer the lower/easier option.
Use current official/Sörmlandsleden/Naturkartan geometry over third-party tracks, especially because nearby Tunabergsrundan/Nävekvarn tracks can include removed or storm-damaged route segments.
Check current Nyköping/Sörmlandskusten fire-ban status before using any prepared fireplace; stricter bans can also prohibit fixed grill places.

Koppartorp/Tunabergs kyrka access is usually line 561 toward Nävekvarn with change at Buskhyttan to line 562. Line 562 service is limited, weekday-heavy in public planners, and some departures are call-controlled; verify live times and book anropsstyrd traffic when required. Current public notes for complementary traffic are date-bound, so verify 2026 service live.
The official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass.

sections.name: Stage 42: Koppartorp to Skyrshyttan
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 42, Koppartorp to Skyrshyttan.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.

Koppartorp is the strong service/access node with parking, Tunabergs kyrka bus stop, toilet, seasonal summer tap, Tunabergs hembygdsgård cafe/museum, Koppartorps rastplats, and mining heritage. The cafe/museum is summer-seasonal and should not be treated as year-round food.
Skyrshyttan is a sparse endpoint and stage 43 junction. Official stage 43 information says there is no good parking at the stage start, only possible roadside space for perhaps one car.

Skyrshyttan-side transit is usually via Munksäter/Munksätter bus stop plus roughly 15 minutes of walking. Knaptorp can be a useful mid-stage bus workaround if line 561 timing fits. Koppartorp/Tunabergs kyrka service may be limited, weekday-heavy, or demand-responsive; verify live Sörmlandstrafiken.
No shop, shelter, designated campsite, verified toilet, or potable water was found mid-stage or at Skyrshyttan.
waterSources: The only verified refill is the Koppartorp church/hembygd summer tap at the start. It is seasonal, not year-round.
No verified potable mid-stage water or Skyrshyttan water was found. Carry water before leaving Koppartorp; treat any natural water as unverified.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden lists stage 42 as 7 km, the 2025 long-distance pass lists 6.5 km, Naturkartan exposes about 6319 m, OSM relation 6575013 measures about 6.6 km, Äventyrligare 6.62 km, AllTrails 6.8 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 6.32 km. Use 7 km as the rounded official planning distance with a measured-line caveat.

Public metadata around stage 42 is inconsistent: OSM relation 6575013 has correct endpoints, stage tags and a 2025 update, while OSM-wiki/search snippets and external tables mix 6.3, 6.5, 7, or stale 10 km/0% values. Prefer Sörmlandsleden/Naturkartan/current local geometry for planning.

Main-route topology runs from Koppartorp/stage 41 to Skyrshyttan/stage 43. For route-builder stitching, snap to OSM node 2889617483 at 58.645025,16.900148 and OSM node 12765514559 at 58.676255,16.886758; local endpoints are close and the current local drawing is usable.
Koppartorp is also a hub for stage 37:2, Gruvslingan, Kummelbergsrundan, Simonberget options, and Tunabergsrundan context.

This is a culture-heavy mining and history stage through Tunaberg bergslag. Official route highlights include Tunabergs hembygdsgård, mine holes, Storgruvan, Kalkberget, Grishyttan, jättegrytor near Älvbro, viewpoints, ormgran/larch stand, Stora Jogershyttan, and old railway embankment toward Skyrshyttan.

Tunaberg-Koppartorp is a national-interest cultural environment for mining and works history, including cobalt, iron and copper mining, medieval smelting remains, and old road/industrial structures. Treat it as protected heritage context, not just scenery.

Old mining remains, mine holes, slag heaps, giant potholes, furnace sites, and old railway structures should be treated as look-but-do-not-disturb heritage and safety hazards. Storgruvan is reported as about 160 m deep and more than 400 m long; stay on marked paths and keep children/dogs close near mine holes.

No official reroute/fault report was found for stage 42 during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Place names appear stable: Koppartorp, Kalkberget, Grishyttan, Älvbro, Stora Jogershyttan/Stor-Jägershyttans gamla tomt, Skyrshyttan.

Team Vildmark, Nya Stigar, SPF and LoisansRundor reports support the stage-42/43 character: varied forest, paths, gravel roads, old crofts, mine areas, giant's kettles, old railway bed, wet grass in poor weather, and a useful Knaptorp bus access point. No credible stage-42-specific bad-marking report was found.

The stage is short but not entirely flat. User reports and AllTrails indicate small climbs, wet/high vegetation at times, knobbly terrain, roots/rock, and moderate ascent around Koppartorp-Kalkberget-Grishyttan and the mining landscape.

No shelter or designated campsite was found on stage 42. A stale user report mentioned an informal homemade rest shelter, likely for hunters; do not map it as official or dependable overnight infrastructure. Use allemansrätten only where appropriate and follow local signs; nearby Simonberget/Kummelberget reserve rules apply if combining with local loops.

The route may cross or edge cultivated/private land in places. Stay on marked trail/roads, do not spread out over fields/crops, avoid yards/private driveways, keep dogs close, and do not block forestry or farm access.

Fires should be limited to the prepared Koppartorp/Storgruvan rest area and only when current fire-ban rules allow it. Stricter bans can prohibit fixed grill places too, and fires should never be made on rock slabs or bedrock.

Kummelberget bird-protection closure and Simonberget tent/fire rules matter for nearby loop combinations: Kummelberget closed February 1-August 15; Simonberget tenting only between toilet and fireplace below the hill for max two nights.

sections.name: Stage 43: Skyrshyttan to Sandstugan
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 43, Skyrshyttan to Sandstugan.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Skyrshyttan is a weak car-access start: official text says there is no good parking at the stage start, perhaps only room for one roadside car.

Official start access is by bus from Nyköping/Nyköpings busstation to Munksäter/Munksätter, then about 15 minutes walking to Skyrshyttan. GTFS/OpenStreetMap spell the operational stop Munksätter; verify live Sörmlandstrafiken because rural service can be sparse.

Sandstugan has a bus stop essentially at the endpoint, but official stage 44 says there is no parking at Sandstugan. Svalstaskogen reserve parking about 1 km beyond Sandstugan is the practical mapped parking context if continuing or staging nearby.

Skyrshyttan-side access is on line 561, while Sandstugan-side access is listed on line 663 in GTFS-based data. A pure public-transport end-to-end day may require careful timing or transfer via Nyköping.
No verified toilet, shelter, campsite, grill/fireplace, shop, cafe, restaurant, or potable-water service was found directly on stage 43.
waterSources: No verified potable water, tap, spring, lake refill, or dependable natural source was found on stage 43. Carry water.
Do not attach stage 44 water points to stage 43 except as onward-planning context.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden and the 2025 long-distance passport list stage 43 as 6 km, while Naturkartan shows 5.9 km/5863 m, OSM relation 6575005 measures about 5.95 km despite a stale 5 km distance tag, Äventyrligare lists 5.8 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 5.77 km. AllTrails' roughly 4.7 km and Nya Stigar's 5.0 km values appear to be lower-confidence simplified/older logs.

Main-route topology runs from stage 42 at Skyrshyttan to stage 44 at Sandstugan. For route-builder stitching, snap to the OSM topology join at 58.676255,16.886758 for Skyrshyttan and 58.703434,16.874178 for Sandstugan; the local official-GPX drawing is close enough for display, with endpoint gaps around 20-40 m.

Stage 43 is easy/green but very service-light and not very wilderness-like as a standalone hike. Expect transport-style walking: old railway embankments, old spruce-plantation/clearcut areas, roughly 2 km forest road, roughly 2 km gravel road from Månstorp, and asphalt into Sandstugan.
The official page showed no current reported faults during the 2026-04-27 pass. Keep any older route-condition reports as historical caveats unless a current source confirms them.

Skyrshyttan has medieval iron/mining context and sits in the wider Tunaberg hytta/mining landscape, but official text says only scattered remains of a medieval bondehytta are visible. Treat remains as look-but-do-not-disturb cultural heritage.

A Team Vildmark report for stages 42/43 supports the practical character: varied forest, paths, gravel roads, old crofts/mining areas, giant's kettles, old railway bed, and final asphalt toward Sandstugan. Their mention of a homemade shelter should not be promoted as an official shelter or dependable rest resource.

A Nya Stigar 2015 note about dumped stone/aggregate near the Skyrshyttan-side end is historical only; no current confirmation was found and the official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass.
No stage-43-specific reserve restriction was found. Nearby Svalstaskogen rules belong primarily to stage 44 context, but matter if continuing beyond Sandstugan.

If continuing into Svalstaskogen on stage 44, reserve rules include no damaging living/dead trees, limited collection only of ordinary berries/edible mushrooms/personal flowers, organized camps require permission, and fires require bringing your own wood. Länsstyrelsen also warns about bark-beetle-damaged spruce/falling trees there, and stage 44 has a post-Sandstugan reroute for bark-beetle damage.
Check current Nyköping/Sörmlandskusten fire-ban status before using any fire on nearby stages; stricter fire bans can prohibit fixed grill places.

sections.name: Stage 44: Sandstugan to Lindbacke
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 44, Sandstugan to Lindbacke.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.

Sandstugan has a bus stop essentially at the start but official text says there is no parking at the stage start. Nearby backup stops include Visätter and Bråkarr; verify live Sörmlandstrafiken departures.
Practical car access is Svalstaskogen reserve parking near the early route, Ryssbergen/Skillerhultsvägen parking in the middle/late stage, or the Lindbacke/Gumsbacken shopping area near the end.
Ryssbergen is the main facility cluster with shelter, tap/drinking-water point, nearby toilet, viewpoints, and several access/parking options.
Lindbacke/Gumsbacken has shops and bus stops, and Nyköping C is the nearest rail anchor, roughly 1.3-1.5 km straight-line from the Lindbacke endpoint.
waterSources: Bergshammar spring after roughly 6.5 km is the first verified water point. It is a natural source, so filter/boil/treat unless current signage confirms potable water.
Ryssbergen tap/drinking-water point beside the shelter is the strongest refill on the stage, but still verify on site because taps can be seasonal or interrupted.
Svanviken/Lindbacke wetland and lakes are nature/bird habitat, not practical drinking-water sources.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden distance is 12 km, Naturkartan lists 12.0 km/11.8 km route geometry, Äventyrligare lists 11.42 km, OSM relation 3696304 measures about 12.15 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 12.13 km. Use 12 km as the catalog/planning distance.

Easy/green stage: forest edge/open views after Sandstugan, Hult/easy forest, more rolling forest, gravel-road sections, Kilaån context, Iron Age grave field and labyrinth, Stora Kungsladugården, and Lindbacke/Svanviken bird-rich pasture/wetland near the end.

Stage topology is busy: stage 36:3 joins from Fada/Bergshammar, 44:1 branches toward Oxelösund/Jogersö near Ryssbergen/Skillerhultsvägen, 44:2 branches from Stora Kungsladugården toward Hållet/stage 45 in Naturkartan/OSM and older official references, and the main route continues to stage 45 at Lindbacke. Show these as related options when the relevant main-route section is selected.

There is a naming/version caveat for 44:2: Stage 44 still references a Kungsladugården-Hållet connector, Naturkartan/OSM retain that longer connector, but the current official 44:2 URL resolves to the shorter 45:2 Blommenhof-Hållet route. Keep this visible so users do not accidentally plan the wrong connector.

Independent route audits confirmed clean joins: stage 43 ends at the stage 44 start, stage 44 ends at the stage 45 start, stage 36:3 joins stage 44 near Bergshammar, and stage 44:1 meets stage 44 near Ryssbergen/Skillerhultsvägen. For route-builder snapping, use OSM nodes 3198909965 at 58.703434,16.874178, 3223700234 at 58.744822,16.994087, 914036955 at 58.729103,16.911059, 3074881314 at 58.734840,16.955879, and legacy 44:2 node 1868989042 at 58.746109,16.968913.

Official text says the route has been rerouted shortly after Sandstugan because of bark-beetle damage. Svalstaskogen reserve also warns that dead spruce can fall; avoid dead-spruce areas in wind. The official stage page showed no separate reported faults during the 2026-04-27 verification pass.

Svalstaskogen reserve rules: do not damage living or dead trees, collect only ordinary berries/edible mushrooms/personal flowers, bring your own wood for any permitted fire, and get permission for organized camps/competitions.

Svanviken-Lindbacke reserve rules are strict: no tenting, no caravans, no fires, dogs leashed, do not disturb birdlife, and do not damage vegetation or ground. Länsstyrelsen currently warns that the Kilaån footbridge is closed as unsafe; older local reports already described worn bridge/boardwalk conditions and confusing lowland route choices.

Ryssbergen reserve rules found in this pass: dogs leashed on exercise/riding trails and no riding on prepared exercise tracks. No blanket Ryssbergen tent/fire ban was verified from the reserve source.
Ryssbergen water is well listed by official/OSM sources, but no independent hiker report verified year-round tap reliability. Treat both the tap and Bergshammar spring as verify-on-site water points.

Cattle may graze at Lindbacke in summer; local reports mention manure, stiles, fence crossings, ticks, mud, wet passages, and seasonal overgrowth as practical nuisances in the grazed/wet lowland areas. Use gates carefully, keep dogs controlled, and give animals space.

sections.name: Stage 44:1: Jogersö. Oxelösund to Ryssbergen
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 44:1, Jogersö. Oxelösund to Ryssbergen.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Oxelösunds kommun.

Jogersö Eco Camp/start area is the strongest start-service node with paid camping, toilets, showers, drinking water/service-house context, seasonal kiosk/small grocery, restaurant/lunch nearby, parking, and beach facilities.

Stjärnholm provides mid-route parking, bus access, and lodging/meal context; verify current Stiftsgården opening and meal arrangements before relying on it because food is more booked-guest/event oriented than guaranteed drop-in trail service. Older hiker reports also flag weak marking/heavy loose gravel around Stjärnholm/riding-path sections, so keep an offline map handy.

Ryssbergen is the endpoint facility cluster with shelter, tap/drinking-water point, nearby toilet, parking, viewpoint, and Ärilä bus access. The small Skillerhultsvägen parking is the main connection back to stage 44.

Public transport is useful but not door-to-door: Jogersövägen is the likely start bus approach, Stjärnholm/Stjärnholmsbadet are mid-route bailouts, Ärila serves the Ryssbergen side, and Nyköping C/Nyköping busstation are the broader rail/bus anchors.

Tempo Oxelösund Sundstigen is the closest proper start-side grocery to the trail corridor. ICA Kvantum Oxelösund and Nyköping/Gumsbacken services are useful town-service options but may be around the 2 km/off-route threshold depending on the selected route.
waterSources: Jogersö Eco Camp/start services and Stjärnholm can be refill/service options when open, but they are not wilderness water sources.

Kvarndammen/St Bene is a strong shelter/rest point, but no reliable official water was confirmed there. A 2018 hiker report found water at the dam dry, and a municipal near-nature source mentions a small spring near Kvarndammen that is not listed as a Sörmlandsleden stage water point; treat this whole area as carry-water territory.
The official spring before Ryssbergen at 58.735100, 16.968467 is the main natural water source. Filter/boil/treat unless current signage confirms potable water.
The Ryssbergen tap/drinking-water point beside the shelter is the best listed endpoint refill, but verify seasonality/function in the field.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden distance is 16.5 km after the July 2025 Jogersöbron-Femöre update; Naturkartan/older official-GPX geometry is about 15.8 km, OSM relation 9628430 measures about 16.1-16.2 km despite a stale 15 km tag, and AllTrails shows about 14.6-14.8 km. Use 16.5 km as the catalog distance and the OSM relation as the best current drawn line until a refreshed official GPX is available.

The route starts at Jogersö/Oxelösund, passes urban-edge paths and small roads, Stjärnholm/Stjärnholmsviken, Kvarndammen/St Bene, forest/ancient-remains areas, Bränn-Ekeby/Källbo, golf-course edges near Ärila/Nyköpings golf, Ryssbergen, and connects to stage 44 near Skillerhultsvägen.

Stage 44:1 is a branch/access route, not the stage-44 mainline. To continue toward Lindbacke, switch to stage 44 at the Ryssbergen/Skillerhultsvägen connection. Route-builder snapping should use the Stage 44 connection near OSM node 3074881314 at 58.734840,16.955879, not Lindbacke.

Official July 2025 update added/new-routed the Jogersöbron-Femöre part and opened a new Femöre shelter on 2025-07-09. The current drawing uses OSM relation 9628430, version 14 from 2025-12-25, because it postdates the reroute. The Arknat Hide&Seek shelter belongs clearly to the Femöre loop/extension context; do not stitch the full Femöre loop or shelter into the classic Jogersö-Ryssbergen line until official stage geometry confirms the exact extension.
Official 2026-04-20 comment reports forestry/thinning just south of Björshultsvägen, north of Stjärnholm; markings were improved, but the area may remain messy for a while.

Official stage page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 verification pass, aside from the 2026-04-20 forestry/thinning comment. Older hiker reports describe wet/muddy going around the Jogersö-Stjärnholm and post-Stjärnholm wetland/boardwalk sections, slippery descents after rain, poor marking around a riding/gravel section near Stjärnholm, high grass, and a confusing golf-course edge. Treat these as seasonal/condition-dependent but plausible.

A hiker report flagged awkward wayfinding around the Ärila/Nyköping golf-course edge, with high grass and a moment of uncertainty near tee/fairway context. Watch markers and local golf-course signs carefully.
Svanviken/Kilaån bridge warning near the Ryssbergen/Svanviken/Kastalen/Lindbacke area can affect nearby loops and continuations; use alternatives via Kastalen/Skillerhultsvägen where relevant.

Ryssbergen reserve rules found in the visitor source: dogs leashed on exercise/riding trails and riding forbidden on prepared exercise tracks. No blanket Ryssbergen tent/fire ban was verified, so apply allemansrätten, local signs, and current fire bans.
Svanviken-Lindbacke reserve rules are stricter for side trips/continuations: no tenting/caravans, no fires, dogs leashed, and do not disturb birdlife.

Femöre/Jogersö local rules matter near the start/extension: dogs may need to be leashed in bathing/exercise/recreation areas, disposable grills are not allowed at Jogersö Eco Camp, and overnight tenting is not allowed in Femöre reserve except where explicitly permitted.

sections.name: Stage 45: Lindbacke to Oppeby (via Nyköping)
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 45, Lindbacke to Oppeby (via Nyköping).
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Nyköping provides train/bus, cafes, hotels, groceries, toilets, and resupply, especially around Nyköpingshus, the bus station, Sörmlands museum, the harbour, central Nyköping, and Oppeby.
No official Sörmlandsleden shelter, campsite, or potable trail-water point was verified on stage 45 itself. Treat this as an urban day section and use town services during opening hours.

Default-map food/service markers should stay curated: show start/end groceries, central museum/castle/harbour/bus-station facilities, a few close cafes/restaurants, and keep dense central restaurant options searchable rather than all pinned by default.
waterSources: Use urban services rather than trail taps: museum/cafes/restaurants, groceries, public toilets with sinks, and possible harbour drinking-water points. Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water availability/quality.
A harbour-side OSM drinking-water point exists but is roughly 0.5-0.6 km off the main Stage 45 line and should be treated as seasonal/verify-on-site until field-confirmed.
The Ryssbergen tap/water point southwest of Lindbacke is around the 2 km/off-route edge for Stage 45 and belongs primarily to Stage 44/44:1 planning, not this urban stage.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 8 km; Naturkartan measures about 8.1 km/8,328 m and marks it green/easy, OSM relation 6575118 measures closer to 8.3 km despite a stale 10 km tag, Äventyrligare lists about 8.23 km, and the local official-GPX line is about 7.8 km. The route is an urban/river/park stage: Lindbacke shops, Oxelösundsvägen tunnel, Idbäck, Teaterparken, bus station, Hamnvägen, Nyköpingshus, Nyköpingsån/Åpromenaden, Hållet-Marieberg-Stenbro, E4 underpass, and Oppeby.

For route-builder snapping, use OSM node 3223700234 at 58.744822,16.994087 for the Stage 44/45 Lindbacke join, OSM node 4354585315 at 58.770413,16.974096 for the Stage 45/46/46:1 Oppeby join, OSM node 1816581778 at 58.748679,17.009761 for the 45:1 Nyköpingshus branch context, and OSM node 522418486 at 58.763651,16.999452 for the Hållet/legacy 44:2/45:2 context.

Official Sörmlandsleden stage page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Current local caveat: Nyköping resecentrum construction continues toward 2028; station-area access has changed, northern commuter parking and a pedestrian tunnel were permanently closed in March 2026, and Brunnsgatan/station-area works have planned closures in summer 2026 and week 44 2026 plus a longer partial closure planned in 2028. Follow live signs and municipal notices near Nyköping C, Brunnsgatan, the bus station, and Nyköpingsån.

Hållet-Marieberg-Stenbro reserve rules apply on the river/reserve part: dogs/cats/pets leashed, fires only at prepared fireplaces, no camping/camp activity without Nyköping municipality permission, do not disturb animals or breeding sites, and do not damage rock/stone/live or dead trees. Current 2025 reserve decision was appealed, but updated C-rules still apply.

Nyköping public-place rules restrict camping/tenting to designated areas such as Strandstuguviken, Örstig, and Västra Hamnsidan unless a police permit applies; do not present stage 45 as a wild-camping stage.

Fire status checked 2026-04-27: local rescue service did not show an active fire ban, but Länsstyrelsen pages showed a forest-fire-risk warning for Södermanland. Check live fire status before using even designated grills.
Nearby Svanviken/Lindbacke context: the Kilaån footbridge in Svanviken reserve is closed as unsafe, but this is a detour/adjacent warning rather than an official stage 45 closure.

Trip reports/blogs generally describe the first urban/industrial part from Lindbacke/Idbäck toward Nyköpingshus as functional and less scenic, while the Nyköpingsån/river, Storhusfallet, old buildings, cafes, Hållet mining-history signs, and Hållet green corridor are the pleasant part. Official/Naturkartan easy grading should override AllTrails' generic moderate label.

Wayfinding risk is mainly urban route-choice complexity around Nyköping's mainline, access routes, branches and loops: Stage 45 relates to 44, 45:1, 45:2, 46, 46:1, the older 44:2/Kungsladugården-Hållet connector, and local Lindbacke/Svanviken loops. Keep branch options separate and show them only when relevant.

sections.name: Stage 45:1: Nyköpingshus to Strandstugeviken
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 45:1, Nyköpingshus to Strandstugeviken.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Nyköpingshus/Nyköping harbour is the reliable start-service area, with city toilets, restaurants/cafes, museum/harbour services, buses, and Nyköping C within walking distance.

The rural/coastal part has few guaranteed public services. Strandstuvikens Havsbad & Camping is the main end-service node with paid camping, toilets/showers/service houses, fresh-water fill for guests, kiosk/shop and restaurant/bar seasonally. Dogs are not allowed on the main beach there, but the camping reports a dedicated dog-bathing area.

End transit is thinner than the start but appears better than older Naturkartan text: current best evidence points to line 2 toward Hasselbacksvägen/Örstig, still with an approach walk and live timetable checks. Older Strandstuviksvägen 3-4 km access and seasonal bad-bus notes should stay as fallbacks, not the only story.
Linudden/Örstig and Strandstuviken have parking/rest/birdwatching access points, but some are reserve, beach, camping, or Arnöhalvön-loop services rather than point-to-point Stage 45:1 services.
waterSources: No verified public potable-water source was found on the rural trail section.
The best city refill is an OSM-mapped harbour drinking-water point near Nyköping; treat it as seasonal/verify-on-site because it is not listed as an official trail water source.

Strandstuvikens camping has service houses with kitchen/showers/toilets and fresh-water filling by the large service house, but access is paid/guest/customer dependent and some food/kiosk/bar services are seasonal.
Kilaån, Stadsfjärden, the sea, and beach/bathing water are not drinking-water sources.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden and OSM relation metadata list stage 45:1 as 12 km. Naturkartan, AllTrails, Äventyrligare and RouteYou show 15-20 km variants, likely due to loop/route-variant handling around Arnöhalvön/Örstigsnäs/Näsudden; do not use those as the canonical stage distance.

The old generated app GeoJSON for 45:1 pointed west of Nyköping toward Fada/Palstorp, which did not match the named stage. The drawn line now uses a point-to-point extraction from the OSM 45:1 relation east/southeast toward Arnö, Linudden, and Strandstugeviken. It measures about 10.45 km and should be treated as best-current direct-stage geometry with 12 km official planning distance; the raw OSM relation members measure about 15.5 km because loop/variant geometry is included.

For route-builder snapping, use OSM node 1816581778 at 58.748679,17.009761 for the Stage 45/Nyköpingshus branch join and OSM/local endpoint node 9926221191 at 58.720582,17.091262 for the Strandstugeviken endpoint cluster. The beach/camping marker around 58.7204,17.0853 is nearby service context, not the route snap endpoint.

Route character: city/castle/harbour start, Kilaån/Stadsfjärden benches and views, Rosenhill/Karlslund/Branthäll, fenced grazing/coastal-meadow areas, Linudden nature reserve, coastal/bird-rich Strandstuviken, and beach/camping endpoint.

Official route text warns that fenced areas may contain grazing animals, usually cows. Reports confirm cattle on/near the route in the Karlberg/coastal-meadow area, including a 2024 comment about cows swimming in the sea. Keep distance, close gates, and leash dogs.

Wetness/mud is the recurring practical condition issue. AllTrails/user reports mention spring mud, July mud/bugs, and route-choice splits; Nya Stigar described parts around Mellanfjärden/Karlberg as overgrown, cattle-churned and muddy with tick risk, while also praising the marking through dense growth. Follow orange markings and carry an offline map.
Strandstuviken includes bird-protection areas closed to entry from 1 April to 30 September. Keep to marked routes/ramps and do not enter closed shore-meadow areas.

Strandstuviken and Örstigsnäs reserve fire rules restrict fires/grilling to manager-prepared places; disposable grills are prohibited. Gas/liquid-fuel stoves are allowed only if used safely and fire bans do not override. Strandstugeviken beach had excellent 2025 bathing-water classification for the 2026 season, but algae/cyanobacteria can still occur; check current bathing status before swimming.
Linudden reserve rules include dogs leashed, no damage to trees/plants, limited berry/mushroom/flower collection, and permission required for organized camps/competitions.

Gästabudet/Örstigsnäs shelter and Näsuddens beach facilities belong to the Arnöhalvön loop/eastern variant, not the simple point-to-point 45:1 endpoint. Show them as related loop options when the user selects the Linudden/Strandstuviken part, not as default point-to-point overnight services.

Frisksportartorpet/Stensborg is a useful rest/exercise/arboretum area and the official manager tip mentions a grill place there, but public access to water/toilets is not confirmed.
Lasarettet/Vårdcentral Åsidan, Trafikplats Hållet, and Nya Kyrkogården bus stops are useful access points; Nyköping C is the practical rail/bus anchor about a short walk from Blommenhof.
ICA Knuten/Oppeby and the Hållet traffic-junction food/fuel cluster are near-route resupply options, but they are urban detours rather than trail facilities.
waterSources: No verified free public potable-water point was found directly on the 1.9-2 km connector.
Frisksportartorpet event/club notes mention water by a sauna building, but this is not confirmed as an always-open public tap; mark as access-uncertain.
Use staffed/customer services such as Blommenhof, Nyköping C, Lasarettet/hospital area, Preem/Burger King, or Fåfängan when open. Natural water in Hållet/Nyköpingsån is not potable.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.
Official Sörmlandsleden lists this as stage 45:2, Blommenhof to Hållet, 2 km. The local route geometry is about 1.94 km and matches the official start/end well.

Naming/topology is messy: OSM/Naturkartan and some third-party sources often discuss the larger Kungsladugården-Hållet connector as 44:2, while the current official site exposes the Blommenhof-Hållet connector as 45:2. Keep this section as a short connector into stage 45.
Route character: short forest/urban connector via Frisksportartorpet/Stensborg, road crossings toward Katrineholm/Eskilstuna, E4 tunnel, and Hållet-Marieberg-Stenbro reserve paths.

Hållet-Marieberg-Stenbro reserve rules: dogs/pets leashed, no camping or camp activity without Nyköping municipality permission, fires only at prepared fireplaces, and no damage to trees/dead wood/rock/stone/cultural remains. Nyköping adopted a new reserve decision on 2025-11-11, but it was appealed; visitor C-rules still apply while the older decision otherwise remains in force.

Nyköping local public-place camping rules are restrictive: do not treat Blommenhof, Hållet, station-area parks, or urban public places as legal camping spots without a permit or a specifically designated campsite.

Official 45:2 page showed no current fault reports during this research pass. Nearby/relevant caveats: Nyköping resecentrum works can alter station-area approaches, and Trafikverket currently lists E4 Blommenhov bridge construction start as 2028; no current closure for the 45:2 E4 tunnel was found.

Fire status is dynamic: Sörmlandskustens räddningstjänst showed no formal fire ban during the research pass, but Länsstyrelsen still displayed fire-risk guidance. In the reserve, use only prepared fireplaces, and avoid all fires during a skärpt eldningsförbud.

sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 46, Oppeby to Vittenberga.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Söra scout area provides midpoint parking/access; Oppeby has nearby food and bus access; Vittenberga has bus/parking context via stage 47.

No official stage-46 toilet was verified. Naturkartan marks Söra-Hovrasjön as near toilet but did not expose an exact toilet pin; Nyköping C toilets are useful for train access but are more than 2 km from parts of this stage.
Oppeby torg has the cleanest food/resupply cluster for the start: ICA Knuten plus nearby pizzeria/cafe/sandwich options. Opening hours and exact businesses should be checked live.

Söra bus stop can be useful around the midpoint, and Vittenberga bus access appears to follow the sparse 667 Runtuna-Lid-Nyköping corridor. Use Sörmlandstrafiken live planning rather than hardcoded departures.
waterSources: Bergsstugan tap is the best verified refill and is listed as year-round in official material.

Hovrasjön/lake water is not quality-tested; Sörmlandsleden general guidance says lake water should be treated/boiled and cannot be guaranteed. A Komoot note reported Hovrasjön water as murky/filter-clogging, so prefer Bergsstugan.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.
Official distance is 8 km; Naturkartan measures about 7.7 km/7,685 m. Official/Naturkartan grade it easy/green; AllTrails' moderate label appears driven by calculated ascent/rooty sections.

Topology is clean: Naturkartan/official geometry and OSM relation 8426302 snap within a few metres at both ends. Use the Oppeby/Släbro hub around 58.770404,16.974075 for stages 45/46/46:1 and the Vittenberga hub around 58.808545,17.016173 for stages 46/47; keep 46:1 as a visible access branch rather than part of stage 46.

Official Sörmlandsleden page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass, and no current Nyköping municipal drift notice was found for Hovrasjön, Söra, Vittenberga, or the stage. Recent AllTrails reports in 2024-2025 also described good conditions.

Route character: starts at the foot/cycle bridge over Nyköpingsån, passes Trumpetarberget views, Hovrasjön shore, a floating/pontoon bridge toward Söra, and mixed road/forest walking to Vittenberga. Expect mostly firm easy paths, with isolated muddy/rooty sections after rain, especially north of Hagalund.

Good tenting is officially noted about 100 m south of Hovrasjön shelter. No intersecting nature reserve, Natura 2000, or Ramsar restriction was found for the Oppeby-Hovrasjön-Söra-Vittenberga corridor during the 2026-04-27 check, but allemansrätten, posted local rules, and leave-no-trace practice still apply.

The route passes local recreation/scout/preschool/horse-use areas around Hovrasjön, Söra and Berga. Expect mixed users, occasional horse context, and possible hunting activity in autumn; keep dogs under strict control and wear visible colors in hunting season.

Fire status is time-sensitive. Nyköping/Sörmlandskustens räddningstjänst showed no current fire ban during the research pass, but users must check live fire-ban and fire-risk status before using any fireplace. Ordinary bans and stricter bans differ, and Sörmlandsleden does not supply firewood at shelters.
Fishing is not covered by allemansrätten. Treat Nyköpingsån, Hovrasjön, and other freshwater along the stage as permit/check-before-fishing areas.

sections.name: Stage 46:1: Skavsta flygplats to Släbro, etapp 46
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 46:1, Skavsta flygplats to Släbro, etapp 46.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Skavsta terminal has toilets, bus/coach access, Pressbyrån/light food, and other commercial airport services; terminal hours and customer access apply.
Airport terminal curb/road access is controlled: use signed airport parking/drop-off or the official F11/Moder Jord stage parking, not roadside stopping in the airport area.
F11/Moder Jord has official 24h free parking by the museum/viewpoint area; distinguish this from paid airport parking.
The Oppeby/Släbro end has local bus access and ICA Supermarket Knuten about 1 km away for reliable resupply.
waterSources: No confirmed public drinking-water tap, shelter, fireplace, or formal campsite was found on this 5.5 km access connector.
Skavsta has toilets and food/drink sales, but no official drinking fountain/refill point was confirmed. Treat airport water as customer/paid-service access unless verified on site.
Use Skavsta terminal/commercial services before starting, ICA Knuten after the end, or continue onto stage 46 to the official year-round Bergsstugan tap.
Nyköpingsån is scenery, not a verified potable source; treat/boil any natural water and prefer carried water here.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Access connector from Skavsta/F11 to the Oppeby/Släbro junction with stage 46. Official distance is 5.5 km; local drawn geometry is about 5.1 km and matches the official endpoints closely. Naturkartan embedded text around 4.2 km and older community tables around 4.0 km appear to be stale distance noise rather than a different route.

Topology: model 46:1 as an optional airport access branch into the shared Oppeby/Släbro hub, not as the main continuation after stage 45. OSM relation 6575251 draws continuously; its end shares the same hub as stages 45 and 46 around 58.770413,16.974096. Use official 58.783767,16.925350 for displayed start metadata, while OSM routable geometry begins about 17 m away.

Expect easy but exposed walking: airport/service-road context, open farmland, asphalt/roadside sections, then the south bank of Nyköpingsån. D 627/Skavstarondellen sections can feel traffic-heavy and have limited shoulder.

User reports describe the Skavsta-road part as more practical connector than destination hike, with Moder Jord/F11 and the Nyköpingsån/Släbro heritage area as the rewarding parts. After rain or in high summer, expect wet grass and nettles along the river path.

The Släbro end is culturally sensitive, with runestones, rock carvings, grave-field/old crossing context, and bridge remains. Stay on paths and do not step on or touch carving surfaces; do not chalk, paint, rub, clean, scratch, climb on, move, dig around, or otherwise alter ancient remains.

No current official fault report, route closure, or municipal Skavsta/F11/Oppeby/Släbro traffic notice affecting the route was found on 2026-04-27. Long-term Skavsta/Ostlänken rail and station works are a dynamic access watch item, not a current route closure.
