facilities.name: Stage 46:1 camping restriction
facilities.description: Nyköping public-place camping rules are restrictive, and this connector crosses airport, road, farmland and heritage contexts. Do not camp at Skavsta, Släbro, public parks/places, road verges, fields or heritage surfaces.

facilities.name: Dog control on Stage 46:1
facilities.description: From 1 March to 20 August dogs must be under strict control where wildlife may be present; Nyköping also requires leash in several public-place contexts. Keep dogs close around roads, heritage sites and Oppeby parks.

facilities.name: Stage 46:1 fire-risk check
facilities.description: No fireplace is confirmed on this connector, and fires should not be made at Släbro heritage surfaces. No formal fire ban was found on 2026-04-27, but fire bans/fire risk change quickly; check Nyköping/Sörmlandskustens before any fire use elsewhere.

sections.name: Stage 47: Vittenberga to Svärta kyrka
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 47, Vittenberga to Svärta kyrka.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Vittenberga has bus access and possible small parking at the forest-road entrance; verify signs and live departures.
Svärta has the closest end-side bus stop by the stage junction, while Svärta kyrka has seasonal water, an access-dependent toilet, parking, and church-area transit about 0.4-0.6 km from the trail.
No active food/resupply was confirmed on or within practical range of stage 47. Older Åstugan cafe listings appear closed/outdated; use adjacent-stage logistics such as Oppeby/Nyköping or Tystberga.
waterSources: No reliable mid-stage drinking-water source was found. Carry water from the start.

The only verified refill is the seasonal summer tap at Svärta kyrka, about 20 m left of the church gate per official stage 48 notes; Swedish Church cemetery guidance says taps normally run roughly week 17 to week 40, and a 2025 comment reported the Svärta tap running on May 1. Verify season and current availability.
No lake or stream refill is apparent on this short stage, and Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee natural-water quality.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.
Official distance is 6 km; Naturkartan shows about 5.8 km and the local drawn route is about 5.4 km with endpoints close to official coordinates.

Geometry caveat: Naturkartan/official GPX line is the best display source for the user-facing Stage 47 endpoint near Svärta kyrka/parking, ending around 58.819854,17.080987. OSM relation 7449377 stops around 58.817581,17.078367, about 295 m earlier at the road/stage-48 handoff, so pure OSM builders need to add the church approach or label the shorter handoff carefully.

Easy forest terrain with small rocky rises, mixed path/gravel-road walking, and short road sections near Vittenberga and the Svärta finish. Hiker reports describe a brief steeper climb just after the Vittenberga road crossing and quite a bit of gravel-road walking.

Wreta/Vreta, the former miner dwelling, Vreta gruva, and remnants of De sjungande stenarna are heritage context near the late-stage road section rather than staffed facilities. Keep to the marked route around private property and old mining remains.

Current official page showed no reported faults during the 2026-04-27 research pass. Recent hiker reports still mention high grass/clearing needs in places, young managed forest, road traffic on narrow gravel roads, and autumn elk-hunting activity.

AllTrails and hiker reports generally rate this as easy rather than a highlight stage: short, connective, and culturally interesting, but with managed forest/clear-cut character and meaningful gravel/road walking.

The endpoint named Svärta kyrka is functionally the Svärta road/stage junction, not the church door. Church parking, seasonal tap, toilet and bus-stop context sit about 350-500 m north/east of the stage junction and should not be used to extend the route geometry.

Svärtaån downstream is Natura 2000 with 100 m strandskydd and protected watercourse values. Ordinary walking on the marked route is not a special restriction, but avoid disturbing the watercourse/shore and do not treat the area as a campsite or service zone.

facilities.name: Vittenberga stage 47 start
facilities.description: Official stage start; connects from stage 46. Possible parking east of the road at the forest-road entrance, but verify signs and do not block access.

facilities.name: Vittenberga bus stop
facilities.description: Closest start-side Sörmlandstrafiken stop, roughly 100-150 m from the stage start. Service can be sparse; verify live departures.

facilities.name: Vittenberga opposite-direction bus stop
facilities.description: Opposite-side Vittenberga stop context; no shelter mapped. Verify live Sörmlandstrafiken departures and road crossing.

facilities.name: Vittenberga possible parking
facilities.description: Official text says possible parking on the east side of the road at the forest-road entrance. Treat as small/unsigned parking context until signs are checked.

facilities.name: Vittenberga road/crossing caution
facilities.description: Rural road access and a short initial climb after the road crossing; walk visibly and use care on road sections. Recent reports describe this as the only notably awkward climb.

facilities.name: Stage 47 high grass / clearing watch
facilities.description: A July 2025 trip report found some parts needed clearing and high grass hid foot placement. Conditions vary seasonally; watch footing in summer growth.

facilities.name: Bergtorp private-road context
facilities.description: Blogs mention passing a farm/garden area. Private property context only; stay on marked route/road.

facilities.name: Stavstugan / private torp context
facilities.description: Old torp/farmstead context noted in a 2025 trip report. Private/camera-sign context was reported; keep to the trail.

facilities.name: Wreta / De sjungande stenarna remnants
facilities.description: Approximate route-side cultural marker. Former psalm-stone culture park near Wreta/Vreta; major stones were reportedly moved or sold in 2016, while blogs note remnants.

facilities.name: Wreta private-property context
facilities.description: Wreta/Vreta gård and former parsonage context is private/view-from-route material, not a facility. Stay on the marked trail and roads.

facilities.name: Vretastugan / former miner dwelling
facilities.description: Approximate late-stage heritage context for the former miner dwelling mentioned by Sörmlandsleden near the end of the stage. Historic mine holes/remains occur in the wider Vreta/Svärta area; keep to the marked trail.

facilities.name: Vreta gruva / old mine caution
facilities.description: Approximate old mine-remains context near the Svärta finish. Old sources and local reporting note deep mine-hole hazards in the wider area; do not explore shafts or fenced/posted remains.

facilities.name: Old Riksettan / road-walk caution
facilities.description: Blogs report a short old-road/road-223 approach before the Svärta finish and occasional fast vehicles on narrow gravel-road sections. Use care with traffic.

facilities.name: Svärta stage junction
facilities.description: Stage 47 end and stage 48 start at the Svärta road/stage junction. Despite the stage name, this is not at the church door; church services are a short offset.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka user-facing endpoint
facilities.description: Naturkartan/official-GPX Stage 47 endpoint and Stage 48 shared church/parking-side point. OSM stage 47 stops about 295 m southwest at the road handoff, so keep this caveat visible in topology/debug views.

facilities.name: Svärta bus stop
facilities.description: Closest end-side bus stop, very near the stage junction. Avoid hardcoding old line numbers; verify live departures with Sörmlandstrafiken.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka bus stop
facilities.description: Alternative church-side stop about 0.5 km from the stage end and close to the water/church area; verify current service.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka
facilities.description: Medieval church with 1200s origins, later restorations, and kyrkligt kulturminne status. Useful landmark near the stage end; church access and services can depend on opening/events.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka summer tap
facilities.description: Official seasonal water tap, about 20 m left of the church gate per stage 48; a 2025 comment reported it running on May 1 and cemetery taps normally run roughly week 17-40. Verify season.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka toilet
facilities.description: OSM-mapped toilet at/near the church, and church history mentions a toilet built into the entrance area. Treat as church/cemetery-hours dependent, not guaranteed 24/7.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka access and respect
facilities.description: Active church/churchyard area. Interior access, toilet availability and water can depend on season, opening and services; be quiet around ceremonies and keep dogs leashed on churchyard areas.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka parking
facilities.description: Church-area parking about 350-400 m north/east of the stage junction; verify signs and event restrictions.

facilities.name: Svärtaån Natura 2000 / strandskydd context
facilities.description: Near the Svärta end/downstream corridor, Svärtaån is Natura 2000 with 100 m strandskydd. Ordinary marked-trail walking is fine, but avoid shore disturbance and do not treat the watercourse edge as a campsite/service area.

facilities.name: Stage 47 hunting-season visibility
facilities.description: A November hiker report encountered active elk hunting. In autumn, wear visible colors, respect signs and hunters, and be prepared for temporary local activity.

facilities.name: Stage 47 fire-risk check
facilities.description: No fireplace was verified on this stage. No formal fire ban was found on 2026-04-27, but status changes quickly; check Nyköping/Sörmlandskustens before any fire or stove use.

sections.name: Stage 48: Svärta kyrka to Holmsjön
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 48, Svärta kyrka to Holmsjön.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun.
Svärta/Svärta kyrka has the practical start services: bus stops near the stage junction and church, simple church-area parking, an access-dependent church toilet, and a seasonal summer tap.

Masugnsjön is the main on-stage overnight/rest node, with an official shelter, fireplace, and dry toilet on the lakeside rock slab. It is shared/first-come and should not be treated as stocked: no guaranteed firewood and no trash service.

Holmsjön endpoint has no confirmed parking, toilet, shop, or direct transit. Plan pickup carefully or continue to stage 49; the nearest researched bus options are back toward Borrvinds kvarn/Åbro vägskäl or onward toward Tystberga.
No reliable active food, lodging, or resupply was found on stage 48 itself. Older Åstugan cafe references are closed/outdated; Tystberga services are next-stage and over 2 km away.
waterSources: The only verified drinking-water refill is the seasonal summer tap at Svärta kyrka, about 20 m left of the church gate; verify season and current availability.
Masugnsjön and Holmsjön are natural surface-water options only. Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality, so filter/boil/treat if used and carry enough water from Svärta.

No mid-stage public tap, shop, or all-season drinking-water point was found. Team Vildmark-style multi-stage planning notes reinforce carrying enough water or a filter if continuing beyond the start tap.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 8 km; Naturkartan measures 7.8 km/7,779 m and the local drawn geometry is about 7.81 km with endpoints close to official coordinates. OSM relation metadata may still show 9 km; treat that as stale legacy tagging, not a reroute.

Topology is clean when OSM relation 7449355 is assembled by shared endpoints rather than raw member order: OSM measures about 7.814 km, starts within 2 m of official 58.817583,17.078333, and ends at 58.829213,17.165855, about 22 m from the official Stage 49/Holmsjön start cluster.
Main-route stage from Svärta kyrka/stage 47 to Holmsjön/stage 49. Expect mixed road, forest road, and hillier forest path, with several road sections before the Masugnsjön/Holmsjön finish.

The stage is unusually strong on mining and ironworks history: Svärta gård/Norshammars bruk, Borrvinds kvarn, Ullabergs masugn, a possible side trip to Förola gruva, and older smelting remains by Masugnsjön.

Hiker/blog reports describe quite a lot of road walking, old E4/Riksettan/E4 noise, and some forestry/clearcut/open sections, but the Masugnsjön shore and shelter area as the scenic high point. A local walking report notes that the old A1/Svärtaån corridor can be narrow and wet, which explains why some road walking is structural rather than a temporary detour.

Terrain is not technically hard but has concentrated rolling/hillier parts and a steeper leafy Svärta-side climb. After rain, wet leaves and ordinary lowland dampness can make slopes and forest-machine/forestry sections less tidy.

No current official fault reports or closure notices were found on 2026-04-27 for Svärta, Masugnsjön, the E4 wildlife tunnel, or Holmsjön. Ostlänken/E4 works around Holmsjön are a future monitoring item, not a current route change. Fire status is dynamic; check Nyköping/Sörmlandskustens current fire-ban page before using the Masugnsjön fireplace.

Holmsjön is a weak logistics endpoint: no parking or close public transport was verified at the stage end. Plan pickup carefully, backtrack to road-corridor stops, or continue toward Tystberga on stage 49.

facilities.name: Svärta stage junction
facilities.description: Official stage 48 start and stage 47 end along road 223 near Svärta kyrka.

facilities.name: Svärta bus stop
facilities.description: Closest start-side Sörmlandstrafiken stop by the stage junction. Older route references mention 555/655; current service may be mainly 655/656 or school-day patterns, so verify live departures.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka bus stop
facilities.description: Alternative church-side stop about 0.5 km from the start and near the water/church area; verify current service.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka
facilities.description: Medieval church with 1200s origins; Sörmlandsleden notes the first Swedish confirmation was held here in 1736 by Jakob Serenius.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka summer tap
facilities.description: Official summer tap about 20 m left of the church gate; seasonal and should be verified before relying on it.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka toilet
facilities.description: OSM-mapped toilet at/near the church; not listed by Sörmlandsleden for this stage, so treat as locally verified/access-dependent rather than guaranteed 24/7.

facilities.name: Svärta kyrka parking
facilities.description: Simple church-area parking roughly 350 m from the stage start per official/Naturkartan notes. Verify signs and event restrictions.

facilities.name: Svärta gård / Norshammars bruk context
facilities.description: Historic ironworks landscape near the old E4 corridor. The main building is private/not a public trail facility.

facilities.name: Åstugan cafe closed/outdated listing
facilities.description: Older maps/blogs may mention Åstugan cafe near the Svärtaån/old-road corridor, but current cafe listings mark it closed. Do not rely on food or toilet service here.

facilities.name: Svärtaån / old A1 road-walk caution
facilities.description: Road-walk and narrow/wet-edge caution. A local walking report notes the Svärtaån corridor was too narrow and waterlogged for the trail to fit beside the road in places.

facilities.name: Åbro vägskäl bus access
facilities.description: Road-corridor bus stop near the early/mid-stage heritage corridor. Useful bailout/access context; verify live departures.

facilities.name: Borrvinds kvarn bus stop
facilities.description: Mapped bus stop on the road corridor near the Borrvinds kvarn context; also one of the closest transit options to the Holmsjön end, but still not close.

facilities.name: Borrvinds kvarn opposite bus stop
facilities.description: Opposite-side Borrvinds kvarn stop on the same road corridor. Useful bailout context only if live service matches the trip.

facilities.name: Borrvinds kvarn / Hedvigsfors context
facilities.description: Heritage context near where cannon blanks from the local blast furnaces were bored using water power; no public service verified.

facilities.name: Ullabergs masugn
facilities.description: Visible blast-furnace remains with dams and information on site; good rest/interpretive stop. Historic sources date the furnace to 1761 and use into the 1800s.

facilities.name: Förola gruva side-trip context
facilities.description: Optional mining-history detour from the official route area. Coordinate is approximate and visitor-safe access should be verified; do not treat mine remains as a facility.

facilities.name: Masugnsskogen nature reserve side trip
facilities.description: Off-route reserve about 1 km north of the trail with difficult unmarked old forest and fallen trees; show as side-trip context, not as an on-stage facility.

facilities.name: Masugnsskogen reserve rules
facilities.description: Off-route reserve rules prohibit camping and fires; dead and fallen trees are protected habitat and should be left in place. Länsstyrelsen also notes bark-beetle-damaged trees, so watch for falling-tree risk.

facilities.name: Masugnsjön forest-road climb
facilities.description: After Ullabergs masugn the route follows forest road and more uneven/hillier forest terrain toward Masugnsjön. Expect possible forestry/open clearcut feel rather than continuous old forest.

facilities.name: Masugnsjön shelter
facilities.description: Official shelter after about 7 km, on a larger rock slab with views over Masugnsjön. Shared, first-come shelter; no booking, no trash bins, and do not assume firewood.

facilities.name: Masugnsjön shelter fireplace
facilities.description: Official text confirms a good fireplace at the Masugnsjön shelter. Use only when current fire-ban and local fire-risk rules allow; Sörmlandsleden does not supply firewood and nearby reserve dead wood must not be collected.

facilities.name: Masugnsjön dry toilet
facilities.description: OSM and official text confirm a toilet at/near the Masugnsjön shelter area.

facilities.name: Masugnsjön lake water
facilities.description: Lake water only, not a verified potable source. Filter/boil/treat if used; shoreline access may be awkward/steep and washing or toilet needs should stay well away from the shore.

facilities.name: Wildlife tunnel under E4
facilities.description: The final approach passes through a wildlife/hiker tunnel under the motorway before reaching Holmsjön. Do not attempt to cross E4 at grade; expect traffic noise and keep to the marked route.

facilities.name: Holmsjön stage junction
facilities.description: Official stage 49 start and stage 48 end at Holmsjön's northwest tip. No parking is confirmed at this endpoint.

facilities.name: Holmsjön OSM chain snap
facilities.description: OSM relation 7449355 ends here and Stage 49 begins here exactly; this is about 22 m from the official/Naturkartan Holmsjön start cluster. Merge these for route-builder continuity.

facilities.name: Holmsjön lake water
facilities.description: Natural lake water at the endpoint only; not a tested drinking-water source. Treat/filter/boil if used.

facilities.name: Holmsjön access caveat
facilities.description: No parking is listed at the Holmsjön stage start/end and no close transit stop was verified. Arrange pickup, walk back to road-corridor stops, or continue toward Tystberga on stage 49.

facilities.name: Stage 48 OSM distance caveat
facilities.description: Official/Naturkartan/local geometry agree on about 7.8-8 km. OSM relation metadata may still show 9 km and should be treated as stale tagging.

facilities.name: Holmsjön / Ostlänken future works watch
facilities.description: Trafikverket Ostlänken/E4 planning includes future work around Holmsjön and a friluftspassage near the existing E4 passage. No current route closure was found on 2026-04-27; recheck when construction changes.

facilities.name: Tystberga trafikplats bus access
facilities.description: Off-route transit context for onward planning from Holmsjön/stage 49, not a stage-48 endpoint stop. Mark as distant/off-route if shown.

facilities.name: Stage 48 fire-risk check
facilities.description: The Masugnsjön fireplace is the only verified fire point on stage 48. No formal fire ban was found on 2026-04-27, but status changes quickly; check Nyköping/Sörmlandskustens current fire-ban status before use.

sections.name: Stage 49: Holmsjön to Bälinge kyrka
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 49, Holmsjön to Bälinge kyrka.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Tystberga.

Holmsjön has no listed parking at the stage start and no close direct transit. Naturkartan/OSM place a shelter and dry toilet at the Holmsjön/Masugnsjön shelter cluster just west of the start, useful as start-side or stage-48 arrival context.
Tystberga is the practical service hub: Coop, restaurants, bus stops, parking, recycling-point context, and nearby paid lodging. Shop and food access are opening-hour or app/BankID dependent.
Bälinge kyrka has user-reported outdoor taps and toilet, nearby road/bus access at Bällinge vägskäl, and parking context at the church/end area. Treat the taps/toilet as likely but comment-sourced.
waterSources: No reliable public drinking-water source was found at Holmsjön or mid-stage before Tystberga. Carry water from stage 48/Svärta or treat natural water.

Coop/restaurants in Tystberga can provide practical resupply when open, but they are commercial/customer services. The Coop hybrid 24-hour model depends on phone, app/Scan & Pay, Mobile BankID, and current access rules.
Outside Bälinge kyrka, a 2024 official-page user comment reports water taps and a toilet. Treat as high-value but still verify season/access locally.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 11 km; Naturkartan measures 10.8 km/10,853 m, current OSM relation 7449352 measures about 10.863 km, and the local drawn route is about 10.815 km with endpoints close to official coordinates.

OSM relation 7449352 is a clean single-component through-line. It snaps exactly to Stage 48 at 58.829213,17.165855 and Stage 50 at 58.843621,17.295508, while the official/local endpoint clusters are nearby aliases: Holmsjön differs by about 5-22 m and Bälinge by about 21-59 m depending on source.

Easy main-route stage from Holmsjön/stage 48 to Bälinge kyrka/stage 50, mostly open landscape, private/minor roads, forest road, short forest sections, Tystberga village, school/sports-area paths, and church approach road. Current OSM geometry is road-heavy rather than deep-forest trail.
Official notes warn that cattle can occur in summer. Close gates, keep dogs controlled, and do not cross private yards or cultivated land outside the marked route.

Team Vildmark, Nya Stigar, and a 2025 hiker blog all describe extensive road/gravel-road walking, E4 noise around Sättra/Holmsjön, open agricultural walking, and easy terrain. The stage is fast and logistically useful because Tystberga has resupply and accommodation, but it is not a wilderness-service stage.
A 2025 hiker report says some markings needed repainting or replacement and a few posts/signs were lying down or hidden. Treat as a maintenance-watch note, not a formal closure.

No current official fault reports were shown on the official stage page during this research pass. No shelter, fireplace, or campsite was verified on the forward stage 49 line beyond the Holmsjön shelter cluster at/behind the start.

Ostlänken Sillekrog-Sjösa planning affects the Sättra-Holmsjön corridor and future rail construction is expected to require route attention/rerouting. No current Sörmlandsleden stage-49 reroute notice was found on 2026-04-27.

facilities.name: Sättra road barrier access caveat

sections.name: Stage 50: Bälinge kyrka to Bråfalls såg
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 50, Bälinge kyrka to Bråfalls såg.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Nynäs.
Bälinge kyrka is the practical start service point, with parking, nearby bus at Bällinge vägskäl, and user-reported church taps/toilet.

Bråfalls såg has parking, a picnic/rest shelter, heritage saw context, and a nearby Sörmlandstrafiken stop. OSM/secondary sources add toilet, bin, and fireplace context, but these are not all official stage-listed facilities.

The stage has no shop, cafe, or verified potable water between Bälinge and Bråfalls. Seasonal Bälinge Sommarkyrkan cafe and off-route lodging exist nearby only when open/booked; use Bälinge/Tystberga or plan onward to Nynäs services.
waterSources: Bälinge kyrka water/toilet reports are comment-sourced from the Stage 49 page rather than an official maintained Stage 50 facility listing. Treat them as useful but not guaranteed; verify season/access locally.
No reliable mid-stage drinking-water source was found. The small creek before the Bråfalls/50:1 split is natural water only and should be treated if used.
Bråfalls såg has toilet/rest access but no verified drinking-water tap.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 6 km; Naturkartan measures 5.7 km/5,735 m, AllTrails lists about 5.6 km, OSM relation 6567461 measures about 5.697 km despite a stale 7 km tag, and the local official-GPX-derived route is about 5.954 km with perfect internal snaps to stages 49, 51, and 50:1.

Stage 50 has source-coordinate alias clusters rather than separate trailheads: official start 58.843550,17.295850 is about 38 m from the local Stage 49/50 snap and about 21 m from the OSM Stage 49/50 snap; official Stage 51/Bråfalls start is about 13 m from the local Stage 50 end and about 4 m from the OSM Stage 50/51 snap.

The first roughly 3 km are on larger and smaller roads through open agricultural landscape; then the route enters Ramdalsskogen and the northern part of Nynäs nature reserve with hillier forest walking. Hiker reports describe the forest part as steep in places with rope assists and stable boardwalks near the stream.
At the signed split near the creek, the main route turns south/right to Bråfalls såg and Nynäs, while branch 50:1 continues toward Björken and stage 54.

Nynäs reserve rules matter here: overnighting in tent, hammock, wind shelter, caravan or camper is only allowed at designated places, fires/grilling only at prepared fireplaces managed by the reserve and only with provided wood, disposable grills are forbidden, and disturbing wildlife or damaging vegetation/dead wood is prohibited.

A 2025 official-page comment mentions poor marking toward Bälinge and rerouting connected to bark-beetle damage, but the official Stage 50 page itself shows no current fault report. Treat this as a navigation caution near the 50/50:1 area; the confirmed active bark-beetle reroute belongs to branch 50:1 and may not match stored GPX/OSM geometry.
Bråfalls is best treated as a rest shelter/picnic shelter, not a guaranteed overnight shelter. No designated Stage 50 campsite was verified.

facilities.name: Bälinge churchyard rule
facilities.description: Treat the churchyard as a quiet memorial place: use paths/parking, avoid disturbing services/funerals, keep dogs controlled and away from graves, and do not picnic or camp on churchyard grounds.

facilities.description: Seasonal church cafe context with summer opening windows reported by the parish. Verify current-year dates and hours before relying on it.

facilities.name: Stage 50 early asphalt traffic
facilities.description: A 2024 hiker report describes a short early asphalt section that can have traffic before quieter gravel-road walking. Use traffic care.

facilities.name: Grinda farm landscape
facilities.description: The route passes Grinda at a distance; official text notes the farm's old Carolinian-style building. Private landscape context only.

facilities.name: Ramdalsskogen / Nynäs reserve entry
facilities.description: The stage enters hillier forest and crosses into Nynäs nature reserve. Reserve rules override ordinary assumptions about camping, fire, plants and wildlife.

facilities.description: A 2025 official-page user comment reports poor marking toward Bälinge and mentions a bark-beetle reroute, but no official Stage 50 fault report was found. Keep map/GPS handy; confirmed active bark-beetle reroute belongs to 50:1.

facilities.name: Bälingedalen viewpoint ridge

facilities.description: In Nynäs reserve, tent/hammock/camper overnighting is only allowed at designated places, generally max one night; fire/grill only at reserve-managed fireplaces with provided wood. Bråfalls rastskydd is not a designated campsite in the researched sources.

facilities.description: Seasonal/off-stage services around Nynäs slott, including visitor information, food/contact services, toilets/RWC context, parking, and nearby STF Bränneriet lodging. More than 2 km from Stage 50; use only if continuing onto Stage 51/Nynäs.

facilities.name: STF Bränneriet distant lodging
facilities.description: Booked lodging near Nynäs slott/Stage 51-52, not a Stage 50 service. More than 2 km from Stage 50; useful only for onward itinerary planning.

facilities.name: Stage 50 fire-risk check
facilities.description: No fireplace was verified on the stage 50 core line. In Nynäs reserve, use only designated managed fireplaces and check current fire-ban status.

sections.name: Stage 50:1: Frillingmossen, etapp 50 to Sjön Björken, etapp 54
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 50:1, Frillingmossen, etapp 50 to Sjön Björken, etapp 54.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Nynäs, Trosa kommun.
This is a branch connector between stage 50 at Frillingmossen and stage 54 at sjön Björken; it is part of the Nynäs Runt loop, not a continuation from Bråfalls såg.

Bråfalls såg is nearby start/access context within about 0.4-0.9 km of the connector, with parking, rest shelter, toilet, bus, and sparse waste/fireplace caveats. Månbacken is nearby end/access context about 1.1-1.4 km from the connector endpoint, with parking/bus/toilet and booked lodging.
Björken has a shelter/fireplace/toilet/bathing area on stage 54 about 0.4 km from the 50:1 endpoint. No shop, cafe, or verified drinking-water tap was found on the connector itself.
waterSources: No reliable drinking-water source was found on 50:1. Carry water from Bälinge/Tystberga/Nynäs or other planned services.

Stora Frillingen, Lilla Frillingen, and Björken are natural lake water only; treat/filter/boil if used and avoid moving untreated water or wet gear between lakes because of crayfish-plague precautions in the Björken area.

Månbackestugorna should not be treated as a water source; hiker/lodging context says guests should bring drinking water. The nearest later official tap in this part of the system is the stage-54 pump near Gisekvarn, far beyond Björken and with quality caveats.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official and Naturkartan distance is 4 km. The local drawn line is about 3.5 km because it starts at the official Frillingmossen fork and runs to Björken; Naturkartan's roughly 4.0 km geometry starts from Bråfalls-side access context. Keep 4 km for planning.

OSM relation 9627989 is the correct 50:1 relation and measures about 3.56 km from Frillingmossen to the Stage 54 corridor near Sjön Björken. Do not model 50:1 as starting at Bråfalls såg, even though Bråfalls is a useful nearby access node.

Light forest connector through Frillingön between two wetland/myr areas and the lakes Stora and Lilla Frillingen, then toward sjön Björken. Hiker reports describe it as one of the prettier short links in this area, with mossy forest, rock, lake views, and useful Nynäs Runt loop-building value.

The official page still shows a fault notice: the temporary reroute remains current because bark-beetle damage makes trees fall easily, especially from the Frillingen guestbook pulpit toward the reroute. Follow orange tape and posted reroute maps on site, and avoid lingering under dead spruce, especially in wind.

Naturkartan publishes a separate temporary-reroute object for 50:1, about 1.0 km long, starting near 58.846847,17.364865 and rejoining near 58.853438,17.372180. The reroute start is on the stored 50:1 line, but the rejoin is about 0.5 km east of the stored 50:1/Björken connector and snaps near Stage 54; show it as active alternate/hazard geometry rather than pretending the stored line is current all the way.

A 2024 user comment on Månbacken runt said the northern part of 50:1 was barely passable but that an alternative route existed. Treat this as anecdotal support for taking the official reroute seriously.

A midpoint rest cliff by Stora Frillingen has a guestbook pulpit. Official steward notes and a 2020 hiker report also mention a wild-boar wallow/spa mid-stage; treat it as wildlife habitat, not an attraction to enter.

The route is in/near Nynäs nature reserve. Reserve rules restrict overnighting to designated places and fires/grilling to reserve-managed fireplaces with provided wood; do not assume wild camping or informal fires are allowed. Fishing is prohibited in Stora Frillingen, Lilla Frillingen, Björken, and Gisesjön inside the reserve, and wet gear should be cleaned/dried/disinfected before moving between lakes because of crayfish-plague risk.

Follow orange tape and posted maps; walked distance and topology may differ from the drawn base line.

facilities.description: Lake water only. Stage 54 notes good bathing but also warns to read crayfish-plague information so it is not spread via wet gear between lakes.

facilities.name: Björken / Frillingen fishing ban
facilities.description: Within Nynäs reserve, fishing is prohibited in Björken, Stora Frillingen, Lilla Frillingen, and Gisesjön. Do not launch boats or fish from floating craft in reserve lakes/watercourses. Check exact reserve boundaries and posted signs.

facilities.name: Crayfish-plague water biosecurity
facilities.description: Clean, dry, or disinfect boots, fishing gear, boats, packrafts and other wet equipment before moving between lakes. Crayfish plague can spread via water and wet gear.

facilities.description: Official 50:1 text says parking is available at Månbacken near the endpoint. This is not directly on the connector; verify signs.

facilities.name: Månbacken bus stop
facilities.description: Official access option: bus to Månbacken, then walk to the stage. It also connects to Vagnhärad by bus per official text; verify live departures.

facilities.name: Månbacken toilet
facilities.description: Mapped toilet near Månbacken/Björken context; stage 54 also notes toilet at Månbacken. Verify season/access.

facilities.name: Månbacken cottages / Nynäs lodging context
facilities.description: Stage 54 and Nynäs reserve material describe simple Månbacken cottages/lodging booked via Nynäs slott. Book ahead; not a free shelter and guests should bring drinking water.

facilities.name: Månbacken road barrier
facilities.description: Nynäs visitor material notes a road barrier blocking access toward Björken/Månbacken cottages and the shelter; walk the final section and do not drive beyond permitted access.

facilities.name: Karlfors/Månbacken access
facilities.description: Common road access for the Björken/Månbacken loop with parking/rest-hut context and bus nearby, about 1 km from Månbacken cabins. Useful for logistics, not on the 50:1 connector itself.

facilities.name: Gisekvarn pump distant water
facilities.description: Current official Stage 54 lists a pump at Gisekvarn fritidshusområde/Kvannestigen. This is far east on Stage 54, not Stage 50:1; do not rely on it for this connector unless your route continues there.

facilities.name: Brevik/Sandvik camping rule update
facilities.description: Nynäs current overnighting info says tenting is limited to designated grass areas at Brevik during renovation from 2026-03-16, max one night; otherwise use Sandviks camping where open. This is loop planning context, not on 50:1.

facilities.name: Gisesjön shelter burned-down notice
facilities.description: Nynäs current news lists a burned-down shelter at Gisesjön. This affects nearby Stage 54/Nynäs loop planning, not the 50:1 connector itself.

facilities.name: Nynäs reserve camping/fire rules
facilities.description: In Nynäs reserve, overnighting is limited to designated places and fires/grilling to managed fireplaces with provided wood. Do not damage dead or living wood; cycling is restricted to roads/gravel roads. Follow posted local rules.

sections.name: Stage 51: Bråfalls såg to Nynäs slott
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 51, Bråfalls såg to Nynäs slott.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Nynäs.
Bråfalls såg has parking, picnic/rest shelter, toilet, and bus access near the start.

Nynäs slott is the strong service end with parking, several visitor-area toilets, seasonal visitor services, STF Bränneriet lodging, gardens, and bus access along road 219; restaurant/cafe status must be checked for the current season.
There is no verified drinking-water tap or shop on the forest part of the stage; use Bråfalls/Nynäs services where open.
waterSources: No natural or public drinking-water source was verified on the core stage 51 line.
At Nynäs, use open visitor services, restaurant/hostel access, or ask staff; do not assume an all-hours outdoor tap.
Rundbosjön and small wetlands are natural water only and should be treated if used.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 4 km; Naturkartan measures 3.8 km/3,820 m, OSM relation 6567468 computes about 3.46 km despite a 4 km tag, and the local drawn route is about 3.63 km from Bråfalls såg to the Nynäs mainline/stage-52 handoff. OSM wiki coverage status is stale, but the relation itself was updated in 2026 and is continuous.

Short but hilly Nynäs-reserve stage over north-south rocky ridges, hällmark forest, road 219 crossing, pasture/field edges, and the Mummerberget viewpoint before descending to Nynäs slott. Hiker reports describe it as more rugged than the short length suggests, with repeated ups/downs, rocky footing, and one user-reported rope-supported steep descent near Nynäs.

Local Stage 50/51 and 51/52 snaps are exact. Official pins are nearby aliases: the Bråfalls official start is about 13 m from the local start and the official Stage 52/Nynäs start is about 15 m from the local Stage 51 end. Keep at least 20 m snap tolerance when reconciling sources.

For route-builder imports, use relation/full-GPX geometry rather than routable-way extraction only: OSM relation 6567468 is one connected chain, but one member way lacks highway/path tags and graph routing that ignores it may drop the final approach into Nynäs.
Cattle can occur near Nynäs ladugård from May into autumn. The official page says a fenced passage was built in 2021 to reduce contact and that passage with dogs is risk-free when using it correctly.
Mummerberget is the key rest/viewpoint. From the ridge there are views toward Rundbosjön and a historical lime kiln where osprey often nest on top; the kiln operated from the early 1900s to 1939.

A July 2023 user comment on the official page said the stage was passable but brush sometimes obscured markings at a few points and made the route challenging for children aged 11-13. User reports also mention modest markings at some crossings/ridges. Treat this as older low-confidence navigation context rather than a current fault report.
No current official Stage 51 fault report was found on 2026-04-27. Nynäs/Gisesjön and other loop notices can still affect onward Nynäs Runt planning.

Nynäs reserve rules prohibit tent/hammock/camper overnighting except at designated places and restrict fires/grilling to reserve-managed fireplaces with provided wood. Current 2026 Nynäs notice limits Brevik tenting to designated grass areas during renovation; use designated sites or booked lodging rather than wild camping.

Other user reports mention modest markings at some crossings/ridges. No current official fault was verified; carry the map and watch for orange markers.

facilities.description: A user report describes a steep descent near Nynäs with a rope for support. Treat as terrain caution for wet rock, tired legs, or dogs, not an official maintained aid guarantee.

facilities.name: Nynäs current fire-risk check
facilities.description: No fire ban was found on the Nyköping/Sörmlandskustens page during research, but Länsstyrelsen displayed a forest-fire-risk banner. Check current municipal fire-ban status and Brandrisk Ute before any fire use.

facilities.name: Nynäs reserve camping/fire rules
facilities.description: No tenting in the reserve except designated places, generally max one night; current 2026 notice limits Brevik tenting to designated grass areas during renovation. Fires/grilling only at managed fireplaces with provided wood. Use lodging/stugor at Nynäs instead of informal camping.

sections.name: Stage 52: Nynäs slott to Sandviks badplats
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 52, Nynäs slott to Sandviks badplats.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Nynäs.

Nynäs slott provides the start-side service cluster: parking, toilets, seasonal restaurant/cafe, Bränneriet lodging, gardens/visitor context, and road-219 bus access; 2026 public visitor season is 20 June-16 August, Wednesday-Sunday 11-16, but food and indoor services still need a current check.

Brevik/Nynäs brygga is the mid-stage camping/service node with summer tap, toilet, parking, fireplace, picnic/waste context, and designated tenting; current Nynäs rules limit tenting to marked grass areas because of 2026 renovation work.

Sandviks badplats and Sandviks camping are separate nearby service nodes: the stage junction/beach/tap is east by the badplats, while the paid camping/service-building area with showers, electricity, waste/recycling context, and camping rules is west of it.
waterSources: Official drinking-water taps are seasonal: Brevik after about 2.5 km at N 58°47.819 E 017°22.797 and Sandviks badplats/camping at N 58°47.708 E 017°25.089.

Do not treat Brevik or Sandvik taps as year-round. A recent official-page user comment reported water at the castle/Brevik, but that should be treated as opening-hour/visitor-service context rather than all-hours trail water.

Tvären/Baltic water and small wetlands are natural/salt-brackish water context only, not practical drinking-water refills. Sandviks badplats bathing water had 2025 samples listed as tjänligt and 2026 season classification as good, but check current bathing-water status in season.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official distance is 7.5 km; Naturkartan measures about 7.0 km/7,025 m, OSM relation 7449057 computes about 6.862 km, Äventyrligare about 6.83 km, and local official-GPX geometry is about 6.958 km. Keep 7.5 km as the planning distance and use measured length as map metadata.

Stage 52 and Stage 53 snap exactly in local geometry at Sandviks badplats, while OSM Stage 52 ends about 52 m west of the local shared point. Stage 53:1 does not share the exact Stage 52/53 endpoint; it starts about 230-245 m east along the early Stage 53/Sandvik area, so a route from Stage 52 to 53:1 should include or snap across that short connector.

Expect a more demanding Nynäs-reserve day than the short distance suggests: rocky knolls just after the castle, a road crossing, old cart road, a noticeable climb, boulder/shingle field, giant's kettle, Röstensberget viewpoint, shore sections, and road/path sections. Wet rocks, repeated climbs/descents, and high grass can slow the route.
Cattle may occur in at least one pasture. Keep dogs controlled, use gates/passages correctly, and avoid disturbing livestock.

The official page showed no current fault reports during the research pass. User reports describe a possible missed-sign point shortly after Nynäs slott, side-road/cottage-area wrong-turn risk near Sandvik, clear but attention-demanding markings, the Tvärens/Lövnösudden shelter in good condition with firewood reported by one hiker, and wider Nynäs Runt junctions as places where GPS/attention helps.

Sandviks badplats is a useful endpoint with sea bathing, parking, toilet, grill/fireplace, changing-room context, and seasonal water. HaV lists the latest 2025 sample as tjänligt with no algal bloom and the 2026 season classification as good, but check current samples during the official 2026 bathing season, especially after rain or visible algae.

sections.name: Stage 53: Sandviks badplats to Karlfors kvarn
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 53, Sandviks badplats to Karlfors kvarn.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Nynäs, Trosa kommun.

Sandviks badplats is the start-side beach/service node with summer tap, toilet, fireplaces, parking, and nearby Stage 52/53/53:1 connections; Sandviks camping is a separate paid service node west of the badplats.

Långmaren is the key mid-stage cultural and water node, with museum-farm context, an official waterpost behind/near the dwelling, and seasonal/event-based visitor services; exterior access is useful year-round but cafe/events, toilet access, and water function are current-check.
Karlfors kvarn/Månbacken is the end-side access node with rest shelter/old washhouse context, mill heritage, parking, and nearby line-554 bus platforms.

Intermediate parking is described at/near Klackavägen, Långmaren, the Långmarenvägen trail crossing, and the Klackavägen/Tofsövägen crossing. Treat these as small local access points where signs and overnight restrictions must be checked on site.
waterSources: Official water points are Sandviks badplats, the spring after about 3 km, and Långmaren. Treat Sandvik as seasonal/summer water, the spring as natural water to treat/filter, and Långmaren as current-check tap water.
No additional dependable all-hours potable source was verified between Långmaren and Karlfors.
Surface water and wetlands in Nynäs reserve are natural water only and should not be treated as practical drinking-water refills.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official and Naturkartan catalog distance is 11 km. Local drawn route is about 10.32 km, OSM relation 6571869 measures about 10.42 km while tagging 11 km, and Naturkartan API geometry measured about 10.15 km in the 2026-04-27 review. Keep official planning distance and measured map distance separate.

Topology: stage 53 starts at Sandviks badplats proper, with branch 53:1 beginning roughly 270 m east/southeast along the first Stage 53 segment. OSM Stage 52 and 53 snap together near Sandviks badplats, while Naturkartan appears to start Stage 53 closer to the 53:1 branch point. Stage 53 ends at Karlfors kvarn where stage 54 begins, and it is also part of Nynäs Runt.

Expect a hilly, rocky Nynäs-reserve stage rather than an easy road walk: forest, bedrock slabs, uneven climbs, meadows/pastures, the Källkälla spring, creeping spruce, older fire-scarred forest, Långmaren, Nyckelby grave field, road 219 crossing, and a final rocky descent to Karlfors. If walking Karlfors-to-Sandvik, that final descent becomes an immediate steep climb.

Recurring flooding around Långmaren is an official issue. Keep the normal route geometry, but follow current local/official alternate-route guidance and any temporary red reroute markings if the ordinary route is wet.

Livestock in pastures is possible, especially around Utängstugan and the Långmaren/open-land portions. Close gates, keep dogs controlled/leashed, give animals space, and avoid walking between cattle and calves.

Recent user-facing reports describe the trail as well marked/good condition, but the official text flags the left uphill turn after a few hundred metres from Sandvik as easy to miss. Older reports also mention high grass, soft muddy holes at Sandviks badplats, quiet/low-traffic trail days, and hunting-season signage near Karlfors; treat these as situational awareness, not fixed closures.
Sörmlandsleden is maintained and permitted as a hiking trail. Use roads or marked cycle routes for cycling/riding rather than wet, rocky, or pasture-sensitive footpath sections.

sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 53:1, Sandviks badplats to Källviks brygga.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Trosa kommun.

Sandviks badplats is the start-side service node with seasonal tap, toilet, fireplaces, parking, and the stage-52/53/53:1 junction; Sandviks camping is a separate paid service node west of the badplats.

Källviks brygga is an access/boat endpoint for Sävö rather than a full service node. Parking and boat access are verified, but no reliable public mainland water or confirmed current public toilet was found at the brygga itself; summer parking can fill and overflow must not block residents, road traffic, or emergency access.

Public transport is awkward: no regular Sandvik/Källvik bus stop was verified. Treat Källviks brygga as car, pickup, complementary taxi, booked boat, or out-and-back logistics unless live Sörmlandstrafiken planning says otherwise.
Sävö services are useful only after a boat transfer. Sävö has island toilets, a water tap by Sävö gård/naturskola, and seasonal hostel/cafe context, but those are not mainland Stage 53:1 services.
waterSources: No reliable potable water was verified on the mainland Stage 53:1 after the Sandviks badplats service cluster.
Use Sandviks badplats/camping water only as seasonal/current-check service water; the Sandviks tap sits about 300 m west of the official 53:1 start pin.

Källviks brygga should not be shown as a drinking-water point unless field-verified. Sävö has water at Sävö gård by the naturskola/gate area and seasonal hostel/cafe services, but only after a boat transfer and when open/booked.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden distance is 8 km; Naturkartan lists 6.9 km/6,896 m and its API geometry measured about 6.876 km, while OSM relation 8426186 measured about 6.866 km. Keep 8 km as the official planning distance and use the OSM relation geometry as the current map line.

The previous official-network GPX extraction for this app ended near Långmaren/Klacka instead of Källviks brygga. Use the OSM relation geometry for 53:1 until the official full-network GPX is corrected.

The first kilometres follow Tvären, a bay linked in official text to a meteorite impact about 450 million years ago. The route then passes Mättinge/Luckebol/Folkvik context, includes roughly 2 km of country-road walking plus a final Källvik road/service approach, and finishes through younger forest/deciduous woodland to Källviks brygga.

User reports describe the Sandvik/Tvären side as the best part, with mostly easy coastal/mixed walking, managed forest, powerline/open corridors, road walking, and a sometimes uneven, brushier, less-used final forest approach toward Källvik. No current official 53:1 fault report was found.
Mättinge/Valjeviken may offer booked lodging or transfer help near the branch, but exact map placement and current offer should be verified before relying on it.

Luckebol nature reserve is side context south of the road corridor; it is not a trail service node, current Länsstyrelsen material says there is no parking there, and its visitor information warns of many bark-beetle-felled/fallen spruces with difficult passage and wind risk.

Boat logistics are safety-critical: Sörmlandstrafiken skärgårdstrafik must be prebooked by 15:30 the day before and may depend on weather/skipper; Sävö Vandrarhem/Café runs prebooked April-October transfers from Källviks brygga, usually 10:30 and 16:00, return 11:00 and 16:30, with extra July-August weekend departures and limited capacity.

Route-builder topology: do not auto-chain Stage 53:1 into Stage 53:2 as a walking route. The mainland line stops at Källviks brygga and the nearest Sävö/53:2 point is roughly 0.55 km away over water, so any continuation must be an explicit boat/transfer edge.

facilities.description: Official start for the access branch to Källviks brygga, just east of the main Sandviks badplats service cluster. Stages 52 and 53 connect nearby in the same Sandvik start area.

facilities.description: Official route text describes the early shoreline along Tvären, a sea bay formed by a meteorite impact about 450 million years ago. Approximate context marker.

facilities.name: Mättinge-Sandvik grill/rest
facilities.description: Official stage steward tip describes a good waterside grill/rest place with benches between Mättinge and Sandviks badplats; user reports corroborate the rest/grill context. Approximate pin only.

facilities.name: Valjeviken Mättinge lodging/transfer context
facilities.description: Nearby booked lodging/transfer context by the 53:1 corridor. Exact service details and pickup/boat-transfer options should be verified directly before relying on them.

facilities.name: Mättinge / Mättingeviken route landmark
facilities.description: Route landmark around the transition from shoreline/forest toward more road and open-land walking. Approximate context marker.

facilities.name: Luckebol route landmark
facilities.description: Official stage text says the route passes Luckebol before the road-walk section. Context marker, not a public service.

facilities.name: Luckebol reserve side context
facilities.description: Side-area reserve context near the road corridor. Not a trail facility; current Länsstyrelsen information says there is no parking at Luckebol and warns that many bark-beetle-damaged spruces have fallen, making passage difficult and windy conditions risky.

facilities.name: Folkvik route landmark
facilities.description: Official stage text says the route passes Folkvik after road walking. Föreningsgården Folkvik has local-history/WC-by-arrangement context but should not be treated as a public trail toilet.

facilities.name: Källviksvägen road-walk section
facilities.description: Official text describes about 2 km of country-road walking around Luckebol/Folkvik before the route returns to easier forest. Watch traffic and road shoulders.

facilities.name: Final young-forest approach to Källvik
facilities.description: Official text describes the last kilometres as easy walking through younger forest and deciduous woodland toward Källviks brygga. User reports mention managed forest/powerline context and possible side-growth near Källvik. Approximate context marker.

facilities.name: Källviks brygga stage end
facilities.description: Stage 53:1 mainland endpoint at Källviks brygga and access point for boat logistics to Sävö. Do not draw a walking continuation across the water; Stage 53:2 is across a roughly 0.55 km boat gap.

facilities.name: Källviks brygga boat access to Sävö
facilities.description: Boat access to Sävö and stage 53:2. Prebook Sävö Vandrarhem boat, Sävö gård transport, or Sörmlandstrafiken skärgårdstrafik; do not assume a chance lift, drop-in service, or guaranteed walk-on ferry.

facilities.name: Källviks brygga parking
facilities.description: Parking near the harbour/brygga; Sävö sources describe free parking but no EV charging. Parking can fill on busy summer days; overflow parking must not block roads, residents, docks, or emergency access.

facilities.name: Källviks brygga water/toilet caveat
facilities.description: No reliable public mainland drinking-water tap was verified at Källviks brygga, and only older/uncertain toilet information was found. Treat as no dependable mainland water and field-check any toilet before relying on it.

facilities.name: Sävö prebooked boat transfer
facilities.description: Sävö Vandrarhem/Café runs April-October prebooked boat transfers from Källviks brygga: usually 10:30 and 16:00 from mainland, 11:00 and 16:30 return, with extra 12:30/13:00 weekend departures in July-August. Crossing is about 10 minutes, capacity is limited, and booking is required.

facilities.name: Sörmlandstrafiken skärgårdstrafik
facilities.description: Demand-responsive archipelago boat service can depart Källviks brygga or Studsvik brygga. Book by 15:30 the day before; Monday trips by Friday 15:30. If no booking exists, no trip runs, and weather/skipper can affect service.

facilities.name: Sävö gård drinking water
facilities.description: Across the water on Sävö, local sources describe a drinking-water tap at Sävö gård/fence. Approximate marker and only useful after boat transfer.

facilities.name: Sävö dry toilets
facilities.description: Across the water on Sävö, official/OSM sources describe multiple dry toilets around the island, including Lägerplatsen/Boholmsviken/west-side contexts. Show as onward-island services only.

facilities.name: Sävö open shelter / Lägerplatsen context
facilities.description: Across the water on Sävö, an open shelter/fireplace/toilet/tenting context exists near the Sävö loop. Show as onward-island context only, not a Stage 53:1 mainland facility.

facilities.name: Sävö Vandrarhem & Café
facilities.description: Seasonal island hostel/cafe service after boat transfer. 2026 cafe hours vary by season; verify before relying on food, water, or lodging.

facilities.name: Sävö stage 53:2 connection
facilities.description: Optional onward Sävö loop/stage 53:2 after boat transfer. Show only as an onward branch option from Källviks brygga/Sävö logistics.

facilities.name: Källvik complementary taxi area
facilities.description: Sörmlandstrafiken complementary traffic includes Källvik/Bromdal/Luckebol/Tofsö/Örboholm area, but must be booked by phone by 16:00 on the weekday before travel. Verify eligibility and timetable.

facilities.name: Studsvik bus access
facilities.description: Closest researched mapped bus stop to the Sandvik/Källvik corridor, but still distant from both ends. Treat as off-route access and verify live Sörmlandstrafiken routing.

facilities.name: Vagnhärad station train access
facilities.description: Remote rail access for taxi/bus planning, roughly 17-19 km direct-line from this branch. Show as regional access, not nearby trail transport.

facilities.name: Current fire-ban check
facilities.description: No municipal fire ban was found during one 2026-04-27 check, but Länsstyrelsen/SMHI showed forest-fire-risk context. Check same-day fire-ban status before using any prepared fireplace.

facilities.name: Nynäs/Sävö reserve camping and fire rules
facilities.description: Nynäs reserve limits camping and fires to designated/managed places. Luckebol reserve is side context with no public parking. On Sävö, dogs must be leashed, fires only at signed prepared fireplaces, tenting is limited by reserve rules, and fenced/designated tent places are recommended because grazing animals roam.

sections.name: Stage 54: Karlfors kvarn to Gisekvarn
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 54, Karlfors kvarn to Gisekvarn.
utilities: Official area: Trosa kommun.

Månbacken bus stops are the closest public transport to the Karlfors start, about 0.2-0.3 km away. Bergs Gård is the most useful mapped bus access near the Gisekvarn end, about 1 km away; Vagnhärad station is remote regional rail access.

Karlfors/Månbacken has parking and rest context near the start. Månbacken also has a toilet, fireplace/rest point, and bookable cottages, but the cottages are paid lodging rather than free trail shelter.

Björken has the main stage-54 rest-shelter/fireplace area and a nearby dry toilet, but it should not be presented as a planned overnight option because Nynäs reserve overnighting is limited to designated places and current Nynäs guidance points campers to Brevik/Sandviks camping. Gisesjön/Prins Alexanders plats has an accessible picnic/rest cluster with toilet, firepit, rest-shelter context, and waste basket, but a 2026-04-09 Nynäs notice says the Gisesjön shelter/grill place burned and is currently unusable until rebuilt.

Gisekvarn has the official pump at Kvannestigen, a lower-confidence second pump at Älgörtsstigen, parking/recycling by the stage end, and stage-55 continuation. Treat pump water as current-check because older hiker and association reports raise quality concerns.
waterSources: The Kvannestigen pump at Gisekvarn is the strongest verified refill point, but hiker reports have described cloudy water in the past and older local association notes mention failed water tests for some pumps; run it, inspect it, and filter/boil if needed.
Älgörtsstigen is a plausible second pump from community/secondary sources, but it is lower confidence than Kvannestigen and should be verified on site.
Björken and Gisesjön are natural lake water only, not potable taps. Treat/filter/boil and do not move wet gear between lakes because of the official crayfish-plague hygiene warning at Björken.
A possible Månbacken spring/source appears in secondary data, but Nynäs lodging guidance says cottage guests should bring drinking water; do not rely on Månbacken as a potable refill.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden and Naturkartan list stage 54 as 8.5 km. The local drawn geometry measures about 8.245 km, Naturkartan geometry about 8.167 km, and OSM relation 6568069 about 8.024 km despite its stale/wrong 7.5 km distance tag. Keep official distance for planning and measured geometry for map display.

Stage 50:1 joins stage 54 near Björken at the connector before the Björken shelter, and should appear as a route-builder connector only after the user selects the relevant Björken part of stage 54. Nynäs Runt uses only Karlfors-to-Björken on stage 54, then turns onto 50:1.

This Nynäs Runt section uses the old mill path from Karlfors, a steep opening climb/descent depending on direction, rocky forest and hällmark, lake/rest areas, and about 1.5 km of old Trosa road walking near Gisekvarn's summer-house area. Watch traffic on the road section and use care on wet rock, mud, dam slopes, and downhills after rain.

Nynäs reserve rules apply: overnighting in tent, hammock, or shelter is allowed only at designated places and max one consecutive night; fires/grilling only at reserve-managed fireplaces using provided wood; disposable grills are forbidden.
Björken has an official crayfish-plague hygiene warning. Avoid moving wet swimwear, fishing gear, bottles, or other wet equipment between lakes without drying/cleaning.

Fishing is prohibited in reserve parts of Björken and Gisesjön; Trosa municipality separately says there is no general fishing in Gisesjön. Check posted signs and current Nynäs reserve rules before fishing anywhere nearby.

Official Stage 54 showed no current fault report during this pass. Older hiker reports mentioned confusing markings near Gisesjön and later corrections by maintainers, plus a 2022 bark-beetle reroute; keep a map handy at Gisesjön junctions but do not treat those older reports as current closure notices.

Länsstyrelsen published a 2026-04-17 decision that planned lowering of the dam water level at Karlfors kvarn was not expected to cause significant environmental impact. Treat as start-area dam/water-work context, not a trail closure.

Nynäs notice from 2026-04-09 says the shelter/grill place burned and is currently unusable while rebuilding is planned; SVT separately reported the fire on 2026-04-06/07. Verify on site before relying on it.

facilities.description: Older/secondary maps mark a backcountry/campsite-style point nearby, but current official reserve rules allow overnighting only at designated places and the 2026 notice says the Gisesjön shelter/grill place is unusable. Do not treat this as legal camping without current signs.

facilities.name: Havrevreten lodging/glamping
facilities.description: Paid seasonal lodging/glamping/hammock-hotel option near the stage 54/55 planning area. Confirm exact location, availability, and transfer/logistics directly.

facilities.description: Official pump/water point near Gisekvarn, about 110 m off route. Past hiker reports mentioned cloudy water and older local association notes mention failed pump-water tests, so inspect, run the pump, and filter/boil if needed.

facilities.description: Second pump reported near Älgörtsstigen in secondary/community data. Lower-confidence than the official Kvannestigen pump; verify on site.

facilities.name: Gisekvarn stage end and recycling area
facilities.description: Official Stage 54 end and Stage 55 start area by Gisekvarn/recycling-station access. The mapped recycling/parking node is nearby at about 58.875093, 17.421662; exact parking rules should be checked locally.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård bus stop, west platform
facilities.description: Closest useful mapped bus access near the Gisekvarn end, roughly 1 km off route. Check Sörmlandstrafiken line 554 and weekday/seasonal patterns.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård bus stop, east platform
facilities.description: Opposite Bergs Gård bus platform for end access near Gisekvarn. Verify live departures before relying on it.

facilities.name: Vackebol bus access
facilities.description: Mapped bus access option roughly 2 km from the Gisekvarn end; mark as distant/off-route when shown for this stage.

facilities.name: Gisekvarnsvägen bus access
facilities.description: Named bus stop pair on the road corridor, but not the closest end access; treat as off-route and verify live service.

facilities.name: Vagnhärad station remote rail access
facilities.description: Remote rail access for taxi/bus planning, about 9 km direct-line from Gisekvarn and farther from Karlfors. Not a nearby trailhead station.

sections.name: Stage 55: Gisekvarn to Trosa
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 55, Gisekvarn to Trosa.
utilities: Official area: Trosa kommun.

Gisekvarn has limited start infrastructure: the official stage start, small parking at the recycling point, and the Kvannestigen pump about 0.6 km off the stage-55 line. No direct bus stop or public toilet was verified at the trailhead.

Dymossen is the only confirmed on-stage shelter/rest facility. It is suitable for rest or overnight use, but there is no water on site and the toilet is OSM/third-party mapped rather than official-stage listed. Treat any fireplace as condition-dependent because the official warning stresses fire risk and no extinguishing water.

Bergs Gård is a strong off-route service hub near the start side, with cafe/farm shop/lodging/toilets/water/parking, a mapped firepit, and weekday bus access, but it is reached via local roads/Bergsrundan rather than being directly on the stage-55 main line.

Trosa has the best end services: buses, town parking, public toilets, potable municipal water via town services/taps, food, lodging, guest harbour/RV services, long-stay/overflow parking at Trosaporten, and onward stage-56 access.
waterSources: There is no water at Dymossen shelter; carry enough through the long middle section.

Use the Gisekvarn/Kvannestigen pump before starting from Gisekvarn, but treat it as start-side/off-route water and verify current operation and quality. A hiker report found the pump water cloudy, matching older local caution around pump water quality.

Bergs Gård has service water if you make the off-route detour and it is open. Trosa has reliable municipal groundwater-based drinking water via public services/taps, and OSM maps harbour/town taps, but verify exact public access and opening hours.
Ringsjön and other lakes on the route are natural water only, not potable refill points; treat/filter/boil if used.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden and OSM list stage 55 as 16 km; OSM relation 6567861 measures about 16.10 km and snaps cleanly to stages 54/56, while Naturkartan site 13902 lists 17.0 km but measures about 16.05 km. The public official GPX is ambiguous here because it mixes/splits nearby stage 55:1 geometry, so use official 16 km as planning distance and OSM/Naturkartan for the current drawn line.

Stage 55 connects stage 54 at Gisekvarn, stage 56 at Trosa, and stage 55:1 at Hungaskogen/Trosabacken. The Hungaskogen split is about 13.5 km from Gisekvarn and 2.6 km from Trosa on OSM/Naturkartan geometry. Stage 55:1 has a spring-2026 reroute note from Vagnhärad to Hungaskogen, so do not rely on old Sillekrog-Hungaskogen geometry for access planning.

The route has about 3 km of forest and mossy rock slabs after Gisekvarn, then Dymossen, Ringsjön/Lugnet context, about 5 km of high hilly forest over Lemdalsberget, Tureholm castle avenue, road crossings/road-walk context near Tureholm-Hungaskogen, Smedstorp viewpoint/rest context, and a cycle/footway into Trosa.

User reports make the Lemdalsberget/Tureholm middle feel harder than a flat 16 km: repeated short climbs, side-slope walking, wet/horse-damaged forest-road sections, boggy early stretches, slippery descending rock/boardwalks after rain, and one weak-marking report before the northward turn toward Tureholm. Carry offline mapping and expect slower going in wet weather.

Dymossen has an official no-water warning and specific fire-risk concern because there is no water to extinguish a fire. Use any fireplace only if current fire-ban status allows and avoid fires in dry conditions. One hiker report also warned that the toilet latch/wood piece could trap a solo visitor, so check the door before closing it fully.
Sörmlandsleden shelters are shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and have no trash bins. Pack out waste and do not count on firewood.

Outside restricted/protected areas, ordinary allemansrätten applies, but do not camp near homes, farmland, public-place areas, or sensitive ground and never light fires directly on rock slabs. Trosa local order rules restrict camping on public places to Trosa Havsbad/marked motorhome places, and Trosa detailed-plan/central areas have stricter fire restrictions.

Stage 55 itself did not show a linked nature reserve in the official page research pass. Nearby reserve rules may matter around Nynäs/Noret or Tomtaklintskogen side trips; Tomtaklintskogen forbids camping and allows fire only at prepared places.
Official stage-55 notices showed no current fault report during the 2026-04-27 research pass; still verify current Sörmlandsleden notices and Krisinformation fire-ban status before hiking.

sections.name: Stage 55:1: Vagnhärad to Hungaskogen, etapp 55
sections.description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 55:1, Vagnhärad to Hungaskogen, etapp 55.
utilities: Official area: Nyköpings kommun, Trosa kommun.

Vagnhärad station is the current official start after the spring 2026 reroute and has strong train/bus access, parking, bicycle parking, EV charging, and nearby Vagnhärad town services. No current public toilet at the station itself was confirmed; the nearest mapped toilet is in Vagnhärad centrum near OKQ8/ICA.

The Hungaskogen/Stage 55 end is a trail junction rather than a transit endpoint. Continue on Stage 55 toward Trosa/Gisekvarn, backtrack to Vagnhärad, or use nearby local-road access only after live route planning.

Old Sillekrog start, Sillekrog parking, Granlund/Sillekrog bus access, and the 16-18 km Sillekrog-Hungaskogen descriptions are stale and should not be treated as current Stage 55:1 services. Naturkartan, OSM relation 8425612, AllTrails, Äventyrligare, and older PDFs/blogs may still expose the removed route.
waterSources: St Hunga spring is the only official water point on the current 55:1 connector, at the published coordinate near the Hunga end. It is an old natural cold spring; Sörmlandsleden does not test or guarantee water quality, so treat/filter and carry backup.
No verified all-hours drinking-water tap was found at Vagnhärad station. Use town services if open, but do not rely on a station refill.
Dymossen shelter on Stage 55 has no water; if continuing from the 55:1 junction onto Stage 55, fill before committing to the longer dry section.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Spring 2026 reroute: Sörmlandsleden says the Sillekrog-Vagnhärad section has been removed and the new route is Vagnhärad station to the main trail. The same official page still contains stale Sillekrog fact-box/start-coordinate metadata, and it says the updated map is pending.

The app draws a provisional Vagnhärad station-to-Hungaskogen line from current official endpoints and the best available network geometry. The provisional line uses the station/parking approach around 58.945234, 17.488223, snaps to the remaining old connector corridor near 58.944563, 17.488386, and measures about 7.24 km to Hungaskogen, close to the official 7.2 km. Do not treat old Naturkartan, OSM relation 8425612, AllTrails, Äventyrligare, or blog geometry from Sillekrog as current.

Model this as an access connector to Stage 55, not as a normal mainline continuation. Once the user selects the relevant Hungaskogen/Trosabacken part of Stage 55, show 55:1 as the Vagnhärad-station access option.

Expect road/residential walking through Vagnhärad, a wetland/Trosaån edge, forest path, gravel road, farmland/farm-road sections, and forest/rural-road sections toward Hunga. User reports repeatedly mention wet/muddy forest sections after rain, especially near Hungaskogen and parts near Vagnhärad.

No shelter, campsite, or verified fireplace was found on the current 55:1 connector. Ordinary allemansrätten may apply away from homes/farmland/restricted areas, but local signs and fire bans override it.

No official reserve entry was verified for the current connector itself, but nearby Lånestaheden/Vagnhärad Runt side areas have stricter rules, including fire only at prepared places, no damaging trees/plants/deadwood, no motor vehicles, and dogs controlled/leashed in pasture/reserve contexts.

Trosa local rules matter near the start: dogs are leashed on public places, March 1-August 20 usually means leash/control in wildlife areas, dog bans apply at named beaches in summer, and camping on public-place-type areas is restricted to Trosa Havsbad/marked motorhome places. Check current fire-ban status before any stove/fire use.

A planned Hungavägen bus stop has been described locally as delayed/expected in spring 2026. Until it appears in current journey planners, use verified Vagnhärad station/Trosalands kyrka/Utterviksvägen-style options rather than assuming transit at Hungaskogen.

Current official route is Vagnhärad-Hungaskogen, 7.2 km, with official map pending.
